# Route one: mixed support, Frobenius, and purity

## 1. The starting object is the mixed-support double—not another split of the bottom zero

Your cumulative LaTeX ledger defines, for a nonzero commutative ring \(A\),
\[
S=G(A)=A\sqcup\{\tau\},\qquad e=0_A,\qquad u=-1_A,
\]
and
\[
D_A=S\oplus S
\]
with coordinatewise addition and multiplication
\[
\boxed{
(a,b)\star(c,d)
=
(ac\oplus ubd,\ ad\oplus bc).
}
\]

The source distinguishes
\[
\mathbf0=(\tau,\tau),\qquad
X_a=(a,\tau),\qquad
Y_b=(\tau,b),\qquad
Z_{a+tb}=(a,b),
\]
where
\[
B=A[t]/(t^2+1).
\]

Thus \(X_e,Y_e,Z_{0_B}\) have different leg-support information even though their ordinary amplitudes vanish. There is still one scalar support construction \(G(A)\). The full support observation is
\[
\operatorname{Chi}:D_A\to\mathbb B[C_2],
\qquad
(a,b)\mapsto(\chi(a),\chi(b)),
\]
with
\[
\chi(\tau)=0,\qquad \chi(a)=1\quad(a\in A).
\]
Its multiplication is
\[
(p,q)(r,s)=(pr\vee qs,\ ps\vee qr).
\]
These are the definitions in the supplied TeX, including the four masks. fileciteturn66file0L2-L2

### The exact recovery map

Let
\[
p_A:G(A)\to A
\]
send \(\tau\) to \(0_A\) and preserve supported amplitudes. Define
\[
\pi:D_A\to B,
\qquad
\pi(a,b)=p_A(a)+t\,p_A(b).
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
(\operatorname{Chi},\pi):
D_A\hookrightarrow\mathbb B[C_2]\times B
}
\]
is injective.

The proof is direct. Since \(1,t\) form a free \(A\)-basis of \(B\), the amplitude determines the two ordinary coefficients. The mask determines whether a zero coefficient came from \(\tau\) or from the supported zero \(e\).

So mixed support is not being collapsed into a scalar Boolean observation. Its complete information is recoverable from the displayed pair.

## 2. The mixed double has an explicit synchronization idempotent

Define
\[
\boxed{E=Z_{1_B}=(1,e).}
\]

Using the source multiplication table,
\[
E^2=E,
\]
\[
EX_a=Z_a,\qquad
EY_b=Z_{tb},\qquad
EZ_z=Z_z,\qquad
E\mathbf0=\mathbf0.
\]

Multiplication by \(E\) therefore sends every supported input to the synchronized face while preserving its ordinary amplitude.

Its image is
\[
ED_A=\{\mathbf0\}\cup\{Z_z:z\in B\}.
\]

Give this image its actual unit \(E\). There is an isomorphism
\[
G(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}ED_A,
\qquad
\tau_B\mapsto\mathbf0,\qquad
z\mapsto Z_z.
\]

More strongly,
\[
\boxed{D_A[E^{-1}]\cong G(B).}
\]

**Proof.** For every unital semiring map \(f:D_A\to T\) making \(f(E)\) invertible, the equation \(f(E)^2=f(E)\) forces \(f(E)=1_T\). Hence
\[
f(x)=f(Ex).
\]
Thus \(f\) factors uniquely through the image of \(x\mapsto Ex\). This is exactly the localization universal property.

The factorization is
\[
\boxed{
D_A\xrightarrow{x\mapsto Ex}G(B)\xrightarrow{p_B}B,
\qquad
p_B(Ex)=\pi(x).
}
\]

This is a concrete idempotent operation on the **mixed-support object**. It neither adjoins another bottom zero nor asserts that all higher objects are the same.

It also gives a precise result to test against your proposed purity mechanism: **the idempotent synchronizes support and preserves amplitudes.** We can now calculate what additional spectral information is carried through that operation.

## 3. The construction extends to every degree, with one shared scalar support

For every \(n\ge1\), keep the same \(S=G(A)\) and define
\[
D_{A,n}=S^n.
\]

For \(0\le k<n\), set
\[
\boxed{
(a\star b)_k
=
\bigoplus_{i+j=k}a_ib_j
\ \oplus\
\bigoplus_{i+j=k+n}u\,a_ib_j.
}
\]

An empty sum is \(\tau\). The unit is
\[
(1,\tau,\ldots,\tau).
\]

For \(n=2\), this is exactly your supplied double.

The associativity proof retains the wrap factor. For three monomial indices,
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{i+j}{n}\right\rfloor
+
\left\lfloor\frac{(i+j)\bmod n+k}{n}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor\frac{i+j+k}{n}\right\rfloor.
\]
Both parenthesizations therefore acquire the same power of \(u\). Distributivity extends the calculation to all coefficients, including absent ones.

Define
\[
B_{A,n}=A[t]/(t^n+1),
\qquad
\pi_n(a)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}p_A(a_i)t^i.
\]

The support map
\[
\operatorname{Chi}_n:D_{A,n}\to\mathbb B[C_n]
\]
retains all \(2^n\) masks. The pair
\[
(\operatorname{Chi}_n,\pi_n)
\]
is injective by the same coefficient-and-mask recovery.

Now put
\[
E_n=(1,e,\ldots,e).
\]
Then
\[
E_n^2=E_n,
\qquad
\boxed{D_{A,n}[E_n^{-1}]\cong G(B_{A,n}).}
\]

For \(n\mid m\), writing \(k=m/n\), the map
\[
\iota_{n,m}:D_{A,n}\to D_{A,m}
\]
places coefficient \(a_i\) in position \(ki\) and puts \(\tau\) in the other positions. Its amplitude map is induced by
\[
t_n\mapsto t_m^k.
\]

The support idempotents obey
\[
E_m\,\iota_{n,m}(E_n)=E_m.
\]

Thus the interlevel map and synchronization commute after the stated localization. These are all-degree formulas, not an inference from the second or third example.

## 4. Frobenius can be defined on those actual mixed-support coordinates

Let \(A\) be an \(\mathbb F_q\)-algebra, with \(q\) odd and \(\gcd(n,q)=1\). Set
\[
F_S(\tau)=\tau,\qquad F_S(a)=a^q\quad(a\in A).
\]

Define
\[
\boxed{
\bigl(\Phi_q(a)\bigr)_{qi\bmod n}
=
u^{\lfloor qi/n\rfloor}F_S(a_i).
}
\]

The index map is a permutation. An absent coefficient remains absent; a supported coefficient whose \(q\)-th power vanishes remains a **supported** zero.

For the original double,
\[
\boxed{
\Phi_q(a,b)
=
\left(F_S(a),\,(-1)^{(q-1)/2}F_S(b)\right).
}
\]

The sign comes from
\[
t^q=(-1)^{(q-1)/2}t
\]
in \(A[t]/(t^2+1)\).

The coefficient Frobenius preserves the source addition by checking the supported case in characteristic \(p\) and the cases containing \(\tau\) separately. Multiplication is preserved because reducing the monomial exponent before or after applying Frobenius gives the same total wrap factor. Consequently,
\[
\boxed{
\pi_n\Phi_q=F_{B,q}\pi_n,
\qquad
F_{B,q}(z)=z^q.
}
\]

Also,
\[
\Phi_q(E_n)=E_n,
\qquad
\Phi_q(E_na)=E_n\Phi_q(a).
\]

This is the actual commutative diagram:
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
D_{A,n}&\xrightarrow{\Phi_q}&D_{A,n}\\
\downarrow\pi_n&&\downarrow\pi_n\\
B_{A,n}&\xrightarrow{z\mapsto z^q}&B_{A,n}.
\end{array}
\]

### The number-field reduction preserves mixed support

For a nonzero prime \(\mathfrak p\subset\mathcal O_K\), put
\[
k_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p,
\qquad q_{\mathfrak p}=N\mathfrak p.
\]

Coefficient reduction gives
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
D_{\mathcal O_K,n}&\longrightarrow&D_{k_{\mathfrak p},n}\\
\downarrow\pi_n&&\downarrow\pi_n\\
\mathcal O_K[t]/(t^n+1)&\longrightarrow&
k_{\mathfrak p}[t]/(t^n+1).
\end{array}
\]

A coefficient divisible by \(\mathfrak p\) becomes the supported residue zero. It does not become \(\tau\). This is where your support distinction remains visible during arithmetic reduction.

The Frobenius calculation applies at \(\mathfrak p\nmid2n\). No assertion about a complete Euler product has discarded the other primes.

### A completed purity calculation

Take
\[
Y_n=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb F_q[t]/(t^n+1)\bigr).
\]

For \(\gcd(q,2n)=1\), choose a primitive \(2n\)-th root \(\zeta\) in \(\overline{\mathbb F}_q\). The geometric points are
\[
r_j=\zeta^{2j+1},\qquad 0\le j<n.
\]

Arithmetic Frobenius acts by the exact affine permutation
\[
\boxed{
j\mapsto qj+\frac{q-1}{2}\pmod n.
}
\]

Deligne’s geometric Frobenius is its inverse. If the cycle lengths are \(d_1,\ldots,d_s\), then
\[
\boxed{
\det(1-TF\mid H^0(Y_{n,\overline{\mathbb F}_q},
\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell))
=
\prod_{j=1}^s(1-T^{d_j}).
}
\]

Every eigenvalue is a root of unity, hence has absolute value one under every complex embedding. This gives **weight-zero purity of this coefficient object**.

For \(n=2\), the determinant is
\[
(1-T)^2\quad(q\equiv1\!\!\pmod4),
\qquad
1-T^2\quad(q\equiv3\!\!\pmod4).
\]

This is a proved passage from your mixed-support coordinates to an actual Frobenius spectrum. The purity follows from the calculated Frobenius action; it is not being inferred from cardinality or from replacing a supported zero by a positive real number.

# 5. What Deligne does to pass from mixed objects to a pure spectrum

The LaTeX makes two operations especially relevant to your programme.

## 5.1 Tensor powers amplify a spectral violation into a contradiction

In §1.5, let \(\mathcal F\) be a lisse \(\iota\)-real sheaf on a smooth absolutely irreducible curve, and let \(r\) be its largest determinantal weight.

Deligne considers every even tensor power:
\[
\mathcal F^{\otimes2k}.
\]

Its local traces satisfy
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^m\mid\mathcal F^{\otimes2k})
=
\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^m\mid\mathcal F)^{2k}\ge0.
\]

That gives nonnegative coefficients in the reciprocal-determinant series. The trace formula is
\[
\prod_x
\det(1-F_xt^{\deg x}\mid\mathcal F^{\otimes2k})^{-1}
=
\frac{
\det(1-Ft\mid H_c^1(X,\mathcal F^{\otimes2k}))
}{
\det(1-Ft\mid H_c^2(X,\mathcal F^{\otimes2k}))
}.
\]

The cohomological estimate controls the denominator’s poles. Because of the coefficient positivity, a local factor cannot introduce a smaller convergence radius and then hide it through cancellation by the other local factors.

For an eigenvalue \(\alpha\) at a point of degree \(d\), the resulting inequality is
\[
|\iota\alpha|^{-2k/d}\ge q^{-kr-1}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\frac{2\log|\iota\alpha|}{d\log q}
\le r+\frac1k.
}
\]

This holds for every positive integer \(k\). A weight exceeding \(r\) by any fixed amount contradicts the inequality for sufficiently large \(k\).

Exterior powers then isolate each determinantal-weight block. The sum of its eigenvalue weights is exactly its rank times its determinantal weight. Every eigenvalue has the upper bound; equality of the sum forces equality term by term.

**That is the source’s actual rigidity-by-contradiction argument.** It uses support-sensitive cohomology, real traces, tensor powers, determinant constraints, and geometric pole bounds together. The argument is in the [English TeX §1.5](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/deligne_en_witness.html#L936), with the corresponding [French section](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/deligne_fr_seg1.html#L798).

## 5.2 The pure object is obtained through two bounds on one image

For \(\mathcal F\) pure of weight \(w\), the upper-bound theorem gives
\[
\text{weights of }H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\le w+i.
\]

For smooth \(X\) of pure dimension \(d\), duality is
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d).
}
\]

The compactly supported group on the right has weights at most
\[
-w+2d-i.
\]

Dualization reverses the sign, while the retained Tate factor \((-d)\) adds \(2d\). Thus
\[
\text{weights of }H^i(X,\mathcal F)\ge w+i.
\]

Now take the natural Frobenius-equivariant map
\[
c_i:H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\to H^i(X,\mathcal F).
\]

Its image is both a quotient of the first group and a subspace of the second. Hence
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{im}c_i
\text{ is pure of weight }w+i.
}
\]

That is the precise result in [§3.3.4–3.3.6](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/deligne_en_witness.html#L2042).

The boundary terms are retained through
\[
0\to j_!\mathcal F
\to j_*\mathcal F
\to i_*i^*j_*\mathcal F
\to0.
\]

This is why the \(j_!\)/\(j_*\) discrepancy in the historical transcription matters. Replacing one by the other changes the object whose purity is asserted.

## 5.3 The dual sign is essential

The French LaTeX defines
\[
K_X=Ra^!\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell,
\qquad
D_XK=R\mathcal Hom(K,K_X).
\]

Its purity condition is
\[
\boxed{
K\text{ has weights }\le w,
\qquad
D_XK\text{ has weights }\le-w.
}
\]

The historical English witness gives an incompatible same-weight formulation at this point. I used the [French §6.2.4](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/deligne_fr_seg3.html#L710), and retained the discrepancy in the reading record.

For proper \(f\), the relevant identities are
\[
D_YRf_*K\cong Rf_!D_XK,
\qquad
Rf_!=Rf_*.
\]

Applying the upper-weight result separately to \(K\) and \(D_XK\) supplies both bounds for the pushforward.

This identifies the role of the global geometry: **properness and duality furnish the second bound.** An infinite quotient preserving an ideal-counting zeta function does not, by its cardinality, give the displayed equality between direct-image functors.

## 5.4 Where the critical line enters

For a Frobenius eigenvalue \(\alpha\),
\[
1-q^{-s}\alpha=0
\]
implies
\[
q^{-\Re s}|\alpha|=1.
\]

Consequently,
\[
|\alpha|=q^{w/2}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Re s=\frac w2.
\]

Weight-one \(H^1\) yields the line \(\Re s=1/2\).

The eigenvalues and polynomial roots must both remain visible:
\[
\alpha\text{ has size }q^{1/2},
\qquad
T=\alpha^{-1}\text{ has size }q^{-1/2}.
\]

The English historical witness reverses those roles after §3.3.6; that sentence is not imported into the argument.

Your globalization preserves the number-field ideal series through its norm bijection. The construction above supplies actual finite-field pure coefficient objects. Deligne supplies the exact cohomological operation producing the pure global image. Those are now explicit stages rather than a single assertion that “the supported spectrum is pure.” The number-field spectral identification with that cohomological image is not established in these sources.

# Route two: the NS origin and unipotent local behavior

## 6. The source class has an exact translation action

For this route, the phrase “only at the origin” must be tested on the whole source triple, including its force.

Retain
\[
\mathcal R_\nu(u,p)
=
\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u-\nu\Delta u+\nabla p.
\]

For \(b\in\mathbb R^3\), define
\[
\mathsf T_b(u,p,f)(x,t)
=
(u(x-b,t),p(x-b,t),f(x-b,t)).
\]

Direct differentiation gives
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R_\nu(\mathsf T_bu,\mathsf T_bp)
=
\mathsf T_b\mathcal R_\nu(u,p),
}
\]
and
\[
\nabla\cdot\mathsf T_bu
=
\mathsf T_b(\nabla\cdot u).
\]

The change of variables \(y=x-b\) preserves \(L^2\) and \(L^\infty\) norms. Rest initial data, smooth compact forcing, and every derivative estimate on the residual are carried by the same map.

A growth path approaching \((0,1)\) becomes a growth path approaching \((b,1)\).

The supplied [endpoint TeX](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/ns_endpoint_derivation.html#L474) proves growth near its selected center. The equation above gives its exact transport to another center. The force is translated too; this does not claim different locations with an unchanged prescribed force.

### Several centers can coexist under the supplied compact-support conditions

Let \(K\) contain the source’s velocity and pressure supports. Choose finitely many \(b_j\) so that \(K+b_j\) are pairwise disjoint, and set
\[
u_\Sigma=\sum_j\mathsf T_{b_j}u,\qquad
p_\Sigma=\sum_j\mathsf T_{b_j}p,\qquad
f_\Sigma=\sum_j\mathsf T_{b_j}f.
\]

For \(j\ne k\),
\[
((\mathsf T_{b_j}u)\cdot\nabla)(\mathsf T_{b_k}u)=0.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R_\nu(u_\Sigma,p_\Sigma)=f_\Sigma,
\qquad
\|u_\Sigma(t)\|_2^2
=
\sum_j\|u(t)\|_2^2.
}
\]

The result retains smooth compact forcing and the bounded-energy estimate, with a terminal growth path at each translated center.

**The marked origin is part of the chosen construction. The cancellation identities do not single out one universal coordinate point.** An arithmetic distinguished support can still be part of a proposed realization, but it cannot be inferred from coordinate-origin uniqueness that the NS source does not assert.

## 7. Deligne’s unipotent calculation retains a whole ladder of boundary weights

The local-monodromy operator is typed as
\[
N:V(1)\to V.
\]

For geometric Frobenius, its underlying matrix relation is
\[
\boxed{FNF^{-1}=q^{-1}N.}
\]

The monodromy filtration satisfies
\[
NM_i\subset M_{i-2},
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
N^k:\operatorname{Gr}_k^MV
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{Gr}_{-k}^MV(-k).
}
\]

The twist is essential: it makes the map Frobenius-equivariant. The source’s local-monodromy theorem gives weight \(w+i\) on \(\operatorname{Gr}_i^MV\) for a generically pure object of weight \(w\). Nonzero boundary grades are included in the theorem. See [§1.6](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/deligne_en_witness.html#L1014) and the [French local-monodromy section](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study/source_views/deligne_fr_seg1.html#L1173).

Here is the coordinate calculation for every block length \(d+1\). On a basis \(v_0,\ldots,v_d\), set
\[
Nv_0=0,\qquad Nv_j=v_{j-1},
\]
\[
Fv_j=cq^jv_j.
\]

Then
\[
N^{d+1}=0,\qquad FNF^{-1}=q^{-1}N.
\]

The monodromy grade of \(v_j\) is \(2j-d\). If \(c\) has weight \(\gamma\), its Frobenius weight is
\[
\gamma+2j
=
(\gamma+d)+(2j-d).
\]

Thus:

\[
\boxed{
\text{relative ladder}=2j-d,
\qquad
\text{center weight}=\gamma+d.
}
\]

The block length retains the directional nilpotent structure. The scalar \(c\) retains the absolute weight information.

Already
\[
N=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
F=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&q\end{pmatrix}
\]
has
\[
\exp(N)=I+N
\]
unipotent and has weights \(0,2\). Multiplying \(F\) by \(q\) preserves \(N\), its filtration, and the relation \(FNF^{-1}=q^{-1}N\), while changing those weights to \(2,4\).

This is the precise local-monodromy comparison your second route needs to retain. **Unipotent behavior organizes the boundary grades; it does not erase them or fix their center by itself.**

The NS continuation supplies an all-order residual construction. It does not yet supply this \(F,N\) pair or a map identifying its fluid correction operator with the local-monodromy operator. The source’s smooth residual can coexist with singular velocity; Deligne’s pure generic object can coexist with mixed boundary grades. Neither construction regards that coexistence as an inconsistency.

# What this reading and calculation change

The two routes now have concrete, source-based content.

**For the first route**, your actual mixed-support object admits a proved synchronization localization and an all-degree Frobenius realization. The finite-field realization has an explicitly calculated pure coefficient spectrum. Deligne’s passage to global purity is the tensor-power pole argument together with the two bounds on
\[
\operatorname{im}(H_c^i\to H^i),
\]
or the corresponding proper-pushforward argument with duality.

**For the second route**, the full NS equation transports the marked singularity to arbitrary translated centers and permits finite disjoint-support combinations. Its residual cancellation therefore does not establish the asserted uniqueness of a universal origin. Deligne’s unipotent theory supplies a full graded boundary calculation, not a rule that every supported singularity must have zero spectral defect.

These calculations do not establish GRH. They do establish the mixed-support maps that were previously absent from my treatment and identify the actual operations in the Deligne LaTeX that carry local information into a pure spectral image.

The [package](sandbox:/mnt/data/Deligne_Mixed_Support_TeX_Study_2026-09-11.zip) contains the original extracted TeX witnesses, line-numbered source views, the new proofs, and six families of finite checks. The checks cover mixed-support multiplication, idempotent synchronization, Frobenius equivariance, finite-field determinants, arbitrary-length block formulas in the tested range, duality exponents, and an NS translation instance. The general identities have written proofs; the finite checks are not presented as a verification of Deligne, the upstream NS manuscript, or GRH.

## A1021 | node cf9ad54a-2906-4d48-9cbd-b9e9677bb362 | assistant | chain 2138

**The replacement here is to lift the arithmetic structure sheaf through your split-zero map, keeping the support information before taking its arithmetic image.** I worked this out at the finite primes, at the archimedean place, and at the added support point.

On the ordinary arithmetic site, the construction is the pullback
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}
=
\underline{H_{G(\mathbb Q)}}
\times_{\underline{H_{\mathbb Q}}}
\mathcal O.
}
\]
Here the underlines denote constant sheaves; \(H\), the maps, and the local conditions are defined below. This gives an actual replacement inside the Connes framework, rather than stopping at the observation that an ordinary ring-valued map identifies the two zeros.

[**Read the continuation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Arithmetic_Sheaf/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Arithmetic_Sheaf/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Sources and exact checks**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Arithmetic_Sheaf_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. The larger target retains the original addition as well as support

Connes–Consani explicitly move to finite-pointed-set functors and \(\Gamma\)-rings to accommodate arithmetic structures that ordinary rings cannot retain. Their construction includes an archimedean structure sheaf and an arithmetic cohomological programme. I used the **“Universal cyclic theory” section of the supplied TeX**, extracted from `Connes.zip`, for the formulas here. fileciteturn67file7L55-L70 citeturn324128academia23

For a commutative semiring \(S\) with its specified additive identity \(0_S\), and a finite pointed set \(X\), define
\[
H_S(X)=S^{X\setminus\{*\}}.
\]

For a pointed map \(f:X\to Y\), define
\[
\boxed{
[H_S(f)a]_y
=
\sum_{\substack{x\ne *\\f(x)=y}}a_x,
\qquad y\ne *,
}
\]
using \(0_S\) for the empty sum.

Multiplication is the map
\[
\mu_{X,Y}:H_S(X)\wedge H_S(Y)\to H_S(X\wedge Y),
\qquad
\mu(a,b)_{(x,y)}=a_xb_y.
\]

Partitioning the fibres of a composite proves functoriality. Distributivity proves the compatibility of multiplication with the finite-sum maps:
\[
\sum_{\substack{f(x)=u\\g(y)=v}}a_xb_y
=
\left(\sum_{f(x)=u}a_x\right)
\left(\sum_{g(y)=v}b_y\right).
\]

This construction preserves the complete semiring structure. More precisely,
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CSemiring}}(S,T)
\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Gamma\text{-ring}}(H_S,H_T).
}
\]

To recover a semiring map, evaluate a \(\Gamma\)-ring morphism at \(1_+=\{*,1\}\). Naturality with coordinate projections recovers its componentwise action; naturality with the fold \(2_+\to1_+\) recovers addition; compatibility with \(\mu\) recovers multiplication.

Now use your actual scalar object
\[
S=G(\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q\sqcup\{\tau\},
\qquad e=0_{\mathbb Q}.
\]

The fold map gives
\[
(1,-1)\longmapsto e,
\qquad
(\tau,\tau)\longmapsto\tau.
\]

The arithmetic projection
\[
p:G(\mathbb Q)\to\mathbb Q,
\qquad p(\tau)=0,\quad p(a)=a,
\]
induces
\[
H_p:H_{G(\mathbb Q)}\to H_{\mathbb Q}.
\]

Thus the original supported cancellation remains present in \(H_{G(\mathbb Q)}\); applying \(H_p\) is the explicitly identified operation that forgets it. No multiplication-only substitute has replaced your original addition.

## 2. The archimedean lift works with the exact finite-sum bound

The Connes construction uses
\[
\mathcal O_\infty(X)
=
\left\{
r\in\mathbb Q^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\sum_x|r_x|\le1
\right\}
\subset H_{\mathbb Q}(X).
\]

The bound \(1\) is the source’s unit-divisor condition. The point of its functorial formulation is that finite sums are implemented only through the specified pointed-set maps, with the entire tuple subject to that bound. The supplied framework uses this archimedean object to extend the arithmetic structure sheaf. fileciteturn67file7L59-L70

Its split-supported lift is
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\infty(X)
=
\left\{
a\in G(\mathbb Q)^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\sum_x|p(a_x)|\le1
\right\}.
}
\]

This is closed under every required operation.

For a pointed map,
\[
\sum_{y\ne *}
\left|
p\bigl([H_{G(\mathbb Q)}(f)a]_y\bigr)
\right|
\le
\sum_{x\ne *}|p(a_x)|.
\]

For multiplication,
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{(x,y)}|p(a_xb_y)|
=
\left(\sum_x|p(a_x)|\right)
\left(\sum_y|p(b_y)|\right).
}
\]

Those two calculations establish the lifted \(\Gamma\)-ring structure. Entries equal to \(\tau\) and entries equal to \(e\) have the same arithmetic magnitude, but their support remains distinct.

### The support cannot be removed by a coherent choice of representatives

The projection
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\infty(X)\to\mathcal O_\infty(X)
\]
is surjective for every finite \(X\). Nevertheless, it has **no pointed natural section**.

Suppose such a section \(s\) existed. The nonzero coefficients \(1/2\) and \(-1/2\) have unique lifts. Coordinate projections therefore force
\[
s_{2_+}(1/2,-1/2)=(1/2,-1/2).
\]

This tuple is admissible because
\[
|1/2|+|-1/2|=1.
\]

Applying the fold upstairs gives \(e\). Applying the fold downstairs gives ordinary zero, whose image under a pointed section must be \(\tau\). Naturality would therefore require
\[
e=\tau,
\]
contrary to the source carrier.

**The available construction is the pullback retaining all lifts, not a choice of one lift per amplitude.** Its failure to admit that natural section is information about the extension itself. It is not a reason to discard the extension.

This is a concrete place where your supported zero affects the arithmetic geometry even though the arithmetic projection is unchanged.

## 3. The finite primes, infinity, and the added support prime now fit into one sheaf

Let \(Y\) be the topological Arakelov compactification used here: its points are the ordinary generic point \(\eta\), the finite primes, and \(\infty\). A nonempty open contains \(\eta\) and all but finitely many closed points.

For a nonempty open \(U\), set
\[
A_U=
\left\{
r\in\mathbb Q:
r\in\mathbb Z_{(p)}
\text{ for every finite }p\in U
\right\}.
\]

Define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}(U)(X)
=
\left\{
a\in G(A_U)^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\infty\in U
\Longrightarrow
\sum_x|p(a_x)|\le1
\right\}.
}
\]

Restriction removes conditions; it does not alter the retained tuple.

This is a sheaf. Compatible tuples on nonempty covering opens agree on their intersections, which contain \(\eta\). They therefore determine one rational tuple. Every finite-prime condition is imposed on a covering member containing that prime; the archimedean condition is imposed on a member containing \(\infty\). The common tuple satisfies all of them.

Its stalks are
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\eta=H_{G(\mathbb Q)},
\qquad
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_p=H_{G(\mathbb Z_{(p)})},
\qquad
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\infty
\text{ as above}.
\]

### Retaining your added prime

The preceding sheaf does not replace the additional prime by \(\infty\). Introduce
\[
\sigma=P_\tau=\{\tau\},
\qquad
Y^+=Y\sqcup\{\sigma\}.
\]

Its nonempty opens are
\[
\{\sigma\}\cup U,
\]
where \(U\) is open in \(Y\), including \(U=\varnothing\).

Define
\[
\mathcal L(\{\sigma\}\cup U)
=
\widetilde{\mathcal O}(U)
\quad(U\ne\varnothing),
\]
and
\[
\boxed{\mathcal L(\{\sigma\})=H_{\mathbb B}.}
\]

Restriction to \(\{\sigma\}\) is the support map \(H_\chi\). The preceding gluing argument and the naturality of \(\chi\) prove the sheaf condition.

On the finite arithmetic part, this recovers the topology and localization charts of your globalization:
\[
D(e)=\{P_\tau\},
\]
\[
D(n)=\{P_\tau\}\cup D_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}(n)
\quad(n\ne0),
\]
with sections \(H_{G(\mathbb Z[1/n])}\) on the latter charts.

The source arithmetic space is recovered by the closed inclusion
\[
i:Y\hookrightarrow Y^+
\]
and the sheaf morphism
\[
\boxed{
i^{-1}\mathcal L
=
\widetilde{\mathcal O}
\xrightarrow{p}
\mathcal O.
}
\]

The absolute coefficient map is
\[
\mathbb S\to\mathcal L,
\]
where \(\mathbb S(X)=X\), and a nonbasepoint \(x\) maps to the divisor with coefficient \(1\) at \(x\) and \(\tau\) elsewhere. Restriction supplies the compatible map \(\mathbb S\to H_{\mathbb B}\) at the support prime. This uses the actual absolute-base framework in Connes–Consani rather than presuming a Boolean-semiring inclusion into a ring. fileciteturn67file7L59-L66

The global sections have the explicit formula
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal L(Y^+)(X)
=
\left\{
a\in G(\mathbb Z)^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\sum_x|p(a_x)|\le1
\right\}.
}
\]

Their arithmetic image is the signed coefficient object: at most one nonzero coefficient, equal to \(+1\) or \(-1\). The lift retains the choice \(\tau\) or \(e\) at every zero-amplitude position.

So the construction now includes **the added support prime, ordinary arithmetic primes, and the archimedean bound simultaneously**, with the arithmetic recovery map proved.

## 4. Your mixed-support double enters by the same operation

Retain
\[
D_A=G(A)^2,
\]
with the source multiplication
\[
(a,b)\star(c,d)
=
(ac\oplus(-1_A)bd,\ ad\oplus bc),
\]
and
\[
\pi:D_A\to B=A[t]/(t^2+1),
\qquad
\pi(a,b)=p_A(a)+t\,p_A(b).
\]

The \(\Gamma\)-ring map
\[
H_\pi:H_{D_A}\to H_B
\]
retains those operations.

For every finite pointed \(X\),
\[
\boxed{
H_\pi(X)^{-1}(0)
=
\{\tau,e\}^{\,2|X\setminus\{*\}|}.
}
\]

Its internal mask multiplication is
\[
(p,q)(r,s)
=
(pr\vee qs,\ ps\vee qr).
\]

Thus the whole ordinary-zero fibre retains the four faces of \(\mathbb B[C_2]\), not only a single scalar presence bit. The internal unit of that fibre corresponds to \((e,\tau)\); its inclusion into \(D_A\) is not asserted to send that element to \(X_1\).

For an arithmetic coefficient sheaf \(\mathcal O_B\subset\underline{H_B}\), define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_{D_A}
=
\underline{H_{D_A}}
\times_{\underline{H_B}}
\mathcal O_B.
}
\]

For \(A=\mathbb Q\), \(B=\mathbb Q(i)\), the archimedean condition becomes exactly
\[
\sum_x|p_A(a_x)+i\,p_A(b_x)|\le1.
\]

At a finite prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\subset\mathbb Z[i]\), it is
\[
p_A(a_x)+i\,p_A(b_x)
\in\mathbb Z[i]_{(\mathfrak p)}
\quad\text{for every }x.
\]

Both are inverse images under the same \(\pi\). This retains the mixed support while applying the arithmetic conditions to the original amplitudes.

## 5. The homological replacement is to retain supported cancellations

There is another concrete place to apply your rule.

An arithmetic comparison map has the form
\[
\delta(r,b)=\iota(r)-b,
\]
where
\[
\iota:\mathbb Q\to\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}
\]
is the diagonal embedding and \(b\) satisfies the prescribed local bounds.

Its split-supported lift is the natural map of pointed functors
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde\delta(a,b)
=
G(\iota)(a)\oplus(-1_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}})b.
}
\]
The sign is retained. This is an additive comparison map, not a claimed multiplicative map.

Taking its strict fibre over external absence would discard a cancellation between supported inputs: their sum remains supported even when its amplitude vanishes.

The replacement already supplied by your framework is the **full supported-null fibre**
\[
\mathcal N
=
H_{G(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})}
\times_{H_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}}}
\{0\}.
\]

Define the supported-cycle object by
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde Z^0
=
\operatorname{Dom}(\widetilde\delta)
\times_{H_{G(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})}}
\mathcal N.
}
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\widetilde Z^0
\cong
\operatorname{Dom}(\widetilde\delta)
\times_{H_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}}}
\{0\}.
\]

This retains the ordinary arithmetic cancellation **and** all the support choices of its inputs. It is a defined object with explicit maps, not an instruction to ignore the distinction between \(\tau\) and a supported zero.

The supplied Connes programme already provides the reason to pursue cohomology in this richer setting: its arithmetic Riemann–Roch construction uses \(\Gamma\)-structures and separately defined cohomologies and duality, rather than ordinary ring reflection alone. citeturn324128academia26

**This continuation establishes the sheaf lift, its gluing, its non-splitting at infinity, and the support-retaining cycle object.** It keeps the original ideal-norm definition of the Dedekind function; it does not silently replace that function by a new section-counting series.

The substantive change is that the purity investigation now has a global arithmetic object carrying the mixed support through the comparison map. The next cohomological calculation can be performed on that object, rather than first erasing the datum and then treating its absence as evidence against the programme.

## A1070 | node 86b375dc-bd7b-494b-b050-0d8680eadae0 | assistant | chain 2308

**The new construction is a filtered arithmetic family that retains your mixed-support fibre, together with a module measuring exactly what changes when the comparison map is taken to its special fibre.** Its size can be calculated. That gives the Weil II comparison something concrete to act on, rather than treating “purity” as a consequence of adding a point.

The Chen–Moriwaki book supplies a particularly useful starting operation: it carries an adelic vector bundle, with data at all its places, to a normed vector space over **one trivially valued place**, retaining its Harder–Narasimhan filtration. I have combined that operation with your support pullback, extended it through all section degrees, and calculated the resulting comparison-image defect.

[**Read the continuation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Sources, proofs, and checks**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. Carry the global arithmetic data to one place without collapsing the fibre

The book’s input is a proper adelic curve
\[
\mathscr A=
\bigl(K,(\Omega,\mathcal A,\nu),(|\cdot|_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\bigr),
\]
with
\[
\int_\Omega\log|a|_\omega\,d\nu(\omega)=0
\qquad(a\in K^\times).
\]
The measure and every absolute value are part of the datum. fileciteturn70file0L245-L280

Retain your one scalar support:
\[
S_K=G(K)=K\sqcup\{\tau\},
\qquad e=0_K\in S_K,
\qquad 0_{S_K}=\tau.
\]

The two observations are
\[
p:S_K\to K,
\qquad p(\tau)=0_K,\quad p(a)=a,
\]
and
\[
b:S_K\to\mathbb B,
\qquad b(\tau)=0_{\mathbb B},\quad b(a)=1_{\mathbb B}\quad(a\in K).
\]

At each place, the pair
\[
a\longmapsto\bigl(|p(a)|_\omega,b(a)\bigr)
\]
sends
\[
\tau\mapsto(0,0),\qquad
e\mapsto(0,1).
\]

This retains presence separately from measured amplitude.

Now take an actual adelic vector bundle
\[
\overline E=(E,(\|\cdot\|_\omega)_\omega).
\]
Its degree is
\[
\widehat{\deg}\overline E
=
-\int_\Omega
\log\|s_1\wedge\cdots\wedge s_r\|_{\omega,\det}\,d\nu,
\]
using the source determinant norms.

Chen–Moriwaki define
\[
\mathcal F^aE
=
\sum_{\substack{0\ne V\subset E\\
\widehat\mu_{\min}(\overline V)\ge a}}V
\]
and associate the norm
\[
\boxed{
\|v\|_{\mathrm{HN}}
=
\exp\!\left(-\sup\{a:v\in\mathcal F^aE\}\right)
}
\]
over the trivial absolute value on \(K\).

**The resulting one-place object retains the entire filtration, not merely the dimension or total degree.** For a Hermitian adelic bundle, its degree is recovered exactly. In the general case the source retains
\[
\boxed{
0\le
\widehat{\deg}\overline E
-\widehat{\deg}(E,\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{HN}})
\le
\frac12\nu(\Omega_\infty)r\log r.
}
\]
fileciteturn77file0L57-L119 fileciteturn77file1L188-L222

### The support-retaining lift

Let
\[
p_M:M\twoheadrightarrow E
\]
be the actual supported coefficient object and its amplitude map. In particular, \(M\) may have a mixed-support zero fibre with several retained faces.

Define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\,a}M
=
p_M^{-1}(\mathcal F^aE).
}
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\bigcap_{a\in\mathbb R}\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\,a}M
=
p_M^{-1}(0_E).
}
\]

Thus the whole supported-null fibre survives every filtration level. There is no selection of a representative that would replace supported cancellation by \(\tau\).

The associated graded observation is explicitly
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\,a}M
\xrightarrow{p_M}
\mathcal F^aE
\longrightarrow
\mathcal F^aE/\mathcal F^{>a}E.
\]

Its complete zero fibre is
\[
p_M^{-1}(\mathcal F^{>a}E).
\]

This is the first map needed for your proposal: **the global adelic data acquire a one-place filtration while their support preimages remain attached.**

## 2. Make that construction compatible with every degree

For a projective \(K\)-scheme \(X\) and line bundle \(L\), put
\[
E_n=H^0(X,L^{\otimes n}),\qquad n\ge1,
\]
with the source supremum-norm families, and retain the graded algebra
\[
K\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}E_n.
\]

The direct HN construction comes with a precise multiplication error. Under Proposition 4.1.3’s hypotheses, write
\[
r_n=\dim_KE_n
\]
for nonzero components and
\[
f(n)=
\frac32\nu(\Omega_\infty)\log r_n
+\int_\Omega b_n(\omega)\,d\nu.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal F^{a_1}E_{n_1}\cdots
\mathcal F^{a_j}E_{n_j}
\subset
\mathcal F^{a_1+\cdots+a_j-f(n_1)-\cdots-f(n_j)}
E_{n_1+\cdots+n_j}.
}
\]
The functions \(b_n\) measure the original norm family’s stated submultiplicativity error. fileciteturn77file1L223-L286

Rather than drop those terms, the book supplies the replacement in Proposition 3.2.2. For its bounded integral graded algebra, with \(f(n)/n\to0\), define
\[
\boxed{
\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}
=
\lim_{k\to\infty}
\|s^k\|_{\mathrm{HN},nk}^{1/k}.
}
\]

The source proves that these are ultrametric norms and that
\[
\|ss'\|_{\mathrm{sp},n+m}
\le
\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}\|s'\|_{\mathrm{sp},m},
\]
while retaining
\[
\boxed{
\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}
\le e^{f(n)}\|s\|_{\mathrm{HN},n}.
}
\]
fileciteturn88file0L13-L49

Keep both norms and that comparison. Define
\[
F^aE_n=\{s:\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}\le e^{-a}\},
\qquad
\widetilde F^aM_n=p_n^{-1}(F^aE_n).
\]

For a compatible supported graded algebra \(M_\bullet\to E_\bullet\),
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde F^aM_n\cdot\widetilde F^bM_m
\subset
\widetilde F^{a+b}M_{n+m}.
}
\]

A product with zero amplitude remains in its full supported-null fibre. The result is now a genuinely multiplicative filtered algebra in **all section degrees**, over the one scalar support \(G(K)\).

## 3. Build the family whose special fibre retains the weights

The next construction packages the entire filtration geometrically.

Let \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R\) be the additive subgroup generated by the actual filtration jumps. It may be dense; no rounding of those jumps is used. Set
\[
B_\Gamma=K[T^r:r\in\Gamma,\ r\ge0].
\]

Define
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R(E_\bullet)
=
\bigoplus_{n\ge0}
\sum_{a\in\Gamma}F^aE_n\,T^{-a}
\subset E_\bullet\otimes_KK[\Gamma].
}
\]

All sums here are finite formal sums. Multiplicativity from the preceding section makes this a \(B_\Gamma\)-algebra.

There are two explicit maps to \(K\):
\[
\epsilon_1(T^r)=1,
\]
and
\[
\epsilon_0(T^0)=1,\qquad
\epsilon_0(T^r)=0\quad(r>0).
\]

To calculate their fibres, choose an adapted basis \(v_{n,j}\) and retain its weights \(\lambda_{n,j}\). Then
\[
\mathcal R(E_n)
=
\bigoplus_j
B_\Gamma T^{-\lambda_{n,j}}v_{n,j}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R(E_n)\otimes_{\epsilon_1}K\cong E_n,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R(E_n)\otimes_{\epsilon_0}K
\cong
\bigoplus_aF^aE_n/F^{>a}E_n.
}
\]

The first fibre recovers the original space. The second retains its graded weights. The adapted basis proves the formulas; the resulting graded-space identification is canonical.

### Keep mixed support before either fibre is observed

Write \(M_\bullet[\Gamma]\) for finite formal coefficient sums in which a coefficient equal to \(e\) remains present, while a coefficient equal to \(\tau\) is absent.

Define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal R}(M_\bullet)
=
M_\bullet[\Gamma]
\times_{E_\bullet[\Gamma]}
\mathcal R(E_\bullet).
}
\]

The two observations are
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal R}(M_\bullet)
\longrightarrow\mathcal R(E_\bullet)
\longrightarrow E_\bullet
\]
and
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal R}(M_\bullet)
\longrightarrow\mathcal R(E_\bullet)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_FE_\bullet.
\]

**The same supported object sits above both observations.** The parameter specialization, the amplitude zero, and external absence are located in the displayed maps; none is substituted for another.

For dense \(\Gamma\), the coefficient algebra need not be Noetherian. The finite-free calculation for each section degree remains valid and is the statement used here.

## 4. The comparison map has a calculable special-fibre defect

This is the main addition to the earlier Weil II comparison.

Let
\[
c:(V,F)\to(W,G)
\]
be a filtration-preserving linear map between finite-dimensional spaces. Put
\[
I=\operatorname{im}c.
\]

There are two filtrations on this same image:
\[
F_{\mathrm q}^aI=c(F^aV),
\]
from the source quotient, and
\[
F_{\mathrm s}^aI=I\cap G^aW,
\]
from the target subspace.

Their identity map satisfies
\[
F_{\mathrm q}^aI\subseteq F_{\mathrm s}^aI.
\]

For integer jumps, define
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_c
=
\mathcal R_{F_{\mathrm s}}(I)/
\mathcal R_{F_{\mathrm q}}(I).
}
\]

Both Rees modules are finite free over \(K[T]\). After inverting \(T\), both become
\[
I\otimes_KK[T,T^{-1}].
\]

Hence \(\mathcal D_c\) is a finite \(T\)-power-torsion module, supported at the parameter origin.

It satisfies
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_c=0
\iff
c(F^aV)=\operatorname{im}c\cap G^aW
\quad\text{for every }a.
}
\]

The condition on the right is strictness of the filtered map.

If the two image filtrations have weights \(\lambda_j\) and \(\mu_j\), counted with multiplicity, then
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{length}_{K[T]}\mathcal D_c
=
\sum_j\mu_j-\sum_j\lambda_j.
}
\]

### Proof of the length formula

The two determinant lattices differ by
\[
T^{\sum_j\mu_j-\sum_j\lambda_j}.
\]

The inclusion has Smith factors \(T^{a_1},\ldots,T^{a_r}\), with \(a_j\ge0\). Its cokernel is
\[
\bigoplus_jK[T]/(T^{a_j}),
\]
whose length is \(\sum_ja_j\). The determinant gives
\[
\sum_ja_j=\sum_j\mu_j-\sum_j\lambda_j.
\]

This calculation does not require assuming that both filtrations have a common adapted basis.

### The information at the special fibre is retained by an exact sequence

Tensor the defining Rees sequence with \(K=K[T]/(T)\):
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tor}_1^{K[T]}(\mathcal D_c,K)
&\longrightarrow
\operatorname{gr}_{F_{\mathrm q}}I
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{gr}_{F_{\mathrm s}}I\\
&\longrightarrow
\mathcal D_c/T\mathcal D_c
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

This identifies where a comparison that is an isomorphism away from the special fibre can lose information at that fibre.

For the identity map on a one-dimensional vector space, with source weight \(0\) and target weight \(2\), the Rees map is multiplication by \(T^2\). Thus
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_c\cong K[T]/(T^2).}
\]

At \(T=1\), the map is the identity. At \(T=0\), it vanishes. Its support is one point; its length is two. The displayed \(\operatorname{Tor}\) sequence retains the special-fibre kernel and cokernel.

**This measures higher information at one support without manufacturing additional bottom support scalars.**

For real jumps, the corresponding quotient over \(B_\Gamma\) is still defined and vanishes exactly for strictness. The continuation does not assign it an ordinary finite module length over a possibly non-Noetherian coefficient algebra.

## 5. This is the point where the Weil II mechanism enters

For a finite-dimensional Frobenius representation, choose a coefficient field containing the eigenvalues and the stated complex embedding. Decompose into generalized eigenspaces:
\[
V=\bigoplus_\alpha V_\alpha.
\]

The spectral weight attached to \(V_\alpha\) is
\[
w_\alpha=
\frac{2\log|\iota(\alpha)|}{\log q}.
\]

Grouping the \(V_\alpha\) by these values defines the spectral-weight filtration.

If
\[
cF_V=F_Wc,
\]
then
\[
c(V_\alpha)\subseteq W_\alpha.
\]

The direct-sum decomposition proves
\[
c(F^aV)=\operatorname{im}c\cap F^aW.
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_c=0}
\]
for that filtration, including non-diagonalizable Frobenius.

In the retained Weil II argument, the comparison is
\[
c_i:H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\to H^i(X,\mathcal F).
\]

The source’s upper bound and the duality-derived lower bound are
\[
\operatorname{weights}H_c^i\le w+i,
\qquad
\operatorname{weights}H^i\ge w+i.
\]

The same strict image must consequently have weight exactly \(w+i\). The duality map retains
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d).
}
\]

The [retained Weil II TeX excerpt](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights/sources/excerpt_deligne_en_witness.tex) contains this image argument; the [French purity excerpt](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights/sources/excerpt_deligne_fr_seg3.tex) retains the opposite dual-weight bound. Their historical-transcription status is documented.

For the adelic construction, the corresponding map control is the book’s height estimate:
\[
f(\mathcal F^aE)
\subseteq
\mathcal F^{a-h(f)}F,
\qquad
h(f)=\int_\Omega\log\|f\|_\omega\,d\nu.
\]

The height is not set to zero. The estimate follows by applying the source’s quotient-slope inequality to each subbundle and its image. fileciteturn77file0L41-L54

The module \(\mathcal D_c\) therefore gives an explicit object for studying the additional information required when the arithmetic comparison initially has only filtered-map control. It replaces the unproved assertion that every such comparison is automatically strict.

## 6. Retain the full weight distribution, not only the Hilbert–Samuel coefficient

The book’s one-place formulas give, for weights \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\),
\[
\widehat{\deg}V=\sum_j\lambda_j,
\qquad
\widehat{\deg}^{+}V=\sum_j\max(\lambda_j,0).
\]
fileciteturn88file1L196-L237

To recover every weight, take the actual metrized line \(\mathbf1(-c)\) with
\[
\|1\|_{\mathbf1(-c)}=e^c.
\]

Tensoring with this line multiplies the original norm by \(e^c\). Define
\[
C_V(c)
=
\widehat{\deg}^{+}(V\otimes\mathbf1(-c))
=
\sum_j\max(\lambda_j-c,0).
\]

Then, as a distribution in \(c\),
\[
\boxed{C_V''=\sum_j\delta_{\lambda_j}.}
\]

The entire slope distribution is recoverable from this function.

Adding the dual gives
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
B_V(c)
&=
\widehat{\deg}^{+}(V\otimes\mathbf1(-c))
+
\widehat{\deg}^{+}(V^\vee\otimes\mathbf1(c))\\
&=\sum_j|\lambda_j-c|.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

It vanishes exactly when every slope equals the specified \(c\). Opposite deviations cannot cancel in this expression.

There is also an observable that does not require selecting \(c\). Give \(\operatorname{End}_K(V)\) its operator norm. In an adapted basis,
\[
\|E_{ij}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=
e^{\lambda_j-\lambda_i}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\widehat{\deg}^{+}\operatorname{End}_K(V)
=
\sum_{i<j}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|.
}
\]

This vanishes exactly for a one-step filtration. It measures the spread remaining in the retained fibre.

### An all-degree calculation

Over the trivially valued field \(K\), take
\[
E_n=H^0(\mathbb P^1_K,\mathcal O(n))=K[X,Y]_n,
\]
and retain arbitrary real parameters \(\alpha,\beta\).

The weighted Gauss norm is
\[
\left\|
\sum_{j=0}^na_jX^{n-j}Y^j
\right\|_n
=
\max_{a_j\ne0}
e^{-((n-j)\alpha+j\beta)}.
\]

This is the supremum norm of the corresponding semipositive Fubini–Study quotient metric. Evaluation at the Berkovich Gauss point
\[
|Y/X|=e^{\alpha-\beta}
\]
attains the coefficient bound. Multiplicativity follows because the initial product in the associated graded polynomial algebra is nonzero.

The complete weights are
\[
\lambda_{n,j}=(n-j)\alpha+j\beta.
\]

Consequently,
\[
\widehat{\deg}E_n
=
\frac{n(n+1)}2(\alpha+\beta),
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\widehat{\deg}^{+}\operatorname{End}(E_n)
=
|\alpha-\beta|
\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}6.
}
\]

The second identity is obtained by summing
\[
(j-i)|\alpha-\beta|
\qquad(0\le i<j\le n).
\]

Meanwhile, the Hilbert–Samuel coefficient is
\[
\boxed{
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\widehat{\deg}E_n}{n^2/2}
=
\alpha+\beta
=
(\overline{\mathcal O(1)}^{\,2})_{\mathscr A_0},
}
\]
where the last equality is the book’s theorem applied to this stated metric. fileciteturn87file2L101-L105 fileciteturn80file0L133-L140

The parameter pairs \((2,0)\) and \((1,1)\) therefore have the same Hilbert–Samuel coefficient, while the full profile and endomorphism degree distinguish them.

The appropriate replacement for a mean-only invariant is now explicit: **retain \(C_{E_n}\), its recovered distribution, and the comparison defect \(\mathcal D_c\)**.

Taking
\[
M_\bullet=G(K)[X,Y]
\]
with supported zero coefficients retained gives a concrete all-degree support algebra for the entire example.

## 7. The global theorem and the resulting research object

Chen–Moriwaki’s arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel theorem applies to an integral projective \(K\)-scheme \(X\), an ample line bundle \(L\), and its semipositive adelic metric family, with \(K\) perfect or \(X\) geometrically integral. It proves
\[
\boxed{
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\widehat{\deg}H^0(X,L^{\otimes n})}
{n^{d+1}/(d+1)!}
=
(\overline L^{\,d+1}).
}
\]
fileciteturn80file0L133-L140

The casting step retains the quantitative comparison
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
((L,\varphi)^{d+1})
\ge{}&
((L,\varphi_0)^{d+1})\\
&-\nu(\Omega_\infty)
\bigl((d+1)\delta\log r+\log(\delta!)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
}
\]
where \(r\) is the embedding-space dimension and \(\delta=(L^d)\). The proof uses the resultant line with its actual symmetric and tensor norms. fileciteturn80file0L18-L60

For the ample section algebra, the HN degree error is \(O(n^d\log n)\). Its contribution vanishes against the displayed \(n^{d+1}/(d+1)!\) scale. That explains the global asymptotic equality while leaving finite-degree filtration information available.

The continuation now has the following connected construction:
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{adelic section spaces with all place norms}\\
&\quad\longrightarrow
\text{one-place filtered spaces}\\
&\quad\longleftarrow
\text{their full mixed-support preimages}\\
&\quad\longrightarrow
\text{a supported multiplicative Rees family}\\
&\quad\longrightarrow
\begin{cases}
\text{original arithmetic amplitudes},\\
\text{graded fibre and comparison defect},\\
\text{complete slope profiles}.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
}
\]

**The advance is the special-fibre comparison module and its exact length formula, together with an all-degree supported realization on which the global adelic estimates apply.** It gives a concrete way to retain and measure what would otherwise disappear when passing to the image used in a Weil II-style argument.

I have not identified the resulting arithmetic comparison with the complete number-field Weil trace. That remaining identification is stated once, with the constructed source and target available—not used as a reason to abandon the construction.

The package contains **79 passing finite exact check groups**, the general proofs, the actual source-reading ranges, and the TeX witnesses. The checks also passed under `python -O`; no claim of a full SGA or Deligne audit is made. The two latest uploads are versions of the same Chen–Moriwaki volume, and the reading record distinguishes them.

The next calculation is consequently no longer “does adding support make everything pure?” It is the concrete calculation of the comparison image, its retained special-fibre module, and its full weight distribution in the arithmetic realization above.

The main advance is an explicit connection between the **retained special-fibre defect** from the previous calculation and the **completed arithmetic trace** already present in your workbench.

## 1. The defect has an exact amplification law

Continue with the two Rees lattices of the same filtered comparison image,
\[
L_Q\subseteq L_P,
\qquad
D_c=L_P/L_Q,
\]
where \(L_Q\) carries the filtration induced from the source and \(L_P\) the filtration inherited from the target. The integer-jump case makes \(D_c\) a finite module supported at \(T=0\). Its length measures the failure of those two filtrations to agree.

For rank \(r\) and every \(m\ge1\), I derived
\[
\boxed{
\ell D_{\operatorname{Sym}^m}
=
\binom{m+r-1}{r}\,\ell D_c.
}
\]

Since
\[
r_m=\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Sym}^m I)
=\binom{m+r-1}{r-1},
\]
this gives
\[
\boxed{
\frac{\ell D_{\operatorname{Sym}^m}}{r_m}
=
\frac{m}{r}\,\ell D_c.
}
\]

**Any nonzero defect therefore grows exactly linearly per rank under symmetric powers.**

The proof retains the full elementary-divisor data. If the original inclusion has exponents \(a_1,\ldots,a_r\), then its symmetric-power inclusion has one exponent
\[
\alpha_1a_1+\cdots+\alpha_ra_r
\]
for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^r\) with \(\sum_i\alpha_i=m\). Summing these gives the formula.

This produces a definite contradiction mechanism: a bound on the **same comparison family**
\[
\ell D_{\operatorname{Sym}^m}\le r_m b_m,
\qquad
\frac{b_m}{m}\longrightarrow0,
\]
forces \(\ell D_c=0\).

The note also proves the tensor- and exterior-power formulas, the composition exact sequence, and the duality pairing. The Chen–Moriwaki logarithmic-rank estimates remain attached to their original maps; I have not silently assigned them to this comparison. Their casting construction supplies the relevant kind of quantitative estimate, while the calculation here determines exactly what such an estimate would force on the defect. fileciteturn90file0L320-L337

## 2. An unchanged determinant can retain a nonzero graded trace

Let \(F\) preserve both filtrations. Define
\[
A_Q(z,F^n)
=
\sum_d z^d
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(F^n\mid(L_Q/TL_Q)_d\right),
\]
and similarly \(A_P\). Let
\[
\Theta_D(z,F^n)
=
\sum_d z^d\operatorname{Tr}(F^n\mid(D_c)_d).
\]

The exact identity is
\[
\boxed{
A_P(z,F^n)-A_Q(z,F^n)
=
(1-z)\Theta_D(z,F^n).
}
\]

At \(z=1\), the difference vanishes. But its first derivative gives
\[
\boxed{
-\left.z\partial_z(A_P-A_Q)\right|_{z=1}
=
\operatorname{Tr}(F^n\mid D_c).
}
\]

So the ordinary trace can remain unchanged while the retained grading records precisely what it has forgotten. This follows from the exact sequence of Rees modules and applies to nonsemisimple \(F\) as well. The proof and determinant version are in §5 of the committed note. fileciteturn115file0L2-L5

For the graded determinant
\[
\mathcal B_c(u,z)
=
\frac{\prod_d\det(1-u z^dF\mid(L_Q/TL_Q)_d)}
{\prod_d\det(1-u z^dF\mid(L_P/TL_P)_d)},
\]
the corresponding result is
\[
\mathcal B_c(u,1)=1,
\]
but
\[
\boxed{
\left.z\partial_z\log\mathcal B_c(u,z)\right|_{z=1}
=
-u\partial_u\log\det(1-uF\mid D_c)^{-1}.
}
\]

This is a concrete way to preserve the lower-level arithmetic observation **without discarding higher information over its fibre**.

## 3. That derivative now maps into the actual arithmetic formula

For the explicitly constructed uniform comparison
\[
L_Q=k[T]\otimes V,
\qquad
L_P=T^{-a}k[T]\otimes V,
\qquad a\in\mathbb Z_{>0},
\]
insert the prime norm through
\[
(u,z)=\bigl((N\mathfrak p)^{-s},(N\mathfrak p)^{-\varepsilon}\bigr).
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal B_{a,F}
=
\frac{L_{\mathfrak p}(s-a\varepsilon,F)}
{L_{\mathfrak p}(s,F)},
}
\]
and
\[
\left.\partial_\varepsilon\log\mathcal B_{a,F}\right|_0
=
a\log N\mathfrak p
\sum_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(F^n)(N\mathfrak p)^{-ns}.
\]

At ramified primes, the construction uses Frobenius on \(V^{I_{\mathfrak p}}\), exactly as in the intrinsic Artin factor. The ramified contribution is retained rather than omitted. fileciteturn90file2L619-L630

After including the discriminant and both archimedean factors, the constructed family is
\[
\mathscr B_{K,a}(s,\varepsilon)
=
\frac{\Lambda_K(s-a\varepsilon)}{\Lambda_K(s)},
\]
where
\[
\Lambda_K(s)
=
|D_K|^{s/2}
\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s)^{r_1}
\Gamma_{\mathbb C}(s)^{r_2}
\zeta_K(s),
\]
with
\[
\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2),
\qquad
\Gamma_{\mathbb C}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s).
\]

Its first variation is
\[
\boxed{
J_{K,a}(s)
=
\left.\partial_\varepsilon\log\mathscr B_{K,a}\right|_0
=
-a\,\frac{\Lambda_K'(s)}{\Lambda_K(s)}.
}
\]

## 1. Start with the actual arithmetic sections and their theta observation

gives \(L_a=c_a\mathbb Z\). Its bounded-section count is
\[

\]

For an even Schwartz function \(\phi\), the exact weighted observation is
\[
\boxed{
\int_{(0,\infty)}\phi(tr)\,d\bigl(N_a(r)-1\bigr)
=
\sum_{v\in L_a\setminus\{0\}}\phi\bigl(th_a(v)\bigr).

\[
\Theta\phi(t)
=
\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}\phi(nt)
=
2\sum_{n\ge1}\phi(nt).

The principal-action arrow is also retained:
\[

and
\[
h_a(qr)=h_{qa}(r).
\]
Its split extension sends external absence to external absence. Thus the theta observation is compatible with the arithmetic objects and their arrows; it has not been introduced afterward as an unrelated function. For the cohomological calculation, use

with
\[

=
\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(x)e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx.
\]

The overlap space is

\mathscr B=
\left\{
F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}):
\sup_{x>0}x^b\left|(-x\partial_x)^kF(x)\right|<\infty
\quad

## 2. Compute an extension-by-zero map whose cokernel is this arithmetic quotient

Define the auxiliary chart space
\[
X_\theta=\{0,\eta,\infty\}
\]
with opens
\[
\varnothing,\quad
\{\eta\},\quad
U_+=\{0,\eta\},\quad
U_-=\{\eta,\infty\},\quad
X_\theta.
\]

Here \(0\) and \(\infty\) name the two chart endpoints. The scalar \(\tau\) is retained in the coefficient construction below; it is not substituted for a chart endpoint.

Define a sheaf \(\mathcal T\) by
\[
\mathcal T(U_+)=V,\qquad
\mathcal T(U_-)=V,\qquad
\mathcal T(\{\eta\})=\mathscr B.
\]

Its restrictions are
\[
r_+\phi=\Theta\phi,
\qquad
r_-\psi(x)=x^{-1}\Theta\psi(1/x).
\]

Poisson summation says
\[
r_-\widehat\phi=r_+\phi.
\]

Sections over each proper nonempty open are an exact evaluation functor on its sheaf diagram. Consequently, the two-open Čech complex computes the cohomology:
\[
\boxed{
C^\bullet:
V\oplus V
\xrightarrow{\ d\ }
\mathscr B,
\qquad
d(\phi,\psi)=\Theta(\phi-\widehat\psi).
}
\]

In particular,
\[
H^1(X_\theta,\mathcal T)
=
Q_\Theta^{\mathrm{alg}}
:=
\mathscr B/\Theta V.
\]

Now take the open inclusion
\[
j:U_+\hookrightarrow X_\theta.
\]

The extension-by-zero complex is
\[
C_+^\bullet=[V\xrightarrow{\Theta}\mathscr B].
\]

The actual sheaf map
\[
j_!j^*\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal T
\]
is represented by
\[
\boxed{
c^0(\phi)=(\phi,0),
\qquad
c^1(F)=F.
}
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
H^1(X_\theta,j_!j^*\mathcal T)
\xrightarrow{\ H^1(c)\ }
H^1(X_\theta,\mathcal T)
}
\]
is the identity on \(Q_\Theta^{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The proof is explicit: the chain-coordinate map
\[
(\phi,\psi)\longmapsto(\phi-\widehat\psi,\psi)
\]
decomposes \(C^\bullet\) as \(C_+^\bullet\) plus one copy of \(V\) in degree zero.

This is an extension-by-zero comparison on the **specified chart space**. I am not identifying that chart space with the full arithmetic curve or asserting that its cohomology already has Deligne’s weight bounds.

The Hausdorff realization is the specified quotient

\mathscr B/\overline{\Theta V}.

Its topology agrees with the strong-Schwartz topology defined in the current workbench appendix: the seminorms using \(x^N+x^{-N}\) and those using individual \(x^b\) bound each other directly. Let
\[

=

\]

For \(\phi\in V\), absolute convergence first gives
\[

=
2\zeta(s)M_+\phi(s),
\qquad \Re s>1.

\[

=
\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s),
\]
and define
\[
A_\phi(s)
=
\frac{2\pi^{s/2}M_+\phi(s)}
{s(s-1)\Gamma(s/2)}.
\]

Taylor subtraction at the real origin continues \(M_+\phi\) meromorphically. Its possible negative-even poles are canceled by the zeros of \(1/\Gamma(s/2)\). The two defining conditions on \(V\) handle the remaining displayed factors at \(s=0\) and \(s=1\). Hence \(A_\phi\) is entire, and
\[
\boxed{\mathcal M\Theta\phi=2\xi A_\phi.}
\]

No division by \(\xi\) at an arithmetic zero is used in that argument.

so

\qquad
\mathcal M\Theta\phi_*=2\xi.

This generator and the full-plane multiplier calculation are now also in the live arithmetic appendix. fileciteturn130file0L2-L5

### The precise diagram

With \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C}\),
\[

\begin{array}{ccc}

&\xrightarrow{\ 1\otimes\Theta\ }&

&\xrightarrow{\ \times 2\xi\ }&
\mathcal O,

where

\qquad

## 5. The map reaches every finite spectral jet, not only the zero values

Let \(Z\) be a finite set of actual zeros of \(\xi\), with their actual multiplicities \(m_\rho\). The map is
\[
\boxed{
J_Z:Q_\Theta^{\mathrm H}
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus_{\rho\in Z}
\mathbb C[t_\rho]/(t_\rho^{m_\rho}),
}
\]
\[
[F]\longmapsto
\left(
\sum_{j<m_\rho}
\frac{(\mathcal MF)^{(j)}(\rho)}{j!}t_\rho^j
\right)_\rho.
\]

It is well defined because every \(\mathcal M\Theta\phi\) is divisible by \(2\xi\). Continuity of the Mellin jets makes it vanish on the closure as well.

**For every \(R>0\), this map is already onto when representatives are restricted to**
\[
C_c^\infty((e^{-R},e^R)).
\]

To prove this, a dependence among its component functionals would imply
\[
\sum_{\rho,j}c_{\rho,j}e^{\rho y}\frac{y^j}{j!}=0
\qquad(-R<y<R).
\]

These exponential polynomials are independent. Applying
\[
\prod_{\sigma\ne\rho}(\partial_y-\sigma)^{m_\sigma}
\]
kills all other blocks and gives an invertible constant-plus-derivative operator on the remaining polynomial block. Thus every coefficient vanishes, proving surjectivity.

The continuation supplies a smooth right inverse, not just this rank argument. Choose \(0<R'<R\) and the bump
\[
\eta_{R'}(y)=
\begin{cases}
\exp[-1/((R')^2-y^2)],&|y|<R',\\
0,&|y|\ge R'.
\end{cases}
\]

For the jet index \(\alpha=(\rho,j)\), put
\[
r_\alpha(x)=x^{\bar\rho-1}\frac{(\log x)^j}{j!}.
\]

The matrix
\[
B_{\alpha\beta}
=
\frac1{j!k!}
\int_{-R'}^{R'}
\eta_{R'}(y)e^{(\rho+\bar\sigma-1)y}y^{j+k}\,dy
\]
is positive definite. For a prescribed finite jet vector \(v\),
\[
\boxed{
F_v(x)
=
\eta_{R'}(\log x)
\sum_\beta(B^{-1}v)_\beta r_\beta(x)
}
\]
is an exact smooth lift.

### The operator is also transported

For
\[
D=-x\partial_x,
\]
integration by parts gives
\[
\mathcal M(DF)=s\,\mathcal MF.
\]

On the \(\rho\)-block,
\[
\boxed{
D\longmapsto \rho I+N,
\qquad
N(t_\rho^j)=t_\rho^{j+1},
\qquad N^{m_\rho}=0.
}
\]

Dilation \(R_aF(x)=F(ax)\) becomes
\[
\boxed{
R_a\longmapsto
a^{-\rho}\exp\bigl(-(\log a)N\bigr).
}
\]

The location \(\rho\), its multiplicity, and its full nilpotent jet are retained by the same map.

## 6. There is now an exact norm to estimate on these actual spectral observations

This is the additional calculation most relevant to the weight question.

On
\[

\[

The measure is tied to the workbench’s retained half-density map:

because
\[

=
\int_{I_R}|F(x)|^2\,dx.

\[
\ell_\rho(F)=\mathcal MF(\rho),

the Riesz vector is \(x^{\bar\rho-1}\). Writing
\[
\kappa=2\Re\rho-1,

\[
\boxed{
\|\ell_\rho\|_{\mathcal H_R^*}^2
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{e^{\kappa R}-e^{-\kappa R}}{\kappa},
&\kappa\ne0,\\[3mm]
2R,&\kappa=0.
\end{cases}
}
\]

Consequently,
\[
\boxed{
\lim_{R\to\infty}\frac1R\log\|\ell_\rho\|
=
\left|\Re\rho-\frac12\right|.
}
\]

For all jets together, the exact Gram matrix is
\[
\boxed{
A_{(\rho,j),(\sigma,k)}
=
\frac1{j!k!}
\int_{-R}^{R}
e^{(\rho+\bar\sigma-1)y}y^{j+k}\,dy.
}
\]

It is positive definite by the same exponential-polynomial independence. The least-norm lift in \(\mathcal H_R\) is
\[
F_v^{\min}
=
\sum_\beta(A^{-1}v)_\beta r_\beta,
\qquad
\boxed{\|F_v^{\min}\|^2=\bar v^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}v.}
\]

The minimizer need not vanish at the interval endpoints. The infimum over smooth compactly supported exact lifts is nevertheless the same: approximate it in \(\mathcal H_R\), then correct the finite jet error with the smooth right inverse above.

## 1. Propagate the original congruence, not just its arithmetic image

Your original note gives the support-preserving congruence
\[

Its quotient and the subsequent arithmetic observation are
\[

G(R/I)\xrightarrow{p_{R/I}}R/I.
}
\]

The first arrow leaves \(\tau\) distinct from the supported zero residue. The second identifies them. These are the two congruences \(\rho_n,\rho_n'\) in the original integer formulation. fileciteturn136file0L2-L5

For a ring map \(h:R\to R'\) satisfying \(h(I)\subseteq I'\), the full diagram is
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(R)&\xrightarrow{G(h)}&G(R')\\
\downarrow q_I^{\mathrm{sp}}&&\downarrow q_{I'}^{\mathrm{sp}}\\
G(R/I)&\xrightarrow{G(\bar h)}&G(R'/I')\\
\downarrow p_{R/I}&&\downarrow p_{R'/I'}\\
R/I&\xrightarrow{\bar h}&R'/I'.
\end{array}
\]

The formulas commute on supported elements and on \(\tau\). The arithmetic norm remains the source’s
\[
N(I)=|R/I|,

equivalently the cardinality of the **supported fibre** inside \(G(R/I)\), rather than the cardinality including external absence.

### The corresponding quotient for your full semimodules

Write the source’s original decompositions as

be an actual \(G(R)\)-linear map. Here

is its support map.

\rho^N_{\varphi(\ell),k}\bigl(f_\ell(M_\ell)\bigr)

Then the quotient is
\[

=

\iff

## 1. Which statements actually carry RH strength?

Your recollection of several related criteria has a real mathematical basis. Their logical statuses need to remain visible:

| Statement | Role in this programme |
|---|---|

| The **full arithmetic spectral image has weight one**, with the spectral identification and its multiplicities retained. | The purity endpoint corresponding to the critical-line assertion. It has not been proved for our constructed object. |
| The paper’s finite spectral operators are self-adjoint in its specified quotient inner product. | A theorem under the paper’s simple-even hypothesis. |
| Their determinant functions converge to the actual \(\Xi\), with the stated factors and the required complex-domain convergence. | The paper’s proposed sufficient route to RH; the convergence is not established by finite self-adjointness. |

The paper explicitly uses
\[

\]
for its quotient inner product. Its abstract and concluding section identify the convergence step as still to be proved. That subtraction is central to understanding why its real finite spectra and global Weil positivity are not yet the same conclusion. fileciteturn148file7L85-L129

**None of my support-preservation calculations established the second or third row.** They constructed inputs for those rows. The research should now be measured against those endpoints, rather than against the number of additional constructions available over the support.

## 2. The precise Weil II mechanism to reproduce

For \(X_0\) smooth of finite type over \(\mathbb F_q\) and a lisse sheaf \(\mathcal F_0\) pure of weight \(w\), Deligne considers the actual map
\[
c_i:H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F).
\]

The two estimates are
\[
\operatorname{weights}H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\le w+i,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{weights}H^i(X,\mathcal F)\ge w+i.
\]

Consequently, the same image
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow I^i
\hookrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\]
has weight exactly \(w+i\). This is Weil II, Corollary 3.3.6, as retained in the supplied TeX. citeturn328388search0

The lower estimate comes through the particular duality map
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d).
}
\]

The upper bound on the compactly supported group on the right is
\[
-w+2d-i.
\]
Dualizing reverses its sign, and the retained \((-d)\) twist adds \(2d\), giving \(w+i\).

**That is the intended proof architecture: two bounds on the same arithmetic image, connected by its actual duality.** A common support point gives us somewhere to organize the fibres. The two-sided bound concerns the operator acting on what remains in those fibres.

In our setting, the relevant data must therefore travel together:
\[
\boxed{
\text{original supported quotient}
\;+\;
\text{arithmetic action}
\;+\;
\text{pairing}
\;+\;
\text{comparison estimates}.
}
\]

Merely pushing an object to a point does not supply the comparison
\[
Rf_!\longrightarrow Rf_*,
\]
its image, or the two estimates. Those are the morphisms and properties to construct over that point.

u_{\lambda,N}
=
\Pi_{\lambda,N}P_\lambda K.
\]

The original arithmetic relation becomes the supported zero in \(\mathfrak Q_{W_*}\). Its image in the finite ground-line quotient is the class
\[
[u_{\lambda,N}]_{E_N/L_{\lambda,N}}.
\]

Define, without changing the source’s eigenvector,
\[
b_{\lambda,N}
=
\frac{\langle v_{\lambda,N},u_{\lambda,N}\rangle}
{\langle v_{\lambda,N},v_{\lambda,N}\rangle},
\]
and retain the spectral gap
\[
g_{\lambda,N}
=
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(
\epsilon_{\lambda,N},
\operatorname{Spec}(A_{\lambda,N})
\setminus\{\epsilon_{\lambda,N}\}
\right).
\]

At a simple lowest eigenvalue, expansion in the orthogonal eigenspaces gives
\[
\boxed{
\|u_{\lambda,N}-b_{\lambda,N}v_{\lambda,N}\|
\le
\frac{
\|(A_{\lambda,N}-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}I)u_{\lambda,N}\|
}{
g_{\lambda,N}
}.
}
\]

This is an estimate for the discrepancy of the **actual arithmetic relation**, not an arbitrary trial quotient.

For \(0\le a<1/2\), Fourier evaluation on the interval has the exact bound
\[
|\widehat f(z)|\le C_{\lambda,a}\|f\|,
\qquad |\Im z|\le a,
\]
where
\[
C_{\lambda,a}^2=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\lambda^{2a}-\lambda^{-2a}}{2a},&a>0,\\[2mm]
2\log\lambda,&a=0.
\end{cases}
\]

Let the explicit omitted tail be
\[
T_\lambda(a)
=
\int_{(0,\lambda^{-1})\cup(\lambda,\infty)}
|K(u)|\max(u^a,u^{-a})\,\frac{du}{u}.
\]

Then the complete comparison is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{|\Im z|\le a}
\left|
b_{\lambda,N}\widehat v_{\lambda,N}(z)-\Xi(z)
\right|
\le{}&
T_\lambda(a)\\
&+C_{\lambda,a}\left(
\|(1-\Pi_{\lambda,N})P_\lambda K\|
+
\frac{
\|(A_{\lambda,N}-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}I)u_{\lambda,N}\|
}{
g_{\lambda,N}
}
\right).
\end{aligned}
}
\]

The theta tail tends to zero. At a fixed \(\lambda\), Fourier completeness controls the projection tail. **The uniform residual-to-gap estimate is the nontrivial term left in this explicit comparison.**

The source’s prolate-wave construction is directly relevant to estimating that term. Its §8 asks for the simple-even property and a sufficiently accurate comparison between the prolate-based trial function and the lowest eigenfunction of \(QW_\lambda\). The formula above attaches that question to our original arithmetic relation and its supported residual class. citeturn972558view0

## 6. The previous origin-jet work now has a specific role

The coordinate map is
\[
\sigma:\mathbb C_z\to\mathbb C_s,
\qquad
\sigma(z)=\tfrac12-iz,
\qquad
\sigma^{-1}(s)=i(s-\tfrac12).
\]

It gives
\[
\sigma^*(2\xi)=2\Xi,
\qquad
\sigma^*(s(1-s))=z^2+\tfrac14.
\]

Therefore the original support-preserving endpoint family becomes
\[
\boxed{
G\!\left(\mathcal O_s/(2\xi[s(1-s)]^m)\right)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
G\!\left(\mathcal O_z/(2\Xi[z^2+\tfrac14]^m)\right).
}
\]

The additional endpoint jets occur at
\[
z=-i/2,\qquad z=i/2.
\]

These are exactly the evaluation points in the paper’s polar term
\[
W_{0,2}(F)=\widehat F(i/2)+\widehat F(-i/2).
\]
fileciteturn148file7L471-L479

That locates the preceding work: it retains the endpoint sector accompanying the middle arithmetic factor. The new estimate in §5 addresses the comparison with that middle factor. The scalar \(\tau\) remains fixed under every displayed quotient map.

## 7. The primary target is a lower bound, not another support theorem

For the positivity route, the paper gives
\[
\mu_\lambda
=
\lim_{N\to\infty}\epsilon_{\lambda,N},
\qquad
\lambda'>\lambda
\Longrightarrow
\mu_{\lambda'}\le\mu_\lambda.
\]

The first identity uses its form-core theorem. Corollary 3.8 states that
\[
\mu_\lambda\longrightarrow0
\]
would establish RH. fileciteturn148file7L677-L691 fileciteturn148file7L902-L929

A concrete estimate to pursue is
\[
\boxed{
QW_\lambda^N(f,f)
\ge-r(\lambda)\|f\|^2
\quad\text{for every }N\text{ and }f,
\qquad
r(\lambda)\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

The quantifier “every \(N\)” matters. It gives
\[
\mu_\lambda\ge-r(\lambda).
\]
For fixed \(\lambda_0\) and arbitrarily large \(\lambda\),
\[
\mu_{\lambda_0}\ge\mu_\lambda\ge-r(\lambda),
\]
so
\[
\mu_{\lambda_0}\ge0.
\]

That establishes positivity of the **unshifted** form. Unlike the determinant route, this route does not require simplicity or evenness of its lowest eigenfunction.

This is where Weil II belongs: obtaining an upper and a dual lower estimate on the **same retained arithmetic comparison**, strong enough to force this sign. A nearly null theta vector provides a small Rayleigh quotient and hence an upper bound on the minimum. The lower bound must control the rest of the comparison image as well.

**The focused programme is therefore**
\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
\text{original split-support quotient and its nontrivial kernels}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{arithmetic relation versus finite spectral relation}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{retained form correction and quantitative comparison}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{Weil II-type two-sided control}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{positivity of the unshifted Weil form}.
\end{gathered}
}
\]

That is the RH branch being pursued. The support construction remains inside the maps; it is not being counted as an already-proved purity statement.

The linked note contains the full derivations, the source-reading ranges, and **17 exact algebraic checks**. It also records a literal factor-four discrepancy in v1’s Gaussian formula and retains the correcting scalar explicitly rather than silently changing either the paper’s input or \(\Xi\). No new GitHub changes were made in this turn.
