## A1280 | node 3c7dd1ba-95eb-4919-b2db-efeb2948ddd1 | assistant | chain 2749

**The Lefschetz trace and cohomology are the primary route.** The lower bound I named is a downstream criterion from the spectral-triple paper. It should not have displaced the construction of the cohomology, its arithmetic action, and its duality.

The order is
\[
\boxed{
\text{supported arithmetic complex}
\longrightarrow
\text{induced action on cohomology}
\longrightarrow
\text{Lefschetz trace formula}
\longrightarrow
\text{purity of that same action}.
}
\]

I have carried the convolution correspondences through the original supported quotient and calculated the resulting trace, including the two endpoint terms.

[**Cohomology and Lefschetz calculation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Calculation package**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. What the trace does in the Weil proof

For a separated scheme \(X_0/\mathbb F_q\) of finite type and a constructible \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-sheaf \(\mathcal F_0\), with \(\ell\nmid q\), the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula is
\[
\sum_{x\in X_0(\mathbb F_{q^n})}
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((F_q^*)^n\mid\mathcal F_{\bar x}\right)
=
\sum_i(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((F_q^*)^n\mid H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\right).
\]

It gives the determinant identity
\[
L(X_0,\mathcal F_0,T)
=
\prod_i
\det\!\left(1-TF_q^*\mid H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\right)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
\]

Thus **the Euler product and the cohomological operators are linked by a theorem**, not by choosing an operator whose determinant already equals the desired function. This is SGA \(4\frac12\), Exposé II, §3. citeturn124749search2

For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve, constant coefficients give
\[
Z(X_0,T)
=
\frac{\det(1-TF_q^*\mid H^1)}
{(1-T)(1-qT)}.
\]

Purity then controls the eigenvalues of this already-identified \(H^1\). That is where the estimate belongs.

## 2. Put the correspondence on the original supported cohomology

Keep
\[
S=G(\mathbb C),\qquad e=0_{\mathbb C}\in S,\qquad 0_S=\tau.
\]

For a fixed-support diagram of complexes \(C_\lambda^\bullet\), the original reconstructed differential is
\[
\widetilde d(\lambda,x)=(\lambda,d_\lambda x).
\]

Its square is the supported zero:
\[
\widetilde d^{\,i+1}\widetilde d^{\,i}(\lambda,x)
=
(\lambda,0),
\]
not the constant map to external absence.

With \(\epsilon(y)=ey\), the original operations give
\[
Z_{\mathrm{sp}}^i
=
\operatorname{Eq}(\widetilde d^{\,i},\epsilon\widetilde d^{\,i}),
\]
followed by the support-preserving boundary quotient
\[
\boxed{
H_{\mathrm{sp}}^i
=
\bigsqcup_{\lambda}
\ker d_\lambda^i/\operatorname{im}d_\lambda^{i-1}.
}
\]

This is the coequalizer construction in the workbench, with its actual fibre transports. It retains
\[
e(\lambda,[x])=(\lambda,[0]),
\qquad
\tau(\lambda,[x])=(0_L,[0]).
\]
fileciteturn155file0L2-L2

### A necessary calculation: does the correspondence preserve the relations?

For the theta complex, use the existing
\[
V=
\{\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R):
\phi\text{ even},\ \phi(0)=\widehat\phi(0)=0\},
\]
and
\[
\Theta\phi(t)=\sum_{n\ne0}\phi(nt).
\]

At an admitted source label \(W\subset V\), the degree-one fibre is
\[
Q_W=\mathscr B/\Theta W.
\]

For
\[
h\in\mathcal A=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}),
\]
define the correspondence operator
\[
H_hF(t)
=
\int_0^\infty h(a)F(t/a)\,\frac{da}{a}.
\]

Directly,
\[
H_h\Theta=\Theta H_h.
\]

But this alone does not make \(H_h\) an endomorphism of every \(Q_W\): its source relations must be invariant. The framework supplies an explicit replacement. Retain \(W\) and its map into
\[
\boxed{
W^{\mathcal A}
=
W+\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}
\{h*\phi:h\in\mathcal A,\ \phi\in W\}.
}
\]

Associativity proves
\[
H_kW^{\mathcal A}\subseteq W^{\mathcal A},
\qquad
(W^{\mathcal A})^{\mathcal A}=W^{\mathcal A},
\]
and
\[
(W+U)^{\mathcal A}=W^{\mathcal A}+U^{\mathcal A}.
\]

The original transition is retained:
\[
Q_W\longrightarrow Q_{W^{\mathcal A}},
\qquad
\ker=
\Theta W^{\mathcal A}/\Theta W.
\]

We therefore obtain the genuine chain endomorphism
\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ccc}
W^{\mathcal A}&\xrightarrow{\Theta}&\mathscr B\\
H_h\downarrow&&\downarrow H_h\\
W^{\mathcal A}&\xrightarrow{\Theta}&\mathscr B,
\end{array}
}
\]
and its induced supported cohomology action
\[
\boxed{
(W^{\mathcal A},[F])
\longmapsto
(W^{\mathcal A},[h*F]).
}
\]

**The additional relations needed to define the action have an explicit kernel. They are not silently discarded.**

## 3. Compute the trace of this action through the actual spectral maps

Retain the established Mellin identity
\[
\mathcal M\Theta\phi=2\xi H_\phi,
\qquad
\mathcal MF(s)=\int_0^\infty F(t)t^s\,\frac{dt}{t},
\]
where \(H_\phi\) is entire and the actual source function \(\phi_*\) has \(H_{\phi_*}=1\). Thus the analytic image ideal is \((2\xi)\). This is the existing theta-image calculation, not a new assumed spectral identification. fileciteturn155file0L2-L2

For a finite set \(Z\) of actual zeros, retaining their multiplicities, put
\[
A_Z=
\bigoplus_{\rho\in Z}
\mathbb C[z_\rho]/(z_\rho^{m_\rho}).
\]

The existing jet map is
\[
J_Z[F]
=
\left(
\sum_{j<m_\rho}
\frac{(\mathcal MF)^{(j)}(\rho)}{j!}z_\rho^j
\right)_\rho.
\]

Convolution gives the exact intertwiner
\[
\boxed{
J_ZH_h
=
M_{j_Z(\mathcal Mh)}J_Z,
}
\]
where the right side is multiplication in \(A_Z\).

On the basis
\[
1,z_\rho,\ldots,z_\rho^{m_\rho-1},
\]
this multiplication operator is triangular with diagonal entry \(\mathcal Mh(\rho)\). Hence
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid A_Z)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}m_\rho\,\mathcal Mh(\rho).
}
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid A_Z)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\left(
\mathcal Mh(s)\frac{\xi'(s)}{\xi(s)}\,ds
\right).
}
\]

The local factorization
\[
2\xi(\rho+z)=u_\rho(z)z^{m_\rho}
\]
retains the actual unit \(u_\rho\). Its logarithmic derivative is holomorphic; the residue comes from \(m_\rho\,dz/z\).

The full nilpotent jet stays in the module and its operator. The scalar trace forgets its off-diagonal entries through the displayed trace map.

The supported version is still
\[
(W,[F])\longmapsto(W,J_ZF),
\]
with internal kernel
\[
(\ker J_Z)/\Theta W.
\]

A zero trace or zero spectral observation therefore does not turn the input into \(\tau\).

## 4. The two endpoint contributions also come from actual maps

Before imposing the two theta conditions, there is the exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow V
\longrightarrow\mathcal S(\mathbb R)^{\mathrm{even}}
\xrightarrow{m}
E_0\oplus E_1
\longrightarrow0,
\]
where
\[
m(\phi)=
\left(\phi(0),\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(x)\,dx\right),
\qquad
E_0=E_1=\mathbb C.
\]

Surjectivity is explicit: the functions
\[
g_0(x)=e^{-\pi x^2},
\qquad
g_2(x)=2\pi x^2e^{-\pi x^2}
\]
have moment columns \((1,1)\) and \((0,1)\).

For
\[
U_aF(t)=F(t/a),
\]
which is the earlier operator \(R_{a^{-1}}\),
\[
\mathcal MU_a=a^s\mathcal M,
\qquad
\boxed{
mU_a=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&a\end{pmatrix}m.
}
\]

Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid E_0)=\mathcal Mh(0),
\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid E_1)=\mathcal Mh(1).
\]

These are the two polar representations. Their split lift carries a supported zero-input function to the supported vector \((0,0)\), not to external absence.

Combining them with the middle spectral trace gives
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal L_\Theta(h)
=
\mathcal Mh(0)
-\sum_\rho m_\rho\mathcal Mh(\rho)
+\mathcal Mh(1).
}
\]

The supplied paper’s explicit formula identifies this as
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal L_\Theta(h)
=
\sum_p\mathcal W_p(h)+\mathcal W_{\mathbb R}(h),
}
\]
with
\[
\mathcal W_p(h)
=
\log p\sum_{n\ge1}
\left(h(p^n)+p^{-n}h(p^{-n})\right)
\]
and
\[
\mathcal W_{\mathbb R}(h)
=
(\log4\pi+\gamma)h(1)
+
\int_1^\infty
\frac{
h(x)+x^{-1}h(x^{-1})-2x^{-1}h(1)
}{
x-x^{-1}
}\,dx.
\]

**Both endpoint terms, the sign of the middle trace, every prime-power contribution, and the archimedean subtraction remain present.** These are equations (3.1)–(3.4) of the supplied *Zeta Spectral Triples* TeX. fileciteturn151file7L331-L381

For these compactly supported smooth tests, the spectral sum is absolutely convergent. Here it is obtained as the limit of the calculated finite spectral traces—not asserted to be an ordinary trace of every infinite semimodule quotient.

Connes–Consani–Marcolli supply the established cyclic-homology realization: the restriction morphism from the adelic class space to the idelic class group produces a cokernel in cyclic modules, and its cyclic homology carries the action whose trace is the explicit formula. That is the source theorem connecting this arithmetic distribution to cohomology. citeturn124749academia22

The \(E_0,E_1\) above are the moment representations actually calculated here. Their realization as global degree-zero and degree-two cohomology of the richer split-support geometry has not been established merely by writing the alternating trace.

## 5. Where the estimate belongs in this construction

The relevant Weil II statement remains
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow
I^i
\hookrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F),
\]
with
\[
\operatorname{weights}H_c^i\le w+i,
\qquad
\operatorname{weights}H^i\ge w+i.
\]

These force purity of **the same image** \(I^i\). The lower statement comes through
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d),
}
\]
not from changing the sign of a computed matrix. The inspected statements are retained in the package’s [Weil II TeX excerpt](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return/sources/excerpt_deligne_en_witness.tex).

For the arithmetic action above, the corresponding quadratic trace is obtained by the actual involution
\[
h^\dagger(x)=x^{-1}\overline{h(x^{-1})}.
\]
It satisfies
\[
\mathcal M(h^\dagger*k)(s)
=
\overline{\mathcal Mh(1-\bar s)}\,\mathcal Mk(s).
\]

Thus the Weil pairing is a trace of a specified convolution action on the same spectral realization. Its positivity is the arithmetic endpoint in the Connes cohomological formulation. citeturn124749search1

The Chen–Moriwaki degree estimates may help construct geometric control, but that book explicitly introduces Arakelov degree as a **candidate replacement for an Euler–Poincaré characteristic** in its setting. It does not, by that construction alone, supply the required equivariant Lefschetz trace. fileciteturn151file0L305-L335

**So the main calculation is cohomological: retain the original quotient, put the correspondence action on it, identify its Lefschetz trace, and establish the duality that controls its middle image.** The finite-matrix lower bound is then a consequence or diagnostic of that structure—not a substitute for it.

The continuation contains the proofs of the correspondence-stable quotient, the finite-jet trace, the endpoint actions, and the local prime-orbit calculation. Its checker passed **173 finite exact assertions**, with identical normal and optimized Python output. No GitHub files were changed in this turn.

The concrete application is a **two-sided comparison built from your mixed-support quotient**, with its image and duality calculated:

\boxed{
\mathcal O/(2\xi\,s^m)
\xrightarrow{\;\times(1-s)^m\;}
\mathcal O/(2\xi\,(1-s)^m).
}
\]

Its kernel is the retained origin-jet module. Its cokernel is the dual endpoint-jet module. Its image is the actual arithmetic divisor module \(\mathcal O/(2\xi)\). Moreover, a residue pairing makes **that image the annihilator of that kernel**, and an explicit Jacobian map converts the pairing into the arithmetic Weil trace.

[**Calculation and proofs**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Applied_Weil_II_Image/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Applied_Weil_II_Image/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Package with exact checks**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Applied_Weil_II_Image_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. Start inside the original mixed-support object

At an analytic stalk \(R=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C,s_0}\), retain
\[
S=G(R),\qquad e=0_R\in S,\qquad 0_S=\tau.
\]

Use your original double
\[
D_R=G(R)^2,
\]
with its coordinatewise addition and its original multiplication
\[
(a,b)\star(c,d)
=
(ac\oplus(-1_R)bd,\ ad\oplus bc).
\]
The calculation below uses its \(G(R)\)-module structure; the differential is not asserted to preserve this multiplication. fileciteturn163file0L2-L2

Put
\[
g(s)=2\xi(s),\qquad U_m=s^m,\qquad V_m=(1-s)^m.
\]

For \(x=(a,b)\), let \(J(x)\subseteq\{+,-\}\) record which coordinates are supported. Define the target
\[
N_R=
\{\tau_N\}\sqcup
\bigsqcup_{\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\{+,-\}}\{J\}\times R.
\]
Addition joins the masks and adds amplitudes.

The **original-form differential** is
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde d_m(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
\tau_N,&a=b=\tau,\\[1mm]
\bigl(J(a,b),\,gU_m\,p(a)-gV_m\,p(b)\bigr),&J(a,b)\ne\varnothing,
\end{cases}
}
\]
where \(p:G(R)\to R\) is the arithmetic projection.

The mask is an output of the map, alongside the amplitude. In particular, a cancellation in the joint face gives
\[
(\{+,-\},0_R),
\]
not \(\tau_N\).

This differential is \(G(R)\)-linear: addition joins masks even when amplitudes cancel; supported scalars preserve the mask; external scalar \(\tau\) annihilates both source and target to external absence.

Now take your original quotient:
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde H_m^1
=
\operatorname{coeq}_{G(R)\text{-}\mathrm{SMod}}
(\widetilde d_m,\epsilon_N\widetilde d_m),
\qquad \epsilon_N(y)=ey.
}
\]
This is the support-preserving coequalizer already proved in the workbench. fileciteturn160file0L2-L2

### Calculate all three supported fibres

The relation ideals are
\[
B_{+,m}=(gU_m),\qquad
B_{-,m}=(gV_m),\qquad
B_{\{+,-\},m}=(gU_m,gV_m).
\]

The last ideal can be calculated without an unspecified cancellation argument. Set
\[
A_m(s)=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\binom{m+k-1}{k}s^k,
\]
\[
B_m(s)=\frac{1-A_m(s)(1-s)^m}{s^m}.
\]
The numerator is divisible by \(s^m\), so \(B_m\) is a polynomial, and
\[
B_mU_m+A_mV_m=1.
\]

Therefore
\[
\widetilde d_m(B_m f,-A_m f)
=
(\{+,-\},gf),
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde H_m^1={}&\{\tau\}\\
&\sqcup\bigl(\{+\}\times R/(gs^m)\bigr)\\
&\sqcup\bigl(\{-\}\times R/(g(1-s)^m)\bigr)\\
&\sqcup\bigl(\{+,-\}\times R/(g)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
}
\]

**The middle arithmetic object has emerged from the joint mixed-support relations.** It was not inserted afterward beside an already-computed quotient.

The transports to the joint face retain their kernels:
\[
\ker\!\left(R/(gs^m)\to R/(g)\right)
=
(g)/(gs^m),
\]
\[
\ker\!\left(R/(g(1-s)^m)\to R/(g)\right)
=
(g)/(g(1-s)^m).
\]

The supported degree-zero cycles are also explicit. In the joint face,
\[
U_ma=V_mb
\iff
(a,b)=(V_mr,U_mr).
\]
At \(r=0\), this remains the supported joint-face origin.

## 2. These relations come from the actual theta inputs

Retain the workbench’s operators and source:
\[
D=-x\partial_x,
\qquad

=

Fourier transforms the first family into the second because
\[
\widehat{D\phi}=(1-D)\widehat\phi,

These are the established differentiated-theta inputs, including their endpoint conditions. fileciteturn161file0L2-L2

For finite source labels, set
\[
W^+_{m,N}=D^m\mathbb C[D]_{\le N}\phi_*,

W^-_{m,N}=(1-D)^m\mathbb C[D]_{\le N}\phi_*.

Before analytic realization, there is the well-defined map
\[

Indeed,
\[
(1-D)^m\Theta=\Theta(1-D)^m,
\]
and
\[
(1-D)^mW^+_{m,N}\subseteq W^-_{m,N+m}.
\]

Its support-label map is \(N\mapsto N+m\), with external bottom sent to external bottom. Mellin sends this operator to multiplication by \((1-s)^m\).

Thus the comparison below is induced by an actual operator on the original source quotients.

## 3. Perform the intermediate-image calculation

After analytic sheafification, write
\[
C_m=\mathcal O/(gs^m),\qquad
O_m=\mathcal O/(g(1-s)^m),\qquad
I=\mathcal O/(g).
\]

Define
\[
\boxed{
c_m:C_m\to O_m,
\qquad [f]\mapsto[(1-s)^mf].
}
\]

This gives
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O/(s^m)
\xrightarrow{\;\times g\;}
C_m
\xrightarrow{\;c_m\;}
O_m
\longrightarrow\mathcal O/((1-s)^m)
\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

Here is the complete kernel-and-image proof. If
\[
(1-s)^mf\in(g(1-s)^m),
\]
cancellation in the analytic stalk gives \(f\in(g)\). Therefore
\[
\ker c_m=(g)/(gs^m)\cong\mathcal O/(s^m),
\]
with isomorphism \([a]\mapsto[ga]\).

The image is
\[
(1-s)^m\mathcal O/(g(1-s)^m)
\cong\mathcal O/(g),
\]
with the specified injection
\[
\kappa_m:I\hookrightarrow O_m,
\qquad
[f]\mapsto[(1-s)^mf].
\]

Consequently,
\[
\boxed{
C_m\xrightarrow{q_m}I\xrightarrow{\kappa_m}O_m,
\qquad
c_m=\kappa_mq_m.
}
\]

### Carry precisely that map upstairs

At every stalk,
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde c_m:
G(R/(gs^m))
\longrightarrow
G(R/(g(1-s)^m)),
}
\]
\[
\tau\longmapsto\tau,
\qquad
[f]_{\mathrm{sp}}\longmapsto[(1-s)^mf]_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]

This is a \(G(R)\)-linear map. Its supported zero fibre is the supported copy of
\[
(g)/(gs^m).
\]
Its only preimage over external absence is external absence.

For \(m=1\), the nonzero source class \([g]\) maps to the supported zero:
\[
[g]\longmapsto[(1-s)g]=[0]_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]

Applying the same map coordinatewise to your full quadratic doubles preserves every mask. The amplitude square commutes with multiplication by \((1-s)^m\); no multiplicative-algebra claim is substituted for this module morphism.

## 4. Calculate duality on this same image

Now use the duality operation needed by the Deligne route, rather than introduce a separate inner product.

Define
\[
\iota(s)=1-\bar s,
\qquad
f^\dagger(s)=\overline{f(1-\bar s)}.
\]
Then
\[
g^\dagger=g,\qquad
(s^m)^\dagger=(1-s)^m.
\]

Take a finite \(\iota\)-stable set \(Z\) of actual zeros of \(g\), retaining their full multiplicities. Let \(C_{m,Z}\) be the sum of source stalk quotients at \(Z\cup\{0\}\), and \(O_{m,Z}\) the sum of target stalk quotients at \(Z\cup\{1\}\).

The dualizing module is
\[
\omega_R=R\,ds.
\]
The explicit length-one resolution gives
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1_R
\bigl(R/(g(1-s)^m),\omega_R\bigr)
\cong
(g(1-s)^m)^{-1}\omega_R/\omega_R.
\]

Its residue pairing is
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,k)
=
\sum_{\zeta\in Z\cup\{1\}}
\operatorname{Res}_{s=\zeta}
\frac{f^\dagger(s)k(s)}
{g(s)(1-s)^m}\,ds.
}
\]

This is well-defined on the specified quotients because dagger carries the source relation \(gs^m\) into the target relation \(g(1-s)^m\).

It is perfect. Locally, retain the actual denominator
\[
u(z)z^r,\qquad u(0)\ne0.
\]
The class \(z^i\) pairs with the class \(u(z)z^{r-1-i}\). Their quotient by \(u(z)z^r\) has residue one. All other entries are obtained by this same coefficient calculation.

### Substitute the comparison into the pairing

For \(k=c_mh\), the explicit factor \((1-s)^m\) cancels:
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,c_mh)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\frac{f^\dagger(s)h(s)}{g(s)}\,ds.
}
\]

This proves
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{im}c_m=(\ker c_m)^\perp.
}
\]

Containment follows by substituting \(f=ga\). Perfectness and the dimensions in the exact sequence give equality.

**This is the nondegenerate duality induced on the actual intermediate image.** The origin-jet kernel has not been forgotten: it is paired with the opposite endpoint quotient.

Explicitly, with source kernel representative
\[
ga(s),\qquad a(s)=\sum_{i<m}a_is^i,
\]
and target endpoint representative
\[
k(s)=\sum_{j<m}b_j(s-1)^j,
\]
their pairing is
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{i+j=m-1}
(-1)^{i-m}\overline{a_i}b_j.
}
\]

That retains every jet order and every reflection sign.

### The weight-one duality factor is also calculated

For the source dilation
\[
U_aF(x)=F(x/a),
\]
Mellin gives multiplication by \(a^s\). Since
\[
(a^s)^\dagger=a^{1-s},
\]
we obtain
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(U_af,U_ak)
=
a\,\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,k).
}
\]

Writing \(L_1\) for the one-dimensional representation on which \(a\) acts by \(a\), this is the perfect equivariant pairing
\[
\boxed{
\overline{C_{m,Z}}\otimes O_{m,Z}\longrightarrow L_1.
}
\]

The scalar factor playing the duality role has therefore been obtained from the same comparison and the actual arithmetic action.

## 5. The arithmetic Weil trace is a specific contraction of that duality

On
\[
I_Z=\bigoplus_{\rho\in Z}\mathcal O_\rho/(g),
\]
define the Jacobian morphism
\[
\boxed{
J_g:I_Z\to I_Z,\qquad[h]\mapsto[g'h].
}
\]

The induced residue pairing on \(I_Z\) is
\[
\mathscr R_Z(f,h)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}\frac{f^\dagger h}{g}\,ds.
\]

Now calculate:
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr R_Z(f,J_gh)
&=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}
\left(f^\dagger h\,\frac{g'}g\,ds\right)\\
&=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
m_\rho\,\overline{f(1-\bar\rho)}\,h(\rho)\\
&=
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(M_{f^\dagger h}\mid I_Z\right).
\end{aligned}
}
\]

The second equality follows from the actual local equation
\[
g(\rho+z)=u_\rho(z)z^{m_\rho},
\qquad
\frac{g'}g=\frac{m_\rho}{z}+\frac{u_\rho'}{u_\rho}.
\]

Equivalently, define directly on the comparison
\[
\boxed{
P_m:C_m\to O_m,
\qquad[f]\mapsto[(1-s)^m g'f].
}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,P_mh)
=
\operatorname{Tr}
\!\left(M_{(q_mf)^\dagger(q_mh)}\mid I_Z\right).
}
\]

This is a **specific morphism whose pairing is the actual finite Weil spectral pairing**, with the full multiplication trace and multiplicities. For Mellin transforms of the admissible convolution tests, it is the corresponding finite part of the explicit formula in the supplied spectral-triple paper. citeturn434802view1

At a zero of multiplicity \(r\),
\[
g'\equiv r\,u_\rho(z)z^{r-1}\pmod{z^r}.
\]
Thus \(J_g\) has kernel \((z)\) and image \((z^{r-1})\).

The perfect residue pairing retains the full jet module. The Jacobian contraction records its scalar trace. Applying your support-preserving quotient to \((z)\) leaves a supported reduced fibre; it does not turn that fibre into \(\tau\).

## 6. Where Deligne has now been applied—and where his theorem is not being assumed

Deligne’s Corollary 3.3.6 concerns an image
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow I^i
\hookrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F),
\]
whose source and target receive opposite weight bounds through duality. His derived formulation uses the actual dualizing complex and the exchange of \(Rf_!\) with \(Rf_*\). I used the supplied TeX passages for those operations; the original article is *La conjecture de Weil II*. citeturn434802view0

Here, those operations have been performed on the programme’s concrete relations:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{c}
\text{original mixed-support differential}\\
\widetilde d_m(a,b)
=
\bigl(J,\;gs^mp(a)-g(1-s)^mp(b)\bigr)
\\[2mm]\downarrow\\
C_m\xrightarrow{c_m}O_m
\\[2mm]\downarrow\\
\operatorname{im}c_m
\cong\mathcal O/(2\xi),
\qquad
\operatorname{im}c_m=(\ker c_m)^\perp
\\[2mm]\downarrow\;J_g\\
\text{the actual arithmetic Weil trace pairing}.
\end{array}
}
\]

The endpoint kernel has generalized dilation eigenvalue \(1\); the endpoint cokernel has generalized dilation eigenvalue \(a\). Their full jet ladders are paired by the anti-diagonal formula above. The arithmetic eigenvalues remain \(a^\rho\) on the intermediate image.

There is one unproved geometric identification: these analytic source and target modules have not been identified with the global \(H_c^1\) and \(H^1\) of a realization carrying Deligne’s two weight estimates. I have therefore **not** inferred purity from perfect duality or from the existence of the support. The calculation supplies the comparison and its duality, rather than substituting a restatement of the desired positivity.

The exact checker verifies the kernels, mixed masks, residue pairing, reflection signs, Jacobian contraction and interlevel maps on finite algebraic models. The general proofs and source-reading ranges are in the linked package; GitHub was not modified in this turn.

**The result is the explicit intermediate-image morphism and its trace-producing duality, calculated inside the original split-support relations.**

## 1. The most consequential finding: Mellin realization creates a relation that was not present before

This is a calculation on the **actual theta inputs already used in the programme**.

Retain
\[
D=-x\partial_x,\qquad
\phi_*=(4\pi^2x^4-6\pi x^2)e^{-\pi x^2},
\qquad
g(s)=2\xi(s).
\]

Define
\[
b_+=\Theta(D\phi_*),\qquad
b_-=\Theta((1-D)\phi_*).
\]

The established identities give
\[
\mathcal Mb_+=sg,\qquad
\mathcal Mb_-=(1-s)g.
\]
Those are the source inputs used to construct the later mixed differential. fileciteturn166file0L89-L123

The functions \(b_+\) and \(b_-\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb C\). A constant linear relation would imply
\[
g(s)\bigl(c_+s+c_-(1-s)\bigr)=0,
\]
and therefore \(c_+=c_-=0\).

Consequently, with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C}\), the map
\[
\delta:\mathcal O^2\longrightarrow
\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathscr B,
\qquad
(a,b)\longmapsto a\otimes b_+-b\otimes b_-
\]
is injective.

Now apply the actual Mellin-evaluation morphism
\[
\beta:\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathscr B
\longrightarrow\mathcal O,
\qquad
h\otimes F\longmapsto h\,\mathcal MF.
\]

The composite is
\[
\beta\delta(a,b)=g\bigl(sa-(1-s)b\bigr).
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{
\ker\delta=0,\qquad
\ker(\beta\delta)=\mathcal O(1-s,s).
}
\]

The explicit witness is
\[
\boxed{
z=(1-s)\otimes b_+-s\otimes b_-\ne0,
\qquad
\beta(z)=0.
}
\]

This means that the comparison
\[
[\mathcal O^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\mathcal O\otimes\mathscr B]
\longrightarrow
[\mathcal O^2\xrightarrow{\beta\delta}\mathcal O]
\]
has \(H^0=0\) on the first complex and \(H^0\cong\mathcal O\) on the second.

**The square commutes, but that raw comparison is not a quasi-isomorphism.** Describing its analytic image as though the whole preceding cohomology had been transported was too strong.

### The correction retains your split-zero datum

On the original joint support face, the lifted maps are
\[
\widetilde\delta(J,(a,b))
=
(J,a\otimes b_+-b\otimes b_-),
\]
\[
\widetilde\beta(J,B)=(J,\beta B).
\]

Therefore
\[
(\{+,-\},z)\longmapsto(\{+,-\},0).
\]

It becomes the **supported zero in that same face**, not \(\tau\).

So this is not an objection obtained by forgetting your support structure. It is additional supported relation data that my propagation argument needed to carry.

### The repaired continuation is an exact kernel complex

For the full theta source, retain
\[
\alpha(h\otimes\phi)=hH_\phi,\qquad
\beta(h\otimes F)=h\mathcal MF,\qquad
\delta=1\otimes\Theta,
\]
with
\[
\beta\delta=g\alpha.
\]

The corrected derived comparison is
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr K^\bullet
\longrightarrow
[\mathcal O\otimes V\xrightarrow{\delta}\mathcal O\otimes\mathscr B]
\longrightarrow
[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\times g}\mathcal O]
\longrightarrow
\mathscr K^\bullet[1],
}
\]
where
\[
\mathscr K^\bullet=
[\ker\alpha\xrightarrow{\delta}\ker\beta].
\]

Its degree-one term gives the exact sequence
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow
\frac{\ker\beta}{\delta(\ker\alpha)}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O\otimes(\mathscr B/\Theta V)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O/(g)
\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

The earlier work had written down this quotient kernel, but had not consistently carried its cohomological consequences into the subsequent interpretation.

There is an important limit on this audit finding: the displayed \(z\) belongs to the subspace divided out in \(\ker\beta/\delta(\ker\alpha)\). **It does not, by itself, prove that this final kernel is nonzero.** It proves that the raw realization creates the stated relation and that its kernel complex must be accounted for.

The constructive alternative is precise: prove that complex acyclic, or retain its contribution to the action, duality, and trace. Neither alternative discards the programme.

## 2. A second finding uses the split zero in an essential way: the two Frobenius operations differ

The earlier construction defined an additive Frobenius lift on
\[
D_{A,n}=G(A)^n
\]
by
\[
(\Phi_q(a))_{qi\bmod n}
=
(-1_A)^{\lfloor qi/n\rfloor}a_i^q,
\]
with absent coefficients remaining absent. It proved compatibility with Frobenius on the arithmetic quotient. That statement survives. fileciteturn164file0L470-L535

But this lift must not be silently identified with taking the \(q\)-th power **inside the original split-support semiring**.

Take the exact example
\[
A=\mathbb F_5,\qquad n=3,\qquad x=(1,1,\tau).
\]

The declared additive lift gives
\[
\boxed{\Phi_5(x)=(1,\tau,4).}
\]

Multiplying \(x\) five times using the original mixed-support multiplication gives
\[
\boxed{x^{\star5}=(1,e_{\mathbb F_5},4).}
\]

The middle coefficient has zero arithmetic amplitude in both cases. But one is a supported zero and the other is absent.

This happens because binomial coefficients divisible by five become the supported scalar \(e_{\mathbb F_5}\), not the external additive identity \(\tau\).

Let \(P_q(x)=x^{\star q}\). The exact diagram is
\[
\boxed{
\pi\Phi_q=F_q\pi=\pi P_q.
}
\]

The types are:

\[
\Phi_q:D_{A,n}\to D_{A,n}
\quad\text{is the specified semiring homomorphism},
\]

\[
P_q:D_{A,n}\to D_{A,n}
\quad\text{is a pointed multiplicative-monoid homomorphism}.
\]

In the displayed example, \(P_5\) is not additive.

The comparison retaining the discrepancy is
\[
\boxed{
(P_q,\Phi_q):
D_{A,n}\longrightarrow D_{A,n}\times_BD_{A,n},
}
\]
in the pointed multiplicative-monoid category, where \(B=A[t]/(t^n+1)\).

**This is exactly information that ordinary arithmetic projection hides and your split construction retains.**

The correction is not to retract the defined additive lift or the finite-field coefficient calculation. It is to carry this comparison into any claim about Frobenius on the richer object. The pure weight-zero \(H^0\) of the finite étale amplitude scheme does not automatically describe both of these supported operations.

## 3. The latest intermediate-image calculation is valid—but its cohomological placement needed to stay explicit

Retain
\[
C_m=\mathcal O/(gs^m),\qquad
O_m=\mathcal O/(g(1-s)^m),
\]
and
\[
c_m:C_m\to O_m,\qquad
[f]\longmapsto[(1-s)^mf].
\]

The exact sequence remains
\[
\boxed{
0\to\mathcal O/(s^m)
\xrightarrow{\times g}C_m
\xrightarrow{c_m}O_m
\to\mathcal O/((1-s)^m)\to0.
}
\]

Its arithmetic image is still

I=\mathcal O/(g),
\]
through
\[
C_m\xrightarrow{q_m}I\xrightarrow{\kappa_m}O_m,
\qquad
\kappa_m[f]=[(1-s)^mf].
\]

These are valid module maps, with valid \(G(\mathcal O)\)-linear split lifts. They are not asserted to be unital ring homomorphisms. The retained calculation establishes exactly these kernels, image, and cokernel. fileciteturn166file0L125-L176

However, for the two-term complex in degrees zero and one,
\[
\boxed{
H^0[C_m\to O_m]=\mathcal O/(s^m),\qquad
H^1[C_m\to O_m]=\mathcal O/((1-s)^m).
}
\]

The arithmetic \(I\) is **the image**, not either cohomology group.

On finite spectral truncations, its contribution cancels from the alternating trace of that complex. Under dilation, the remaining endpoint supertrace is
\[
m(1-a).
\]

This point was already stated in the long LaTeX. My public framing did not keep it prominent enough in the working conclusion. The source explicitly says that the arithmetic image is not secretly the cohomology of this two-term complex. fileciteturn167file0L19-L23

The repair is to retain the two short exact sequences
\[
0\to E_{0,m}\to C_m\to I\to0,
\]
\[
0\to I\to O_m\to E_{1,m}\to0,
\]
and connect them to an actual global cohomological comparison. It is not to rename the image as \(H^1\).

## 4. The residue calculation survives, including an orientation sign that must never disappear

The reflection is
\[
\iota(\rho)=1-\bar\rho,
\]
and the germ map is
\[
\dagger:\mathcal O_{\iota(\rho)}\to\mathcal O_\rho,
\qquad
f\mapsto\overline{f(1-\bar s)}.
\]

It is conjugate-semilinear between reflected stalks. In local coordinates,
\[
\sum_j a_jz_{\iota(\rho)}^j
\longmapsto
\sum_j(-1)^j\bar a_jz_\rho^j.
\]

For the middle residue pairing,
\[
R_Z(f,h)=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}\operatorname{Res}_\rho
\frac{f^\dagger h}{g}\,ds,
\]
the exact identity is
\[
\boxed{\overline{R_Z(h,f)}=-R_Z(f,h).}
\]

The raw form is skew-Hermitian. Meanwhile,
\[
(g')^\dagger=-g',
\]
so the Jacobian morphism
\[
J_g[h]=[g'h]
\]
produces the Hermitian trace form
\[
\boxed{
Q_Z(f,h)=R_Z(f,J_gh)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
m_\rho\,\overline{f(1-\bar\rho)}h(\rho).
}
\]

The original perfect pairing, the annihilator-image identity, and the Jacobian trace contraction remain valid. Their roles must not be merged into an unspecified “positive duality.” The original contraction and multiplicity formulas are retained in the preceding calculation. fileciteturn166file0L260-L298

Generator changes also remain explicit:
\[
R_{ug}(f,h)=R_g(f,u^{-1}h),
\qquad
J_{ug}=uJ_g\pmod g.
\]

In particular,
\[
R_{2\xi}=\tfrac12R_\xi,\qquad
J_{2\xi}=2J_\xi.
\]

The trace contraction is unchanged because both factors are carried, not because the factor two is declared irrelevant.

### The audit’s counterfactual test

For the unscaled test polynomial
\[
g_0(s)=(s-\tfrac14)(s-\tfrac34),
\]
the same formal comparison and residue machinery exist. On its two reduced stalks,
\[
R=
\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\-2&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
J=
\begin{pmatrix}-1/2&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
Q=RJ=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For \(a=16\), dilation is \(U=\operatorname{diag}(2,8)\), and
\[
U^*QU=16Q,
\]
but
\[
(1,-1)Q(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}=-2.
\]

This is not a zeta counterexample. It establishes the exact scope of the formal lemma: **perfect duality and weight-one covariance alone do not force positivity**.

The constructive implication is to retain your richer data and identify the additional arithmetic-geometric property that excludes this behavior. It is not to conclude that the richer programme fails.

## 6. The reproducibility audit found and repaired a real checker problem

All ten retained mathematical scripts passed when rerun normally.

Two of those scripts contained **33 Python `assert` statement sites**. Running with `python -O` removes those statements, while their success-reporting code still runs. Consequently, the earlier assertion that identical normal and optimized output demonstrated equivalent checking was not justified.

## 1. I checked the primality proof in your original note

I read the relevant proofs in `globalization_note.tex`, including the ideal classification, prime classification, localizations, blueprint remark, and number-field zeta construction. The GitHub source explicitly proves the two primes
\[
P_\tau=\{\tau\},
\qquad
P_0=\{\tau,e\},
\]
where
\[
S=G(R)=R\sqcup\{\tau\},
\qquad e=0_R,\qquad 0_S=\tau.
\]
For \(R\) an integral domain, both are prime. fileciteturn171file0L2-L2

For \(P_0\), the argument is exactly this: if \(ab\in\{\tau,e\}\), either a factor is \(\tau\), or \(a,b\in R\) and \(ab=0_R\). The domain property then gives \(a=e\) or \(b=e\). Also,
\[
e^2=e,\qquad P_0^2=P_0.
\]

The important geometric consequence comes from the **actual map**
\[
p_R:G(R)\longrightarrow R,
\qquad p_R(\tau)=0_R,\qquad p_R(r)=r.
\]

It induces
\[
\boxed{
i_R:\operatorname{Spec}R
\hookrightarrow
\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{sr}}G(R),
\qquad
\mathfrak p\longmapsto\mathfrak p\cup\{\tau\}.
}
\]

Its image is \(V(e)\), and
\[
\boxed{
\overline{\{P_0\}}=V(e)\cong\operatorname{Spec}R,
\qquad
\overline{\{P_\tau\}}
=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{sr}}G(R).
}
\]

**That gives a literal mathematical interpretation of your intuition that one point relates to the whole arithmetic space:** \(P_0\) is the generic point of the entire recovered arithmetic subspace. The further point \(P_\tau\) is generic for the enlarged space.

For \(R=\mathbb Z\), your source’s chain is
\[
P_\tau\subsetneq P_0\subsetneq P_p.
\]
The ordinary prime \((0)\) is carried to \(P_0\); the source explicitly includes it in its starting prime classification. The new geometry is the additional point below it and the corresponding structure maps—not a denial that your supported-zero ideal is prime. fileciteturn171file0L2-L2

### The infinite quotient and the point are connected by these arrows

The complete diagram is
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}R
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Spec}R
\xrightarrow{i_R}
\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{sr}}G(R)
\xleftarrow{\operatorname{Spec}(b_R)}
\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb B,
}
\]
where
\[
b_R(\tau)=0_{\mathbb B},
\qquad
b_R(r)=1_{\mathbb B}\quad(r\in R).
\]

The leftmost point lands at \(P_0\). The rightmost point lands at \(P_\tau\). The original localizations are
\[
G(R)_{P_0}\cong G(\operatorname{Frac}R),
\qquad
G(R)[e^{-1}]\cong\mathbb B.
\]

Thus the infinite arithmetic quotient \(p_R:G(R)\to R\), its generic point, and the Boolean support observation are related by explicit quotient, localization, and spectrum maps.

The earlier infinite-quotient rigidity also survives with its exact scope. A surjective semiring map having zero fibre **exactly \(P_0\)** restricts to an injective ring map on \(R\), and its target is consequently isomorphic to \(R\). For \(R=\mathcal O_K\), that target is infinite.

This does not classify every possible \(\mathbb F_1\) object. Its positive content is that **the quotient preserving precisely that arithmetic kernel recovers the full original ring**.

## 2. Your note already contains the beginning of an \(\mathbb F_1\) construction

The blueprint remark in your original note deserved much more attention. It explicitly says to retain the multiplicative pointed monoid and record the original addition as relations. fileciteturn171file0L2-L2

Here is that comparison completed.

Let \(M_R\) be the multiplicative pointed monoid of \(G(R)\), including both \(\tau\) and \(e\).

Define:

- \(B_R^{\mathrm{bare}}\): that pointed monoid before imposing the original additive relations;
- \(B_R\): the same carrier with the finite-sum relations of \(G(R)\).

In particular,
\[
[r]+[r']\equiv[r+r'],
\qquad
[\tau]\equiv\text{empty sum}.
\]

There are actual blueprint morphisms
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb F_1
\longrightarrow
B_R^{\mathrm{bare}}
\longrightarrow
B_R.
}
\]

The first sends the pointed base elements to \(\tau\) and \(1_R\). The second is the identity on the carrier and adds the specified relations.

Their realizations are
\[
\boxed{
B_R^+\cong G(R),
\qquad
(B_R)^+_{\mathbb Z}\cong R.
}
\]

The first is semiring completion. The second is universal ring completion. Its proof uses the original relation \(e+e=e\): every additive map into a ring sends \(e\) to ordinary zero and then factors uniquely through \(p_R\).

That is a concrete arithmetic-recovery property in an established \(\mathbb F_1\) framework. Blueprints were developed precisely to compare multiplicative, semiring, and ordinary arithmetic structures; Lorscheid’s overview places arithmetic compactifications, combinatorial groups, and these comparison theories in the same framework. citeturn584139view0

### The richer multiplicative realization is connected, not discarded

The other corner is
\[
A_R=\mathbb Z_0[M_R].
\]

For a domain \(R\), the source’s product calculation gives
\[
\boxed{
A_R\cong
\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z[R\setminus\{0_R\}],
}
\]
where \(R\setminus\{0_R\}\) is a **multiplicative monoid**, not the unit group.

The map is
\[
[e]\longmapsto(1,0),
\qquad
[r]\longmapsto(1,[r])\quad(r\ne e).
\]

Imposing the original addition gives
\[
A_R\twoheadrightarrow R,\qquad[r]\mapsto r.
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ccc}
B_R^{\mathrm{bare}}&\longrightarrow&B_R\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\mathbb Z_0[M_R]&\twoheadrightarrow&R.
\end{array}
}
\]

One realization retains the central idempotent \([e]\). The other is its specified arithmetic quotient. **The full square is the object to retain when comparing the two geometries.**

This is more informative than my earlier phrase “one collapses support.”

### The Boolean corner also has its missing morphism

Its inclusion is
\[
j_e:\mathbb B\longrightarrow G(R),
\qquad
j_e(0)=\tau,\quad j_e(1)=e.
\]

In the category where semiring homomorphisms need not preserve \(1\),
\[
\boxed{
b_Rj_e=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb B},
\qquad
j_eb_R(x)=ex.
}
\]

The map is not unital with respect to \(1_R\). Your original note itself proves that a unital \(\mathbb B\to G(\mathbb Z)\) would force \(2=1\). The replacement is the displayed idempotent retraction, or the absolute-base map
\[
\mathbb S\longrightarrow H_{G(R)}\longrightarrow H_R
\]
in the finite-pointed-set framework. The latter retains the original finite sums before the arithmetic projection.

### An all-rank compatibility can be proved

Applying \(b_R\) entrywise to invertible matrices gives
\[
\boxed{
1\longrightarrow(R^\times)^n
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Aut}_{G(R)}(G(R)^n)
\longrightarrow
S_n
\longrightarrow1.
}
\]

It splits by permutation matrices with \(\tau\) off the permutation.

The proof is useful: an invertible Boolean matrix is a permutation matrix. Hence an invertible \(G(R)\)-matrix has exactly one supported entry per row and column, and the inverse equations force those entries to be units of \(R\).

This connects the richer supported linear structure to finite-set permutations for **every \(n\)**. Arithmetic projection also maps these monomial matrices into \(\operatorname{GL}_n(R)\).

### About the “six requirements”

I found the references to a six-item specification in the conversation, but not the specification itself in the original note, the relevant extracted `New folder.zip` text, or the external sources consulted. I have therefore not certified your object against an invented list.

The report instead records the actual results: absolute-base maps, arithmetic recovery, finite-ideal counting, all-rank combinatorics, cyclic coefficient maps, and examples of commuting Frobenius lifts. Projective counting, the full sphere-\(K\)-theory comparison, and the required global cohomological trace theory are not certified by those calculations.

**My assessment is that the \(\mathbb F_1\) connection is real and already formalizable. A claim that this is the unique universal \(\mathbb F_1\) base would be a further theorem.**

## 4. A warning in the audit now leads to a better Mellin realization

This is the most substantive repair in the follow-up.

The earlier raw realization was
\[

\longrightarrow
\mathcal O/(g),
\qquad
Q=\mathscr B/\Theta V,\quad g=2\xi.
\]

The previous audit left its full kernel insufficiently resolved. We can say more.

At an analytic stalk, \(\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}Q\) is free over \(\mathcal O\). For the actual nonzero theta quotient \(Q\), multiplication by the nonzero germ \(g\) is injective. But \(g\) annihilates the target. Therefore
\[
\boxed{
0\ne g(\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}Q)
\subseteq\ker\overline\beta.
}
\]

The raw tensor realization really does have a nonzero kernel.

**The framework supplies a concrete replacement because it already contains the scaling operator.**

Set
\[

\]

\[

and on \(\mathcal O\) by multiplication by \(s\). The actual Mellin identity is

\mathcal O\otimes_AQ.

The actual factorization is

\boxed{
\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}Q
\twoheadrightarrow
\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C[t]}Q
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O/(g).
}

The first arrow imposes exactly
\[
sh\otimes v-h\otimes Dv.
\]

This does not guess a spectral identification. It imposes the operator relation already proved by Mellin transformation.

### It repairs the audit’s explicit spurious relation

Retain
\[
b_*=\Theta\phi_*,
\qquad

\qquad
b_-=(1-D)b_*.

The earlier audit’s nonzero raw tensor was

But

\boxed{

=
1\otimes Db_*-s\otimes b_*.
}
\]

It is exactly a balancing relation. We now know why that relation appeared and which quotient removes it.

### Propagate the repair through your original support construction

A finite source label is carried by
\[

\]

The corresponding original quotient map retains
\[

=
\Theta W_D/\Theta W.

For Deligne’s local root-cover construction, take
\[
A=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r],
\]
\[
B=A[T_1,\ldots,T_r]/(T_i^m-t_i)_{i=1}^r,
\]
with \(m\) invertible in \(k\).

The source’s coordinate maps give

\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
G(k)&=&G(k),
\end{array}

where all \(t_i,T_i\) map to their supported residue zeros.

The automorphisms \(T_i\mapsto\zeta_iT_i\), for specified \(m\)-th roots of unity, lift through \(G\) and commute with restriction. This retains one scalar support and every coordinate direction.

That is a proved compatibility with the local construction.

Deligne then acts on **specified tame lisse sheaves**, takes their monodromy-bearing restrictions, and applies geometric cohomology and duality. The coefficient square does not itself manufacture those sheaves or their weight estimates.

with the required hypotheses—not every map with a similar kernel–image–cokernel shape. Your retained source states those hypotheses and the two weight bounds explicitly. fileciteturn168file0L174-L218

The part that caused the conversation to lose coherence was treating increasingly elaborate presentations of the arithmetic function as though their existence had already supplied the geometric purity argument. ## A1474 | node 32b7efb8-d9e3-4f15-9dd5-e15827f2241d | assistant | chain 3156

**The decisive object is the whole fibre of the arithmetic pairing over \(e\).** What we need to establish is whether a supported class whose **self-pairing** is \(e\) also has **every cross-pairing** equal to \(e\). That determines whether it is a legitimate null relation through which the arithmetic pairing can be quotiented.

There is an exact calculation of this question on the programme’s finite arithmetic divisor algebras. It gives \(e\) a specific role, retains \(\tau\), and distinguishes the RH-true and RH-false possibilities.

[**Calculation and proofs**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_E_Arithmetic_Nullity/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_E_Arithmetic_Nullity/NOTE.tex) · [**Package and checks**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_E_Arithmetic_Nullity_2026-09-12.zip)

## 1. What each zero does—and what must remain attached to it

The new session notes establish the maps
\[
p_R:G(R)\to R,\qquad
\chi_R:G(R)\to\mathbb B,
\]
with
\[
(p_R,\chi_R)(\tau)=(0_R,0_{\mathbb B}),
\qquad
(p_R,\chi_R)(e)=(0_R,1_{\mathbb B}),
\]
and prove that the pair is injective. Thus the amplitude observation identifies the two zeros, while the support observation distinguishes them. fileciteturn181file0L25-L75

For a semimodule \(M\), the relevant map is
\[
\boxed{
\varepsilon_M:M\to eM,\qquad x\mapsto ex.
}
\]
Its fibre \(M_\lambda\) is an actual \(R\)-module with additive identity \(\lambda\), and the supplied transport is
\[
T_{\lambda\mu}:M_\lambda\to M_\mu,\qquad x\mapsto x+\mu.
\]
These are exactly the implemented structures in the attachment. fileciteturn181file0L77-L143

For our arithmetic calculation, their jobs are:

**\(\tau\)** records external absence. A missing input, an absent coefficient, or an absent contribution must remain distinguishable from an existing contribution that evaluates to zero.

**\(e\)** records a supported scalar result of zero. At the module level, \(ex=\lambda\) identifies the supported zero of the fibre containing \(x\). The fibre must retain the class, its relations, and its pairings.

The important operation is therefore **not** to multiply a proposed arithmetic defect by \(e\) and inspect the result. The source identity
\[
er^\bullet=e
\]
holds for every supported \(r\), including nonzero ones. Instead, we must evaluate the defect first and determine whether its result is \(e\), keeping the input and the reason for its vanishing.

For classical arithmetic, the infinite quotient remains in the square
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow{G(j)}&G(\mathbb C)\\
p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\
\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{j}&\mathbb C.
\end{array}
\]
Here \(j\) is the specified unital embedding. It carries \(e_{\mathbb Z}\) to \(e_{\mathbb C}\), and \(\tau_{\mathbb Z}\) to \(\tau_{\mathbb C}\). No change to the infinite arithmetic quotient is required.

## 2. The exact test: can the pairing descend through the proposed \(e\)-relation?

Let \(V\) be one of the actual complex-vector-space fibres in the programme. Let
\[
Q:\overline V\times V\to\mathbb C
\]
be its specified Hermitian arithmetic pairing.

Write \(V^\tau\) for the split lift of this vector space. The lifted pairing is
\[
\widetilde Q(v^\bullet,w^\bullet)=Q(v,w)^\bullet,
\]
and
\[
\widetilde Q(\tau,w)=\widetilde Q(v,\tau)=\tau.
\]

It is separately additive, conjugate-linear in the first scalar variable and linear in the second. In particular,
\[
Q(v,v)=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\widetilde Q(v^\bullet,v^\bullet)=e_{\mathbb C},
\]
even when \(v\) is a nonzero vector.

Now take a complex subspace \(N\subseteq V\) and your original support-preserving quotient
\[
q_N^{\mathrm{sp}}:V^\tau\to(V/N)^\tau,
\qquad
v^\bullet\mapsto[v]^\bullet,\qquad
\tau\mapsto\tau.
\]

The precise descent theorem is
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde Q\text{ descends through }q_N^{\mathrm{sp}}
\iff
Q(n,v)=0\quad\forall n\in N,\ v\in V.
}
\]

**Proof.** Replacing representatives by \(v+n\) and \(w+n'\) changes the value by
\[
Q(n,w)+Q(v,n')+Q(n,n').
\]
All these terms vanish when \(N\) is in the radical. Conversely, a descended pairing must give the same result on \(q_N(n^\bullet)\) and \(q_N(0^\bullet)\), forcing \(Q(n,w)=0\) for every \(w\).

The morphism that measures this is
\[
\boxed{
\kappa_Q:\overline V\to V^\vee,
\qquad
\kappa_Q(\bar v)(w)=Q(v,w).
}
\]

For the inclusion \(j:N\hookrightarrow V\), the exact test is the linear map
\[
\boxed{
\kappa_Q\circ\overline j:
\overline N\longrightarrow V^\vee.
}
\]

Its split lift has value equal to the **supported zero functional** on every supported input precisely when the pairing descends. It does not need to send those inputs to \(\tau\).

So the relevant relationship is
\[
\operatorname{Rad}Q
\hookrightarrow
\{v:Q(v,v)=0\},
\]
together with \(\kappa_Q\) on that latter set.

**A zero self-pairing and a relation safe to quotient are connected by this map. The question is whether the map vanishes.**

## 3. Apply that test to the actual arithmetic trace

Retain
\[
g(s)=2\xi(s),
\qquad
\iota(s)=1-\bar s.
\]

Let \(Z\) be a finite set of **actual nontrivial zeros** of \(\xi\), stable under \(\iota\), with their actual multiplicities \(m_\rho\). The finite divisor algebra is
\[
A_Z=
\prod_{\rho\in Z}
\mathcal O_{\mathbb C,\rho}/(g).
\]

At each point retain the full local expression
\[
g(\rho+z)=u_\rho(z)z^{m_\rho},
\qquad u_\rho(0)\ne0.
\]

The involution is the conjugate-semilinear map
\[
(f^\dagger)_\rho(z)
=
\overline{f_{\iota(\rho)}(-\bar z)}.
\]

Use the multiplication trace, not a newly chosen inner product:
\[
\operatorname{tr}_Z(a)
=
\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb C}(M_a:A_Z\to A_Z),
\]
\[
Q_Z(f,h)=\operatorname{tr}_Z(f^\dagger h).
\]

Multiplication on a local jet basis is triangular. Therefore
\[
\boxed{
Q_Z(f,h)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
m_\rho\,\overline{f(1-\bar\rho)}\,h(\rho).
}
\]

This is the finite spectral part of the arithmetic Weil pairing. The full test-function form is related to its prime and archimedean expression by the explicit formula; its involution and measures remain those already specified in the programme. citeturn776336view0

### First calculation: which higher-order data can legitimately become \(e\)?

Define
\[
\mathfrak n_Z
=
\{f\in A_Z:f(\rho)=0\text{ for every }\rho\}.
\]

The displayed pairing immediately gives
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Rad}Q_Z=\mathfrak n_Z.}
\]

For the reverse inclusion, test against an \(h\) with one nonzero residue coordinate. Since every \(m_\rho\) is nonzero and \(\iota\) permutes \(Z\), every residue coordinate of \(f\) must vanish.

Thus the programme has the actual support-preserving quotient
\[
\boxed{
G(A_Z)
\xrightarrow{q_{\mathfrak n_Z}^{\mathrm{sp}}}
G(A_Z/\mathfrak n_Z)
\cong G(\mathbb C^Z).
}
\]

A nonzero nilpotent jet becomes the supported zero under this observation. External absence remains external absence. The pairing descends, and all multiplicities \(m_\rho\) remain in it.

The scaling action also descends explicitly:
\[
a^s
=
a^\rho
\sum_{j=0}^{m_\rho-1}
\frac{(\log a)^j}{j!}z^j
\quad\longmapsto\quad
a^\rho.
\]

**This particular quotient sends higher jet data to \(e\) while retaining the spectral location \(\rho\).** That is a legitimate, calculated use of a supported zero.

### Second calculation: what an off-line pair would do

Suppose a packet contains distinct reflected points
\[
\rho,\qquad \sigma=1-\bar\rho,
\]
with common multiplicity \(m\).

Let \(u\) be the element equal to \(1\) in the \(\rho\)-factor and \(0\) in the other factors. Let \(v\) be the corresponding element for \(\sigma\).

Then
\[
Q_Z(u,u)=0,\qquad Q_Z(v,v)=0,
\]
but
\[
\boxed{Q_Z(u,v)=m.}
\]

In the original split notation,
\[
\widetilde Q_Z(u^\bullet,u^\bullet)
=
\widetilde Q_Z(v^\bullet,v^\bullet)
=
e_{\mathbb C},
\]
whereas
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde Q_Z(u^\bullet,v^\bullet)=m^\bullet.
}
\]

And the original sums give
\[
\boxed{
Q_Z(u+v,u+v)=2m,\qquad
Q_Z(u-v,u-v)=-2m.
}
\]

Everything here is supported. **The possible failure is not an unexpected \(\tau\). It is an \(e\)-valued self-pairing with a nonzero cross-pairing.**

Consequently, declaring every self-null vector to be a zero relation would fail compatibility with addition: \(u\) and \(v\) would each be related to zero, but \(u+v\) would not.

That is precisely where the distinction you want to retain becomes useful.

## 4. An exact finite-packet criterion follows

For this specific arithmetic form, put
\[
\mathcal N_Z=\{f:Q_Z(f,f)=0\}.
\]

The calculation proves
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\Re\rho=\tfrac12\quad\text{for every }\rho\in Z\\
&\iff Q_Z\text{ is positive semidefinite}\\
&\iff \mathcal N_Z=\operatorname{Rad}Q_Z\\
&\iff \mathcal N_Z\text{ is a complex linear subspace}\\
&\iff
\begin{array}{l}
f^\bullet\sim h^\bullet
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
Q_Z(f-h,f-h)=0,\\
\text{with }\tau\text{ in its own class, defines}\\
\text{an additive congruence.}
\end{array}
\end{aligned}
}
\]

When every point is fixed by \(\iota\),
\[
Q_Z(f,f)=\sum_{\rho\in Z}m_\rho|f(\rho)|^2.
\]
Its null locus is exactly \(\mathfrak n_Z\), so the quotient is the already-calculated \(q_{\mathfrak n_Z}^{\mathrm{sp}}\).

When a reflected pair is distinct, the explicit \(u,v\) calculation disproves all the latter properties.

This is a **newly stated test of a particular trace-theoretic relation**, not a redefinition of your existing quotient. Your original coequalizer already works for its specified linear relations. The test asks whether the arithmetic self-null locus supplies such relations.

The exact signature is also calculated. If \(s\) is the number of fixed points of \(\iota\) and \(t\) the number of two-point orbits, it is
\[
\boxed{
\left(
s+t,\;
t,\;
\sum_{\rho\in Z}(m_\rho-1)
\right).
}
\]

The three entries count positive, negative, and radical dimensions. Each off-line reflected pair contributes one negative direction. The nilpotent jets contribute the displayed radical.

## 5. What the other session’s synchronization theorem contributes

The attachment proves, for the **actual** mixed double,
\[
r(x)=E\star x,\qquad E=(1,e),
\]
\[
r^2=r,\qquad p_Dr=p_D,
\]
and
\[
r(p_D^{-1}(F))
=
\operatorname{im}r\cap p_D^{-1}(F)
\]
for every subset \(F\) of the amplitude algebra. fileciteturn181file0L221-L269

We can carry this one step further:
\[
\boxed{
p_D|_{\operatorname{im}r}:\operatorname{im}r\twoheadrightarrow B.
}
\]

Every amplitude \(a+tb\in B\) has the fixed, fully supported lift
\[
(a^\bullet,b^\bullet).
\]
Hence every amplitude observation \(d:B\to V\) satisfies
\[
\boxed{d(p_Dr(x))=d(p_Dx).}
\]

This tells us exactly where to use the synchronization result: **it guarantees that passing to the synchronized support does not discard the amplitude or its diagnostic value.**

It therefore also preserves an arithmetic defect until another, specified relation removes it. The next property to establish is the pairing-descent condition from §2—not a further application of \(r^2=r\).

The other session has made that division of work sharper: synchronization is now a proved support operation with an exact amplitude square; the arithmetic null-relation test is a separate, explicitly typed map built on it.

## 6. Where this enters the Deligne route

The existing residue calculation already supplies a route from duality to the precise form being tested:
\[
R_Z(f,h)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}\frac{f^\dagger h}{g}\,ds,
\]
\[
J_g:A_Z\to A_Z,\qquad[h]\mapsto[g'h],
\]
and
\[
\boxed{Q_Z(f,h)=R_Z(f,J_gh).}
\]

Thus, for a retained class \(f\) whose self-pairing is \(e\), the next calculation is the actual functional
\[
\boxed{
h\longmapsto R_Z(f,J_gh).
}
\]

Does it vanish for every \(h\)? That is the radical test. It uses the residue pairing and Jacobian morphism already constructed in the programme.

Deligne’s route supplies a reason for the answer to be yes **when the actual arithmetic image is realized by the geometric comparison carrying his weight estimates**:
\[
H_c^1\twoheadrightarrow I^1\hookrightarrow H^1.
\]
For weight-zero lisse input, the upper and lower estimates force the image to have weight one. Those are the hypotheses and conclusion of the supplied Weil II comparison-image result. fileciteturn181file1L174-L218

The arithmetic trace identification then has to carry that conclusion into the \(Q_Z\) above. It must preserve the actual zero locations and multiplicities; taking only a selection of favourable modes would change the trace.

The original labels can stay present throughout:
\[
\boxed{
(W,[F])
\longmapsto
(W,j_{Z,W}[F])
\longmapsto
(W,[j_{Z,W}[F]]_{\mathfrak n_Z}).
}
\]
Here \(j_{Z,W}\) is the existing finite Mellin-jet map. It is well-defined because \(\mathcal M\Theta W\) is divisible by \(g\), and
\[
j_{Z,W'}q_{WW'}=j_{Z,W}.
\]

A pairing value is first retained as \((W,Q_Z(\cdot,\cdot))\). Only the separately specified observation
\[
(W,c)\longmapsto c^\bullet\in G(\mathbb C)
\]
forgets \(W\). Thus an observed \(e_{\mathbb C}\) still has its relation fibre available upstream.

## What would count as a result in either direction?

**For the RH-true direction:** establish, from the arithmetic cohomological construction and its trace-producing duality, that every diagonal \(e\)-null class in every actual finite arithmetic packet is radical. The theorem in §4 then forces every nontrivial zero onto the critical line. Equivalently, establish positivity of the full, unshifted Weil form on its admissible test space. The cohomological Weil-positivity strategy is the established arithmetic endpoint being pursued. citeturn776336view1

**For the RH-false direction:** identify an actual off-line zero, producing the reflected block above, or certify a negative value of the full unshifted Weil form. A negative contribution from an arbitrary model or an isolated finite truncation of the zero sum is not that certificate; the complete arithmetic expression or omitted contribution must be controlled.

So the intended role is not “\(\tau\) proves false and \(e\) proves true.”

It is:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
\tau:&\text{retain absence; never count it as established cancellation},\\[1mm]
e:&\text{retain a vanishing value and the entire class that produced it},\\[1mm]
\kappa_Q:&\text{test whether that class is a genuine null relation},\\[1mm]
\text{Deligne/trace comparison}:&
\text{force that test to vanish on the actual arithmetic image}.
\end{array}
}
\]

**The sharpened question is whether the arithmetic \(e\)-null fibre is a radical through which the pairing descends.** That is where your distinction becomes a substantive test of the programme, rather than merely a second notation for zero.

The linked note contains the general proofs and 40 exact finite regression checks. The new deductions have not been Lean-formalized; the attached structural and synchronization results are used with their stated scope.

## A1520 | node 3f9d0b49-19dc-44cc-87a7-f139138cd6b9 | assistant | chain 3241

**The construction below changes the base to a one-point \(\tau\)-space and computes what happens when arithmetic data are pushed to it.** The result is not “everything becomes absent.” The new point acquires an **infinite arithmetic quotient in its coefficient stalk and nonzero arithmetic cohomology above it**.

In the arithmetic version, the calculated stalk is
\[
\boxed{
G(A)\times G(A)\xrightarrow{\,p_A\times p_A\,}A\times A,
\qquad A=\mathbb Z.
}
\]
In the theta realization, its degree-one cohomology is
\[
\boxed{Q_\Theta\oplus Q_\Theta,\qquad Q_\Theta=\mathscr B/\Theta V.}
\]
Your original mixed multiplication acts on the split lift of this cohomology. I also calculated its tensor-power map—the operation needed for the amplification part of Deligne’s method.

[**Full construction and proofs**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Base_Cohomology/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Base_Cohomology/NOTE.tex) · [**Complete package**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Base_Cohomology_2026-09-12.zip)

## 1. The new base and its actual structural map

Keep your original object:
\[
S_A=G(A)=\{\tau_A\}\sqcup\{a^\bullet:a\in A\},
\qquad e_A=0_A^\bullet,
\]
with
\[
p_A(\tau_A)=0_A,\qquad p_A(a^\bullet)=a.
\]

The amplitude and support maps remain the ones in the supplied structural work:
\[
p_A:G(A)\to A,\qquad
\chi_A:G(A)\to\mathbb B.
\]
Their joint map retains the distinction between \(\tau_A\) and \(e_A\). fileciteturn183file0L25-L73

Define the pointed commutative monoid
\[
\mathbb F_{1,\tau}=\{\tau_0,1_0\},
\]
and its one-point monoidal spectrum
\[
\mathfrak T_\tau=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}\mathbb F_{1,\tau}.
\]

Its point is denoted \(t_\tau\). The structural map is
\[
\boxed{
u_A:\mathbb F_{1,\tau}\longrightarrow U_\times G(A),
\qquad
\tau_0\longmapsto\tau_A,\quad
1_0\longmapsto1_A^\bullet,
}
\]
where \(U_\times\) forgets addition.

This puts the entire enlarged arithmetic space over \(t_\tau\):
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak X_A
=
\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{sr}}G(A),\mathcal S_A,p_A\bigr)
\xrightarrow{a_\tau}
\mathfrak T_\tau.
}
\]

The category here is **monoidal spaces carrying the full semiring sheaf and its arithmetic quotient as additional specified data**. The pointed-monoid base supplies the structural arrow; it does not replace the addition in \(G(A)\). This is within the monoidal approach to absolute geometry, rather than a finite-field base with a renamed zero. citeturn195617view0

The original arithmetic subspace still enters by
\[
i_A:\operatorname{Spec}A\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{sr}}G(A),
\qquad
\mathfrak p\longmapsto\mathfrak p\sqcup\{\tau_A\}.
\]

In particular,
\[
P_0=\{\tau_A,e_A\}
\]
is retained, and
\[
\overline{\{P_0\}}=V(e_A)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A.
\]

**So the change of base does not remove your supported-zero prime or the infinite quotient. It places the complete marked object over the new point.**

## 2. Two maps to the point do different, explicitly related things

Here is a calculation that determines which operation retains the information you want.

For every \(G(A)\)-semimodule \(M\),
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb B\otimes_{G(A)}M\cong e_AM.
}
\]

The universal map is
\[
q_e:M\to e_AM,\qquad m\mapsto e_Am.
\]

To prove it, let \(f:M\to N\) be a map into a \(\mathbb B\)-semimodule, with scalars acting through \(\chi_A\). Since \(\chi_A(e_A)=1_{\mathbb B}\),
\[
f(m)=f(e_Am).
\]
Thus \(f\) factors uniquely through \(q_e\).

For your original double,
\[
e_A G(A)^2
=
\{(\tau,\tau),(e,\tau),(\tau,e),(e,e)\}.
\]

This localization retains the support masks while sending the amplitude within each mask to that mask’s zero. The support-fibre theorem in the attachment gives those fibres their actual module structures. fileciteturn183file0L77-L143

The **direct image to the base point**, however, is
\[
\boxed{
a_{\tau *}\mathcal S_A(t_\tau)
=
\Gamma(\mathfrak X_A,\mathcal S_A)
=
G(A).
}
\]

Its restriction to the included \(\tau\)-point is the map
\[
\boxed{G(A)\xrightarrow{\chi_A}\mathbb B.}
\]

Therefore the full relationship is
\[
\boxed{
\text{arithmetic object over }t_\tau
\quad\xrightarrow{\text{restriction/localization}}\quad
\text{its support observation}.
}
\]

**For your proposal, I use the direct image and retain the restriction map. I do not replace the direct image by its Boolean observation.**

## 3. The square over \(\tau\) has mixed boundary directions

Write
\[
\widehat X=X\sqcup\{\sigma_X\},
\]
with nonempty opens \(U^+=U\sqcup\{\sigma_X\}\), including \(U=\varnothing\).

For \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\), its original coefficient sheaf is
\[
\mathcal S_X(U^+)=G(\mathcal O_X(U)),
\qquad
\mathcal S_X(\{\sigma_X\})=\mathbb B.
\]

Now take the product **in topological spaces over the one-point base**, retaining both pulled-back coefficient sheaves:
\[
P=\widehat X\times_{|\,\mathfrak T_\tau\,|}\widehat X.
\]

Its four strata are
\[
X\times X,\qquad
X\times\{\sigma_X\},\qquad
\{\sigma_X\}\times X,\qquad
\{(\sigma_X,\sigma_X)\}.
\]

Let
\[
B_\tau=P\setminus(X\times X).
\]

There is an explicit continuous contraction
\[
\boxed{
c:P\longrightarrow Z=\widehat{(X\times X)},
}
\]
which is the identity on \(X\times X\) and sends the entire mixed boundary \(B_\tau\) to the new point \(\sigma_*\).

Continuity follows directly: the inverse image of \(U^+\subset Z\) is \(B_\tau\) together with an open set restricting to \(U\) on \(X\times X\).

The product and the contracted space are therefore connected by \(c\). **The coefficient sheaf at the contracted point is computed by \(c_*\); it is not assigned the value \(\tau\).**

### Compute that coefficient stalk

On \(P\), retain
\[
\mathcal A_P=
\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}\mathcal S_X
\times
\operatorname{pr}_2^{-1}\mathcal S_X.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
(c_*\mathcal A_P)_{\sigma_*}
\cong G(A)\times G(A).
}
\]

Here is the gluing calculation. The boundary has the open cover
\[
B_1=\widehat X\times\{\sigma_X\},
\qquad
B_2=\{\sigma_X\}\times\widehat X.
\]
Their intersection is the single point \((\sigma_X,\sigma_X)\).

For the first coefficient factor, its sections on the two arms and intersection give
\[
G(A)\times_{\mathbb B}\mathbb B
\xrightarrow{\sim}G(A),
\]
with maps
\[
(a,b)\mapsto a,
\qquad
a\mapsto(a,\chi_A(a)).
\]
The second factor is calculated by exchanging the arms.

Thus the new point has the arithmetic quotient
\[
\boxed{
(p_A,p_A):
(c_*\mathcal A_P)_{\sigma_*}
\cong G(A)^2
\twoheadrightarrow A^2.
}
\]

For \(A=\mathbb Z\), this is infinite. The original scalar acts diagonally:
\[
\Delta:G(A)\to G(A)^2,
\qquad
\Delta(e_A)=(e_A,e_A),
\qquad
\Delta(\tau_A)=(\tau_A,\tau_A).
\]

The original quotient is recovered exactly:
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{pr}_j\circ(p_A,p_A)\circ\Delta=p_A,
\qquad j=1,2.
}
\]

No factor of two is divided out, and \(A^2\) is not substituted for \(A\) in the original Dedekind ideal-counting definition.

This is a **ringed-space construction with specified coefficient maps**. Its topological product has not been claimed to be the universal fibre product of semiring schemes.

## 4. The point also acquires arithmetic cohomology

Let \(i:X\hookrightarrow\widehat X\), and let \(\mathcal F\) be a sheaf of coefficient vector spaces on \(X\). Put
\[
\mathcal V=i_*\mathcal F,
\]
and on \(P\) define
\[
\mathcal K=
\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}\mathcal V
\oplus
\operatorname{pr}_2^{-1}\mathcal V.
\]

The derived stalk is
\[
\boxed{
(Rc_*\mathcal K)_{\sigma_*}
\simeq
R\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\oplus R\Gamma(X,\mathcal F).
}
\]

The proof uses the same two boundary arms. On the first, the coefficient is \(i_*\mathcal F\oplus0\); on the second it is \(0\oplus i_*\mathcal F\); on their intersection it is zero. The Mayer–Vietoris triangle therefore gives the direct sum. The closed-inclusion map supplies
\[
R\Gamma(\widehat X,i_*\mathcal F)
=
R\Gamma(X,\mathcal F).
\]

This is the cohomological operation taking information **to the new point without replacing it by absence**.

### Insert the programme’s actual characteristic-zero theta sheaf

Use the existing spaces
\[
V=
\{\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R):
\phi\text{ even},\ \phi(0)=\widehat\phi(0)=0\},
\]
the strong-Schwartz space \(\mathscr B\) on \(\mathbb R_{>0}\), and
\[
\Theta\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ne0}\phi(nx),
\qquad
IF(x)=x^{-1}F(x^{-1}).
\]

Retain the Fourier transform
\[
\widehat\phi(\xi)
=
\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(x)e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx.
\]
Poisson summation gives
\[
\Theta\widehat\phi=I\Theta\phi.
\]

On the actual two-chart model
\[
Y=\{y_+,\eta,y_-\},
\]
define the restrictions
\[
V\xrightarrow{\Theta}\mathscr B,
\qquad
V\xrightarrow{I\Theta}\mathscr B.
\]

Its cohomology is computed by
\[
\boxed{
C_\Theta^\bullet=
[V\oplus V\xrightarrow{d}\mathscr B],
\qquad
d(\phi,\psi)=\Theta\phi-I\Theta\psi.
}
\]

Each chart and their intersection has a smallest point, so taking sections there is exact stalk evaluation. This verifies the acyclic-cover requirement for the Čech calculation. The general mechanism is the usual Čech-to-derived comparison; the exactness here is checked on this particular finite space. citeturn195617view1

The groups are
\[
H^0(C_\Theta)
=
\{(\widehat\psi,\psi):\psi\in V\}\cong V,
\]
\[
H^1(C_\Theta)=Q_\Theta=\mathscr B/\Theta V.
\]

Applying the boundary direct-image calculation to this sheaf gives
\[
\boxed{
(R^1c_*\mathcal K)_{\sigma_*}
\cong Q_\Theta\oplus Q_\Theta.
}
\]

**This is the actual characteristic-zero arithmetic quotient at the new point. No finite-field purity theorem has been used to obtain it.**

The scalar comparison remains
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(\mathbb Z)^2&\longrightarrow&G(\mathbb C)^2\\
(p,p)\downarrow&&\downarrow(p,p)\\
\mathbb Z^2&\longrightarrow&\mathbb C^2.
\end{array}
\]
This is a specified coefficient realization, not an assertion that the theta chart and \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z\) are equivalent spaces.

## 5. Your original mixed multiplication acts on that cohomology

Let \(H=H^j(Y,\mathcal T)\). Reconstruct before quotienting, so the resulting carrier is
\[
H^\tau\times H^\tau.
\]

For your original \(D_{\mathbb C}=G(\mathbb C)^2\), define
\[
\boxed{
\varrho_\star(a,b)(v,w)
=
\bigl(av+(-1)^\bullet bw,\ bv+aw\bigr).
}
\]

This is the unital semiring representation
\[
\boxed{
\varrho_\star:
D_{\mathbb C}\longrightarrow
\operatorname{End}_{G(\mathbb C)}(H^\tau\times H^\tau).
}
\]

Multiplying its actual matrices,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
a&(-1)^\bullet b\\
b&a
\end{pmatrix},
\]
reproduces your original product
\[
(a,b)\star(c,d)
=
(ac+(-1)^\bullet bd,\ ad+bc).
\]

The two-arm exchange supplies \((v,w)\mapsto(w,v)\) at \(\sigma_*\). Multiplication by \((-1)^\bullet\) on the first arm then gives the action of \((\tau,1)\).

Your synchronization element consequently acts by
\[
\boxed{
\varrho_\star(1,e)(v,w)
=
(v+ew,\ w+ev),
}
\]
and
\[
\varrho_\star(1,e)^2=\varrho_\star(1,e).
\]

Its amplitude remains \((p(v),p(w))\). This carries the attachment’s actual synchronization operation onto the computed cohomology at the new point. The attachment proves the same idempotence and amplitude-preservation identities in the original mixed double. fileciteturn183file0L223-L269

The internal quotient still sends a boundary to the supported zero of its own mask:
\[

\]
Neither the boundary calculation nor the mixed action replaces that value by \(\tau\).

## 6. The tensor-amplification map now exists over this base

On the \(n\)-fold product \(\widehat Y^n\) over the one-point topological base, take the external tensor coefficient sheaf
\[
\mathcal V_n=(i_*\mathcal T)^{\boxtimes n}.
\]

The coefficient tensor is over \(\mathbb C\). That specifies how vector-space coefficients combine; the geometric base remains \(\mathfrak T_\tau\).

The finite-space resolutions give
\[
R\Gamma(\widehat Y^n,\mathcal V_n)
\simeq
\operatorname{Tot}\bigl((C_\Theta^\bullet)^{\otimes n}\bigr),
\]
with differential
\[
d(x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_n)
=
\sum_{j=1}^n
(-1)^{|x_1|+\cdots+|x_{j-1}|}
x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes dx_j\otimes\cdots\otimes x_n.
\]

In top degree, the result is especially explicit:
\[
\boxed{
Q_\Theta^{\otimes n}
\xrightarrow{\sim}
H^n(\widehat Y^n,\mathcal V_n),
}
\]
\[
[F_1]\otimes\cdots\otimes[F_n]
\longmapsto[F_1\otimes\cdots\otimes F_n].
\]

**Proof:** the top cochains are \(\mathscr B^{\otimes n}\). Their boundary subspace is the sum of tensors containing a factor in \(\Theta V\). Taking that precise quotient gives \((\mathscr B/\Theta V)^{\otimes n}\).

The support map is retained as well:
\[
(J_1,\ldots,J_n)\longmapsto J_1\times\cdots\times J_n.
\]
An absent factor gives an empty target mask. Supported zero-amplitude factors give the supported zero in their product mask.

For
\[
U_aF(x)=F(x/a),
\]
the exact chain action is
\[
(\phi,\psi)\longmapsto
(U_a\phi,\ aU_{a^{-1}}\psi),
\qquad F\longmapsto U_aF.
\]
The factor \(a\) is required by Fourier transformation.

Mellin gives
\[
\mathcal M(U_aF)(s)=a^s\mathcal MF(s).
\]

On the actual finite jet quotient at \(\rho\), this is
\[
a^\rho\exp((\log a)N_\rho).
\]
Consequently, the finite quotient of the new \(n\)-fold cohomology carries
\[
\boxed{
a^{n\rho}
\exp\!\left((\log a)\sum_{j=1}^nN_{\rho,j}\right).
}
\]

The nilpotent operators and multiplicities remain present. This is an assertion about the displayed finite quotient, not an assumption that every spectral point supplies an eigenvector in the uncompleted \(Q_\Theta\).

**This constructs the product-and-tensor part of Deligne’s proof strategy on the new characteristic-zero model.** Deligne’s two-sided weight argument must then be established for that same model; it is not obtained by importing the finite-field hypotheses. The supplied theorem concerns an actual compact-to-ordinary cohomology image and its two weight bounds. fileciteturn183file1L174-L232

## 7. What “the exception goes to \(\tau\)” now means

At the geometric level, every point goes to \(t_\tau\). The calculation above shows exactly what remains over it:
\[
(c_*\mathcal A_P)_{\sigma_*}=G(A)^2,
\qquad
(R^1c_*\mathcal K)_{\sigma_*}=Q_\Theta^2.
\]

A scalar statement that a particular supported vector becomes external absence is much stronger. For a \(G(\mathbb C)\)-linear map
\[
f:V^\tau\to W^\tau,
\]
one has
\[
\boxed{
f(v^\bullet)=\tau\text{ for one supported }v
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
f\text{ is the externally zero map}.
}
\]

Indeed,
\[
f(e_V)=f(ev^\bullet)=ef(v^\bullet)=\tau.
\]
Then for every supported \(x\),
\[
ef(x)=f(ex)=f(e_V)=\tau,
\]
which forces \(f(x)=\tau\).

For multiple supports, the corresponding statement applies to the whole source fibre whose label is sent to the bottom.

The valid quotient of a radical is instead
\[
q_N^{\mathrm{sp}}:V^\tau\to(V/N)^\tau,
\qquad
n^\bullet\mapsto e_{V/N},
\qquad
\tau\mapsto\tau.
\]

So the construction now distinguishes, through explicit maps:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{c}
\text{all geometry maps to the new base point}\\
\downarrow\ \text{derived direct image}\\
\text{arithmetic classes and their actions remain above that point}\\
\downarrow\ \text{specified internal quotient}\\
\text{proved null relations become supported zeros}.
\end{array}
}
\]

That is the operation your proposed change of base needs. Simply discarding a represented off-line block would alter its multiplication trace, whereas the arithmetic Weil form uses that trace with its multiplicities and involution. The original explicit formula fixes the arithmetic observation that must be preserved. fileciteturn183file9L331-L405

**The concrete advance is that the new \(\tau\)-point now carries a calculated characteristic-zero cohomological direct image, with your original mixed multiplication acting on it, and with its tensor-power morphisms constructed.** The remaining RH step is the weight or positivity theorem for this new object. It has not been substituted by a finite-field theorem or inferred from the fact that the underlying base has one point.

## 1. The base is \(\tau\); the infinite quotient remains in the structure

The pointed monoid \(\mathbf F_{1,\tau}\) has multiplication, identity \(1\), and absorber \(\tau\). It does **not** impose \(1+1=1\). Its blueprint presentation includes the relation identifying the empty sum with \(\tau\).

For your original scalar object,

\qquad e_R=0_R^\bullet,

\qquad
\tau\mapsto\tau,\quad1\mapsto1_R^\bullet.
}
\]

It induces the structural map
\[

\]

Every prime lies over the single prime \(\{\tau\}\) of this base. This is an actual morphism in the blueprint framework, which accommodates pointed monoids and semirings in the same category. citeturn919404academia36

The infinite arithmetic quotient is still
\[
\boxed{

\]

\[

G(\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow{G(j)}&G(\mathbb C)\\
p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\
\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{j}&\mathbb C,
\end{array}
\qquad j:\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb C.
\]

Both \(e\) and \(\tau\) are tracked through this square.

giving

\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\chi_R}
\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{sr}}G(R)
\xrightarrow{a_R}
\mathfrak b_\tau.
}
\]

The first arrow lands at \(P_\tau\). Your original note computes its stalk as
\[
G(R)[e_R^{-1}]\cong\mathbb B,
\]
whereas the stalk at the supported-zero prime is
\[
G(R)_{P_0}\cong G(\operatorname{Frac}R).

Those are the actual localization maps, not interchangeable descriptions of the base. fileciteturn185file0L114-L141

**The construction uses the structural morphism \(a_R\), keeping \(p_R\) attached. It does not replace the arithmetic object by its Boolean localization.**

## 4. Compute the right-adjoint object instead of importing Deligne’s finite-field one
