\frac{f^\dagger(s)h(s)}{g(s)}\,ds,

f^\dagger(s)=\overline{f(1-\bar s)}.

=

m_\rho\,\overline{f(1-\bar\rho)}h(\rho)

\operatorname{Tr}(M_{f^\dagger h}\mid A_Z).

Its split lift preserves the input support label. A zero functional or trace value is the corresponding supported zero; the input’s relation fibre remains available upstream.

Take external products of the actual chart model over the underlying point of \(\mathfrak b_\tau\).

\[

=
\sum_j
(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}|x_k|}
x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes dx_j\otimes\cdots\otimes x_r.
\]

On the joint arithmetic fibre, its top cohomology is
\[
\boxed{
H^r\mathsf A_{\tau,r}(\mathcal T^{\boxtimes r})
\cong Q^{\otimes r}.
}
\]

The numerator is \(\mathscr B^{\otimes r}\). The relations are the sum of the subspaces having \(\Theta V\) in at least one factor. Quotienting those relations gives exactly the displayed tensor product.

The corresponding right-adjoint calculation is
\[
\boxed{
K_{\tau,r}(W)
\simeq
S_{(\eta,\ldots,\eta)}W[r].
}
\]

For an actual spectral residue class at \(\rho\), the induced \(r\)-fold action is \(a^{r\rho}\). Its exact modulus comparison is
\[
\boxed{
\log\frac{|a^{r\rho}|^2}{a^r}
=
r(2\Re\rho-1)\log a.
}
\]

This performs the tensor-amplification operation on the arithmetic quotient over the new base. It does not yet bound the displayed quantity.

## What this changes in the programme

The construction is now
\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
\text{original split-supported theta object over }\mathfrak b_\tau\\
\downarrow\ \mathsf A_\tau\\
\text{arithmetic cohomology }Q
\text{ with all original support faces}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{computed right-adjoint object }K_\tau(\mathcal L_1)\\
\downarrow\\
\text{finite spectral duality, arithmetic trace, and tensor amplification}.
\end{gathered}
}
\]

There is a precise answer to the proposed “exceptions land in \(\tau\)” operation. A structural map of the geometry to \(\mathfrak b_\tau\) retains the cohomology through \(\mathsf A_\tau\). Deleting a finite packet \(A_B\), by contrast, is the specific projection
\[
A_Z[-1]\longrightarrow A_{Z\setminus B}[-1].
\]
Its cone has
\[
H^0=A_B,
\]
and the removed trace is
\[
\sum_{\rho\in B}m_\rho\mathcal Mh(\rho).
\]
Finite Mellin interpolation makes that nonzero for some admissible \(h\) whenever \(B\) is nonempty. Thus deletion has a retained, testable cohomological contribution.

The remaining issue is **a weight or positivity theorem for this new-base arithmetic realization**. The right adjoint calculated here is to algebraic \(R\Gamma\) on the stated chart category; it has not been promoted to an involutive Verdier duality or an extraordinary pullback for an unconstructed proper arithmetic curve. The chart model also does not yet provide all finite-prime geometry merely because it has a structural map to \(\operatorname{Spec}G(\mathbb Z)\).

But this turn has performed the requested change in the object of study: **the base is the absolute \(\tau\)-point, the arithmetic action is characteristic-zero scaling, and the cohomological dual is calculated on that model.** The supplied package contains the proofs, source windows, and 79 finite regression-check records, including the support operations, adjoint complex, reciprocal chart action, tensor signs, and trace contribution of a deleted packet.

## A1694 | node 1fa0ebbc-f569-40c1-b7ac-b523da19a5f0 | assistant | chain 3576

**I constructed a continuous left inverse for the theta map on the full original test-function spaces:**
\[
\boxed{
\Lambda:\mathscr B\longrightarrow V,
\qquad
\Lambda\Theta=\operatorname{id}_V.
}
\]

This gives the programme a **global continuous choice of representatives for its arithmetic cohomology**, rather than representatives constructed separately for each finite spectral packet. It also proves that the original theta image is closed in the specified strong-Schwartz topology.

I published the derivation as **draft PR #10**, stacked on #9: five added files, no existing files modified or deleted, and no merge. fileciteturn223file0L2-L13 fileciteturn223file0L32-L35

[**Read the continuation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Global_Comparison/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Global_Comparison/NOTE.tex) · [**Complete package**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Global_Comparison_2026-09-12.zip) · [**Updated programme state**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Global_Comparison/PROGRAMME_STATE.md)

## 1. The inverse is built from the actual arithmetic map

The base remains \(\mathfrak b_\tau\), with
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow{G(j)}&G(\mathbb C)\\
p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\
\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{j}&\mathbb C.
\end{array}
\]

Retain the same source:
\[
V=
\left\{
\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R):
\phi\text{ even},\
\phi(0)=0,\
\int_{\mathbb R}\phi=0
\right\},
\]
and the same target:
\[
\mathscr B=
\left\{
F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}):
\sup_{x>0}x^b|D^kF(x)|<\infty
\quad\forall b\in\mathbb Z,\ k\ge0
\right\},
\qquad D=-x\partial_x.
\]

The arithmetic map is still
\[
\Theta\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ne0}\phi(nx)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\phi(nx).
\]

### Recover both exterior regions

Define, away from \(x=0\),
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal UF(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)F(n|x|).
}
\]

The factor \(1/2\) is retained because \(\Theta\) sums over both positive and negative integers.

Absolute convergence permits rearrangement by divisors:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal U\Theta\phi(x)
&=\sum_{m,n\ge1}\mu(m)\phi(mnx)\\
&=\sum_{k\ge1}
\left(\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)\right)\phi(kx)
=\phi(x).
\end{aligned}
\]

With
\[
JF(x)=x^{-1}F(1/x),
\qquad
\widehat\phi(\xi)=
\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(x)e^{-2\pi ix\xi}\,dx,
\]
the actual Poisson identity gives a second recovery:
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal U\Theta\phi=\phi,
\qquad
\mathcal UJ\Theta\phi=\widehat\phi
\quad(x\ne0).
}
\]

For arbitrary \(F\), these formulas supply controlled exterior data. Smoothness at the origin is obtained by the following construction, not presumed.

### Solve the position–Fourier reconstruction problem

Choose and retain smooth, compactly supported, even functions \(\alpha,\beta\), with values in \([0,1]\), each equal to \(1\) near zero. On \(L^2(\mathbb R,dx)\), set
\[
A_\alpha=M_\alpha,
\qquad
B_\beta=\mathcal F^{-1}M_\beta\mathcal F,
\qquad
T_{\alpha,\beta}=A_\alpha B_\beta.
\]

I proved
\[
\boxed{\|T_{\alpha,\beta}\|<1.}
\]

The kernel is
\[
\alpha(x)\check\beta(x-y),
\]
so \(T_{\alpha,\beta}\) is Hilbert–Schmidt and compact. If its norm were \(1\), compactness would supply a unit vector attaining it. Equality in
\[
\|A_\alpha B_\beta f\|
\le\|B_\beta f\|
\le\|f\|
\]
would force \(f\) to have compact support and \(\widehat f\) to have compact support. The latter makes \(f\) the restriction of an entire function; the former makes it vanish on a real interval. Hence \(f=0\), a contradiction.

Thus the exact inverse exists:
\[
(1-T_{\alpha,\beta})^{-1}
=\sum_{k\ge0}T_{\alpha,\beta}^{\,k},
\qquad
\left\|(1-T_{\alpha,\beta})^{-1}\right\|
\le\frac1{1-\|T_{\alpha,\beta}\|}.
\]

The denominator remains in every estimate. There is no claimed uniform gap as the cutoffs vary.

Now define
\[
Y_{\alpha,\beta}F
=
(1-\alpha)\mathcal UF
+
\alpha\mathcal F^{-1}\bigl((1-\beta)\mathcal UJF\bigr),
\]
and
\[
\Phi_{\alpha,\beta}F
=
(1-T_{\alpha,\beta})^{-1}Y_{\alpha,\beta}F.
\]

The exterior factors vanish near zero and satisfy Schwartz estimates. Moreover, \(T_{\alpha,\beta}\) maps \(L^2\) continuously into Schwartz functions. Therefore
\[
\Phi F=YF+T\Phi F
\]
proves that \(\Phi F\) is Schwartz, with explicit seminorm bounds.

On an actual theta input,
\[
Y_{\alpha,\beta}\Theta\phi
=

\]

The orbit construction gives, exactly,
\[
G_T=
\begin{pmatrix}
T&T^2/2\\
T^2/2&T+T^3/3
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
W_T=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&T\\
T&T^2
\end{pmatrix}.

Their generalized eigenvalues are
\[

The control error therefore tends to zero, **while the nilpotent operator stays nonzero**.

\frac{M_{i+j}(2\Re\rho-1,T)}{i!\,j!}
(N^*)^iGN^j,
}
\]
where
\[
M_k(\delta,T)=\int_0^T e^{\delta t}t^k\,dt.
\]

All powers of \(N\), all metric entries, and the parameter \(\delta\) remain.

As a check against manufacturing purity, the separate calibration

This is the useful distinction made by an actual map: the orbit-Gram construction can reduce a metric error caused by a retained nilpotent chain, but it does not project a genuine spectral-weight discrepancy away.

=
\langle F,H\rangle.

Degree and orthogonality then determine the full recurrence:
\[
\boxed{
Du_0=u_1+\frac12u_0,
}
\]
\[

Du_n
=
u_{n+1}+\frac12u_n
-\frac{\mathfrak h_n}{\mathfrak h_{n-1}}u_{n-1}.
}
\]

The coefficient \(1/2\) follows from that integration-by-parts identity with the original measure \(dx\). The generator remains \(D=-x\partial_x\).

For the same finite arithmetic object, put

=
\mathfrak h_{n+1}
\left(r_{n+1}^*r_n+r_n^*r_{n+1}\right).

while

u_{n+1}^*R_n=\mathfrak h_{n+1}r_{n+1}.

Substitution gives the formula.

=
\mathfrak h_{n+1}r_{n+1}^*r_{n+1}.

\mathsf c_n&\mathsf a_n\\
\mathsf b_n&\overline{\mathsf c_n}

\[

=
\mathfrak h_{n+1}
\left(
|\Re\mathsf c_n|
+
\sqrt{
\mathsf a_n\mathsf b_n-(\Im\mathsf c_n)^2

\[

W_n^{\mathrm D}
=
-S_Z^*G_n^{-1}W_nG_n^{-1}S_Z.

The norm sequence \(\mathfrak h_n\) comes from the original theta function, independently of which finite spectral packet is selected.

\[

\qquad
p_{j+1}(z)=2z\bigl(p_j(z)-p_j'(z)\bigr),

the source functions are
\[

p_j(\pi m^2x^2)e^{-\pi m^2x^2}.

Using the exact inversion
\[
\mathcal JF(x)=x^{-1}F(1/x),
\]
I moved the integral over \((0,1)\) to \((1,\infty)\). This produces an absolutely convergent double-sum formula for every Gram entry, with its monomial integrals expressed through
\[
\int_1^\infty x^{2r+2s}e^{-cx^2}\,dx
=
\frac{\Gamma(r+s+\tfrac12,c)}
{2c^{r+s+1/2}}.
\]

The note proves an explicit bound for truncating both integer sums. It does not interchange an uncut double sum with an integral down to zero.

The first four unscaled norm squares evaluate approximately to
\[

1.27900724784648514,\quad
13.0555493025705584,\quad
250.008976819049915,\quad
6694.66668552562751.
}
\]

With integer cutoff \(8\), the largest proved **integer-tail bound** for the corresponding \(4\times4\) raw Gram matrix is approximately
\[
1.745\times10^{-44}.
\]

The 80- and 100-digit evaluations agreed in the printed forty-digit norm values. These are numerical evaluations, **not validated-rounding certificates**; the tail bound controls omitted integer terms, not floating-point rounding or subsequent Gram inversion. ## 3. The actual arithmetic metric is an inverse full-jet moment matrix

The Hilbert observation is the retained
\[

This gives the actual positive measure

=
\left|

\right|^2\frac{dt}{2\pi}.

The entire function \(g/h\) supplies the values at any selected zero on this integration line.

In the fixed polynomial basis \(1,t,\ldots,t^N\), define
\[

=
\int_{\mathbb R}
\overline{(\tfrac12+it)^i}
(\tfrac12+it)^j\,d\nu_h(t).
\]
This matrix is positive definite. A polynomial of zero norm would vanish almost everywhere on the integration line and hence identically.

Let \(J_{h,N}\) be the matrix of the **full** map \(\mathcal J_{h,N}\). It includes the arithmetic unit \(\upsilon_h\), not merely evaluation at the selected points.

\[
\mathcal C_{h,N}
=
J_{h,N}M_{h,N}^{-1}J_{h,N}^*,

\[

=
M_{h,N}^{-1}J_{h,N}^*

\[

J_hR_{h,n}=1,\qquad
G_{h,n}=R_{h,n}^*R_{h,n}
=
\mathcal C_{h,n+d}^{-1}.
}
\]

Here \(P_n\) is the orthogonal projection onto the original \(L_n\), and \(s_h\) is the earlier arithmetic section.

### Proof of the minimum and the formula

Every polynomial with the required jet \(u\) is
\[
C_{h,N}u+z,\qquad J_{h,N}z=0.
\]
The cross term vanishes because
\[
z^*M_{h,N}C_{h,N}u
=
z^*J_{h,N}^*\mathcal C_{h,N}^{-1}u=0.
\]
Therefore its squared norm is exactly
\[
u^*\mathcal C_{h,N}^{-1}u+z^*M_{h,N}z.
\]

This proves the unique minimum. The preceding exact sequence identifies every allowed correction with an element of \(L_n\), so the minimizer is precisely \((1-P_n)s_h\).

**The full arithmetic Gram matrix can therefore be calculated without subtracting two nearly equal Gram matrices.** Every derivative at a multiple zero and every coefficient of \(g/h\) remains in the matrix \(J_{h,N}\).

For one simple zero, the formula specializes to

## 6. A global density calculation identifies the conditioning that must be retained

I proved that the **single original derivative family**

\[

\le
C(1+|t|)^{11/2}e^{-\pi|t|/2}

for sufficiently large \(|t|\). The gamma estimate used is DLMF 5.11.9. citeturn148073view0

This is the main new construction for advancing the Deligne-style control.

Its primitive receives the coefficient \((-1)^{j-1}\); the tensor differential supplies the other \((-1)^{j-1}\). The resulting boundary is \(+h(t_j)P_j\). Both signs are retained.

In the total-degree monomial basis,
\[

=

### One next total-degree layer contains the complete derivative defect

Put
\[

=
\mathcal T_h^{(k)}\mathcal I_{k,M},

and define the actual orthogonal relation layer
\[

=
(1-P_{\mathcal B_{k,M}})\mathcal B_{k,M+1}.
}

\[

=
\binom{M+k}{k-1}.
}
\]

=
D^{(k)}R_{k,M}-R_{k,M}A_h^{(k)}
\in\mathcal B_{k,M+1}.

Now take the two maps into that **same** relation layer:
\[

Y_{k,M}=P_{\mathcal E_{k,M}}R_{k,M},
}
\]
\[

=
(1-P_{\mathcal B_{k,M}})B_{k,M}.
}
\]

Integration by parts gives
\[

\]
Substituting the displayed defect and using orthogonality proves
\[

=
(A_h^{(k)})^*G_{k,M}
+
G_{k,M}A_h^{(k)}
-kG_{k,M}
=
-(Y_{k,M}^*C_{k,M}+C_{k,M}^*Y_{k,M}).

\[
\operatorname{rank}W_{k,M}
\le
2\binom{M+k}{k-1}.

\[

\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal E_{k,M},
\qquad
[z]\longmapsto(1-P_{\mathcal B_{k,M}})z.

## 4. A highest-degree identity gives the relative control

The arithmetic polynomial recurrence is
\[
\boxed{
tp_n=p_{n+1}+b_np_n-a_np_{n-1},
\qquad
a_n=\frac{\omega_n}{\omega_{n-1}},
\qquad
\Re b_n=\frac12.
}
\]
Here \(a_0=0\). The potentially nonzero \(\Im b_n\) is retained.

To derive it, multiplication by \(t\) on the integration line has adjoint multiplication by \(1-t\). Pairing against the earlier polynomials gives the negative coefficient \(-\omega_n/\omega_{n-1}\); the diagonal coefficient is
\[
b_n=
\frac{\int(\tfrac12+iy)|p_n(\tfrac12+iy)|^2\,d\nu_h(y)}
{\omega_n}.
\]
The recurrence and the cancellation below are instances of the orthogonal-polynomial mechanism behind Christoffel–Darboux, here carried through the full arithmetic jet map. citeturn815161search0

For each \(|\beta|=M+1\), define
\[

=
\sum_{j:\beta_j>0}
a_{\beta_j}z_{\beta-e_j},
\qquad
E_+=[w_\beta]_{|\beta|=M+1}.
\]
The matrix \(E_+:\mathbb C^r\to E^{\otimes k}\) is a boundary-coordinate map; it is not the scalar \(e\).

Let
\[

\qquad A=M_t.
\]

The calculated identity is
\[

\mathcal Z_M
:=
A_k\mathcal C_M+\mathcal C_MA_k^*-k\mathcal C_M
=
F\Omega^{-1}E_+^*
+
E_+\Omega^{-1}F^*.
}
\]

\[

=
\frac{\omega_{\alpha+e_j}}{\omega_\alpha}.
\]
The diagonal terms contribute exactly \(k\mathcal C_M\). Only adjacent pairs crossing the highest-degree boundary remain, giving the displayed formula.

The original derivative boundary is connected by
\[

\]

=
(1-P_{\mathcal B_M})B_M
=
b_M\Omega^{-1}E_+^*G_M.
}
\]

\[

&=A_k^*G_M+G_MA_k-kG_M\\
&=G_M\mathcal Z_MG_M\\
&=-\left(Y_M^*C_M^{\mathrm{rel}}

\end{aligned}

\]

This recovers the preceding boundary-control equation through the **same \(Y_M,C_M^{\mathrm{rel}}\)**, including its minus sign.

2\sqrt{\Gamma_{k,M}\lambda_{k,M}}\,G_M.

\preceq
\Gamma_{k,M}\mathcal C_M.

Cauchy–Schwarz in the specified \(\Omega^{-1}\) pairing then bounds the two cross terms.

### The relations still have their original theta primitives

For a relation written as \(H_0A_0+\Delta H_1A_1\), the exact identity is
\[
\boxed{
H_0A_0+\Delta H_1A_1
=
h(s_1)\frac{A_0+rA_1}{2}
+
h(s_2)\frac{A_0-rA_1}{2}.
}
\]

Its two cochain primitives are
\[
\frac{A_0+rA_1}{2}(D_1,D_2)
(\phi_*\otimes F_h),
\]
\[
-\frac{A_0-rA_1}{2}(D_1,D_2)
(F_h\otimes\phi_*).
\]

The second primitive’s minus sign meets the second tensor-differential minus sign. Both terms therefore produce the positive relation displayed above.

The unit \(\upsilon_h\otimes\upsilon_h\) descends through \(\Phi\) and stays in the full jet map. At every degree, the induced quotient is still the original internal quotient. A relation becomes the zero of its receiving support fibre; different labels are not identified by that quotient. fileciteturn256file4L42-L58

## 4. Push the arithmetic norm to a matrix weight

The source density is unchanged:
\[
w_h(t)=
\left|
\frac{g(\tfrac12+it)}{h(\tfrac12+it)}
\right|^2\frac1{2\pi}.
\]

Use
\[
u=t_1+t_2,\qquad v=t_1-t_2.
\]
Then
\[
t_1=\frac{u+v}{2},\qquad
t_2=\frac{u-v}{2},\qquad
dt_1dt_2=\frac12\,du\,dv.
\]

On the original integration lines,
\[
S=1+iu,\qquad r=iv,\qquad \Delta=-v^2.
\]

Write a symmetric numerator of degree at most \(M\) as
\[
P(S,\Delta)=
\sum_{a=0}^{\lfloor M/2\rfloor}\Delta^a f_a(S),
\qquad
\deg f_a\le M-2a.
\]

Define the matrix-valued density
\[
\boxed{
\mathsf W_{ac}(u)
=
\frac{(-1)^{a+c}}2
\int_{\mathbb R}
v^{2(a+c)}
w_h\!\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)
w_h\!\left(\frac{u-v}{2}\right)\,dv.
}
\]

Substitution into the original norm proves
\[
\boxed{
\|\mathcal T_h^{(2)}\Phi P\|^2
=
\int_{\mathbb R}
f(1+iu)^*
\mathsf W(u)
f(1+iu)\,du.
}
\]

The proof retains the Jacobian \(1/2\), every factor \(1/(2\pi)\) inside \(w_h\), and the signs from \(\Delta=-v^2\).

Every finite matrix \(\mathsf W(u)\) is positive definite: its quadratic form integrates the squared modulus of a nonzero polynomial in \(-v^2\) against a density positive almost everywhere. The prior exponential-moment estimates supply convergence.

Its first entry is the scalar convolution
\[
\mathsf W_{00}(u)=(w_h*w_h)(u).
\]
The remaining entries carry the relative-coordinate moments. The full pushforward retains those entries.

### Separate the base contribution through an actual isometry

Write
\[
\mathsf W(u)=
\begin{pmatrix}
m_0(u)&b(u)\\
b(u)^*&C(u)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The explicit triangular map is
\[
\boxed{
(f_0,f_{\mathrm{rel}})
\longmapsto
\left(f_0+m_0^{-1}bf_{\mathrm{rel}},\,f_{\mathrm{rel}}\right),
}
\]
with inverse
\[
(a,z)\longmapsto(a-m_0^{-1}bz,z).
\]

It transforms the norm into the direct sum weighted by
\[
\boxed{
m_0(u),
\qquad
C(u)-b(u)^*m_0(u)^{-1}b(u).
}
\]

The exact image of the original degree-constrained polynomial family remains part of this construction. The ratio \(m_0^{-1}b\) need not be polynomial, so its target is not enlarged to arbitrary independently chosen functions.

This gives a definite base/relative decomposition on which to study the estimate, without discarding the relative covariance.

### The construction extends to every tensor degree

For \(k\) factors, retain
\[
S=\sum_{i=1}^ks_i,\qquad
x_i=s_i\quad(i<k),\qquad
s_k=S-\sum_{i<k}x_i.
\]

The real-coordinate Jacobian is one. Writing
\[
P=\sum_\alpha x^\alpha f_\alpha(S),
\qquad
\deg f_\alpha\le M-|\alpha|,
\]
produces the matrix density
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W_{\alpha\beta}(u)
={}&
\int_{\mathbb R^{k-1}}
\overline{\prod_{i<k}(\tfrac12+it_i)^{\alpha_i}}
\prod_{i<k}(\tfrac12+it_i)^{\beta_i}\\
&\qquad\cdot
\prod_{i<k}w_h(t_i)\,
w_h\!\left(u-\sum_{i<k}t_i\right)
\,d^{k-1}t .
\end{aligned}
}
\]

The remaining variable is exactly
\[
S=\frac{k}{2}+iu.
\]
All transverse polynomial degrees and their matrix pairings remain.

## 5. The canonical control calculation commutes with this descent

Let \(T\) be the explicit change of source polynomial coordinates and \(U\) the explicit change of quotient coordinates. The complete matrix comparison is
\[
\boxed{
M'=T^*MT,\qquad
J'=U^{-1}JT.
}
\]

Consequently,
\[
\boxed{
K'=U^{-1}K(U^{-1})^*,\qquad
G'=U^*GU,
}
\]
\[
\boxed{
A'=U^{-1}AU,\qquad
W'=U^*WU,\qquad
R'=RU.
}
\]

These follow by substitution into
\[
K=JM^{-1}J^*,\qquad
G=K^{-1},
\qquad
W=A^*G+GA-kG.
\]

Thus the matrix-weight realization calculates the **same** canonical representatives, arithmetic jets, and relative control. Its source isometry also carries the next relation layer and the two maps \(Y,C_{\mathrm{rel}}\) used in
\[
W=-(Y^*C_{\mathrm{rel}}+C_{\mathrm{rel}}^*Y).
\]

This is where the other session’s inverse-kernel estimate enters unchanged:
\[
-\epsilon G\preceq W\preceq\epsilon G
\iff
-\epsilon K\preceq AK+KA^*-kK\preceq\epsilon K.
\]
Its explicit comparison is \(u=K\lambda\), retaining both Rayleigh quotients and the representative map. fileciteturn256file0L27-L69

The new operation has not manufactured a smaller constant. It has turned the same estimate into a one-variable matrix-weight problem with its relative fibre explicitly available.

## 6. Compute the dual and trace of the sum-line object

For the actual finite ordered or symmetric image \(E\), let \(A\) be its sum operator and put \(\mathcal R=\mathbb C[S]\).

There is an explicit free resolution:
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow\mathcal R\otimes E
\xrightarrow{SI-A}
\mathcal R\otimes E
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_A}
E
\longrightarrow0,
}
\]
where
\[
\operatorname{ev}_A(P\otimes v)=P(A)v.
\]

Injectivity follows by inspecting the highest polynomial coefficient. Exactness follows from
\[
\boxed{
S^jv-A^jv
=
(SI-A)
\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}S^{j-1-i}A^iv.
}
\]

Let
\[
E^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C),
\qquad
A^\vee\lambda=\lambda\circ A.
\]

Dualizing the displayed resolution gives
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal R}(E,\mathcal R\,dS)
\simeq
[\mathcal R\otimes E^\vee\,dS
\xrightarrow{SI-A^\vee}
\mathcal R\otimes E^\vee\,dS]
\]
in degrees \(0,1\), and
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal R}(E,\mathcal R\,dS)
\cong E^\vee.
}
\]

The map is
\[
\left[\sum_jS^j\lambda_j\,dS\right]
\longmapsto
\sum_j(A^\vee)^j\lambda_j,
\]
with inverse the constant class.

The corresponding right adjoint is the actual module functor
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C[S]}(B_k,-),
\]
where \(B_k\) is the finite algebra being pushed forward. This uses the precise restriction-of-scalars category underlying the finite-morphism adjoint. citeturn153367view1

For the cochain shift \(C[b]^i=C^{i+b}\), the arithmetic degree is retained:
\[
\boxed{
R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal R}
(E[-k],\mathcal R\,dS[1])
\simeq E^\vee[k].
}
\]

### Its pairing retains the whole resolvent

The duality above is represented by
\[
\boxed{
\langle v,[P(S)dS]\rangle
=
\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Spec}A}
\operatorname{Res}_{S=\lambda}
P(S)\bigl((SI-A)^{-1}v\bigr)\,dS.
}
\]

Expansion at infinity gives exactly
\[
\sum_j\lambda_j(A^jv),
\]
which proves the formula and its nondegeneracy.

For a block \(A=\lambda I+N\), retain
\[
\boxed{
(SI-A)^{-1}
=
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
\frac{N^j}{(S-\lambda)^{j+1}},
\qquad N^\ell=0.
}
\]

The scalar trace is the further observation
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}(\psi(A))
=
\sum_\lambda
\operatorname{Res}_{S=\lambda}
\psi(S)\frac{\chi_A'(S)}{\chi_A(S)}\,dS,
\qquad
\chi_A(S)=\det(SI-A).
}
\]

For \(\psi(S)=a^S\), this is the same finite scaling trace, with cohomological sign \((-1)^k\). The finite polynomial \(\chi_A\) is connected to the action by the displayed determinant map; it does not replace the source function \(g=2\xi\).

## 7. All higher-order fibres can be calculated

For an ordered tuple of roots with orders \(m_i\), the local fibre is
\[
L=
\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_k]/(z_1^{m_1},\ldots,z_k^{m_k}),
\]
with
\[
A=\rho_\Sigma I+N,
\qquad
\rho_\Sigma=\sum_i\rho_i,
\qquad
N=M_{z_1+\cdots+z_k}.
\]

Put
\[
D_0=\sum_i(m_i-1),
\]
and define \(c_r\) by
\[
\prod_i(1+t+\cdots+t^{m_i-1})
=
\sum_rc_rt^r,
\qquad c_{-1}=0.
\]

The complete \(\mathbb C[S]\)-module pushforward is
\[
\boxed{
\pi_*L
\cong
\bigoplus_{r=0}^{\lfloor D_0/2\rfloor}
\left(
\frac{\mathbb C[S]}
{(S-\rho_\Sigma)^{D_0-2r+1}}
\right)^{\oplus(c_r-c_{r-1})}.
}
\]

The proof constructs the maps. On each monomial factor define
\[
F_i z_i^j=j(m_i-j)z_i^{j-1},
\qquad
H_i z_i^j=(2j-(m_i-1))z_i^j.
\]
Their sums satisfy
\[
[N,F]=H,\qquad [H,N]=2N,\qquad [H,F]=-2F.
\]

For a degree-\(r\) primitive \(p\), \(Fp=0\), the explicit ladder map is
\[
\boxed{
[P(S)]\longmapsto P(\rho_\Sigma+N)p.
}
\]
Its length is \(D_0-2r+1\). The ladder identity
\[
FN^jp=j(D_0-2r-j+1)N^{j-1}p
\]
and the graded dimensions give the multiplicities in the decomposition.

The proof uses an explicitly declared auxiliary diagonal Gram to construct invariant complements. Its connection to the actual arithmetic Gram is the operator
\[
G_{\mathrm{arith}}^{-1}G_0.
\]
After choosing ladder coordinates \(U\), the arithmetic metric is still
\[
U^*G_{\mathrm{arith}}U,
\]
with all cross-ladder entries retained. The algebraic decomposition supplies no positivity estimate by changing that metric.

### A concrete higher-jet example

For an order-three local factor taken twice, its symmetric fibre has dimension six. With
\[
X=z_1+z_2,
\]
it has the two ladders
\[
1,\ X,\ X^2,\ X^3,\ X^4,
\]
and
\[
p=z_1^2-z_1z_2+z_2^2,\qquad Xp=0.
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{
\pi_*L^{S_2}
\cong
\mathbb C[S]/(S-2\rho)^5
\oplus
\mathbb C[S]/(S-2\rho).
}
\]

This is a local algebra calculation, not a claim that \(\xi\) has a triple zero.

The general symmetric calculation retains separate occupation idempotents even when two different collections of roots have the same sum. Their fibres do not become one scalar evaluation merely because \(S\) has the same value.

The original split lift of each ladder map fixes \(\tau\). Under an explicitly chosen shorter-ladder quotient, a top jet becomes the supported zero; the full pushforward keeps that jet before the quotient.

The new object is

\begin{gathered}
\text{original arithmetic tensor complex over }\mathfrak b_\tau\\
\downarrow\\

\downarrow\\

\downarrow\\

This performs a concrete product-to-one-parameter step for the programme. The supplied Deligne argument likewise follows tensoring with a geometric pushforward and an additional estimate; the tensor operation alone does not improve the weight bound. fileciteturn256file7L238-L266

p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\

Keep
\[
C_+=[V\xrightarrow{\Theta}\mathscr B],
\qquad
Q=\mathscr B/\Theta V,
\qquad
D=-x\partial_x,

and the actual Mellin identity
\[

g=2\xi,

h(s)=\prod_{\rho\in Z}(s-\rho)^{m_\rho},
\qquad
v_h=\frac gh,
\qquad

## 2. The sum pushforward has a calculated \(1/k\) estimate, with its mass retained

Define the actual spectral amplitude and its density:
\[
a_h(t)=\frac{v_h(\tfrac12+it)}{\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
w_h(t)=|a_h(t)|^2,
\]
\[
\boxed{
\mu_h=\int_{\mathbb R}w_h(t)\,dt
=
\|F_h\|_{L^2((0,\infty),dx)}^2.
}
\]

The factor \(\sqrt{2\pi}\) is the retained Mellin–Fourier Plancherel factor. The mass \(\mu_h\) is not assigned the value one.

The original reflection gives
\[
g^\dagger=g,
\qquad
h^\dagger=(-1)^{\deg h}h,
\qquad
v_h^\dagger=(-1)^{\deg h}v_h.
\]
On the integration line, this means
\[
\overline{a_h(t)}=(-1)^{\deg h}a_h(t).
\]

Consequently, \(a_h\) and \(a_h'\) have the same fixed real or imaginary phase. This proves
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal I_h
:=
\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{|w_h'(t)|^2}{w_h(t)}\,dt
=
4\int_{\mathbb R}|a_h'(t)|^2\,dt
=
4\int_0^\infty(\log x)^2|F_h(x)|^2\,dx.
}
\]

The integral is finite because \(F_h\) belongs to the specified test space. At a zero of \(a_h\), the calculation uses the smooth amplitude and its derivative; it does not require a bounded logarithmic derivative.

### Keep the sum and every relative direction

For \(k\ge2\), use
\[
u=\sum_{i=1}^kt_i,
\qquad
y_i=t_i-\frac uk\quad(i<k),
\qquad
y_k=-\sum_{i<k}y_i.
\]

The inverse is
\[
t_i=\frac uk+y_i,
\]
and the real Jacobian has absolute value one. For two factors, the earlier coordinate is \(v=2y_1\), recovering its Jacobian \(1/2\).

Define
\[
\Psi_k(u,\mathbf y)
=
\prod_{i=1}^ka_h(u/k+y_i).
\]

Its fibre is the actual Hilbert space
\[
\mathscr H_u=L^2(\mathbb R^{k-1},d\mathbf y),
\]
and
\[
m_k(u)
=
\|\Psi_k(u,\cdot)\|_{\mathscr H_u}^2
=
w_h^{*k}(u).
\]
In particular,
\[
\boxed{\int_{\mathbb R}m_k(u)\,du=\mu_h^k.}
\]

The line inclusion and its orthogonal projection are
\[
j_{0,u}:\mathbb C\to\mathscr H_u,
\qquad
c\mapsto c\Psi_k,
\]
\[
\Pi_{0,u}Z
=
\Psi_k\frac{\langle\Psi_k,Z\rangle}{m_k(u)}.
\]

Now retain the part of the derivative outside that line:
\[
\boxed{
n_k(u)
=
(1-\Pi_{0,u})\partial_u\Psi_k
=
\partial_u\Psi_k-\frac{m_k'}{2m_k}\Psi_k.
}
\]

### The exact estimate

Let
\[
\mathcal I_{h,k}
=
\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{|m_k'(u)|^2}{m_k(u)}\,du.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal I_{h,k}
+
4\int_{\mathbb R}\|n_k(u)\|_{\mathscr H_u}^2\,du
=
\frac{\mu_h^{\,k-1}}{k}\mathcal I_h.
}
\]

**Proof.** Differentiation at fixed relative coordinates gives
\[
\partial_u\Psi_k
=
\frac1k
\sum_{i=1}^k
a_h'(t_i)\prod_{j\ne i}a_h(t_j).
\]

Upon integrating its squared modulus, the \(k\) diagonal terms each contribute
\[
\mu_h^{k-1}\|a_h'\|^2.
\]

Every distinct-index cross term contains
\[
\left|\int_{\mathbb R}\overline{a_h}a_h'\,dt\right|^2=0,
\]
because that integral is \(\tfrac12\int w_h'=0\). Therefore
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\|\partial_u\Psi_k\|^2\,du
=
\frac{\mu_h^{k-1}}{4k}\mathcal I_h.
\]

The orthogonal decomposition defining \(n_k\) gives
\[
\|\partial_u\Psi_k\|^2
=
\frac{|m_k'|^2}{4m_k}
+
\|n_k\|^2.
\]
Integrate and multiply by four.

This applies the established projection mechanism behind Fisher-information convolution inequalities, but retains the actual arithmetic amplitude, its mass, and the complete relative residual. It does not assume log-concavity or a Gaussian approximation. citeturn576038view0

**The relative contribution is a calculated nonnegative term, not a discarded direction.** The pair
\[
\bigl(\Pi_{0,u}\partial_u\Psi_k,\ n_k\bigr)
\]
recovers the full derivative by addition.

## 3. The full relative matrix now has an explicit connection

The scalar calculation is only the constant relative column. I also carried the derivative through the entire finite relative polynomial family.

Write
\[
S=\sum_i s_i,
\qquad
z_i=s_i-S/k.
\]
Choose the specified relative polynomials \(\theta_\alpha(\mathbf z)\), independent of \(S\), and retain the original filtered numerator
\[
P(\mathbf s)=\sum_\alpha\theta_\alpha(\mathbf z)f_\alpha(S),
\qquad
\deg f_\alpha\le M-\deg\theta_\alpha.
\]

Define
\[
j_u:\mathbb C^r\longrightarrow\mathscr H_u,
\qquad
j_uc
=
\Psi_k(u,\mathbf y)
\sum_\alpha\theta_\alpha(i\mathbf y)c_\alpha.
\]

The three actual matrix integrals are
\[
\boxed{
\mathsf W=j_u^*j_u,
\qquad
\mathsf B=j_u^*j_u',
\qquad
\mathsf T=(j_u')^*j_u'.
}
\]

The full matrix \(\mathsf W\) is positive definite. Fixed arithmetic phase gives
\[
\mathsf B=\frac12\mathsf W'.
\]

Set
\[
\Pi_u=j_u\mathsf W^{-1}j_u^*,
\qquad
\Gamma_u=\mathsf W^{-1}\mathsf B,
\qquad
N_u=(1-\Pi_u)j_u'.
\]

The exact differentiated map is
\[
\boxed{
\partial_u(j_uc)
=
j_u(c'+\Gamma_uc)+N_uc.
}
\]

Its two components are orthogonal:
\[
j_u^*N_u=0.
\]
The connection is metric-compatible:
\[
\boxed{
\Gamma_u^*\mathsf W+\mathsf W\Gamma_u=\mathsf W'.
}
\]

The entire normal contribution is
\[
\boxed{
N_u^*N_u
=
\mathsf T-\mathsf B^*\mathsf W^{-1}\mathsf B
=
\mathsf T-\frac14\mathsf W'\mathsf W^{-1}\mathsf W'
\succeq0.
}
\]

No commutation of \(\mathsf W\) with \(\mathsf W'\) is assumed. Direct substitution therefore gives
\[
\boxed{
\|\partial_u(j_uc)\|^2
=
(c'+\Gamma_uc)^*\mathsf W(c'+\Gamma_uc)
+
c^*N_u^*N_uc.
}
\]

This is the full matrix version of the scalar decomposition. Every relative coefficient remains.

### Changing the relative frame carries an additional derivative term

For an explicitly specified invertible matrix \(C(u)\), let \(j_u^C=j_uC(u)\). The transformed maps are
\[
\boxed{
\mathsf W^C=C^*\mathsf WC,
\qquad
\Gamma^C=C^{-1}\Gamma C+C^{-1}C',
\qquad
N^C=NC.
}
\]

That \(C^{-1}C'\) term is now present when using the preceding pointwise triangular square-completion map. Multiplication by \(S\) still intertwines through the original coordinate change; differentiation carries the displayed additional term.

The exact image of the original degree-constrained coefficient functions is retained. It is not replaced by all measurable sections of the resulting bundle.

## 4. This derivative is connected to the original scaling operator by a specified map

It satisfies

Thus the new estimate concerns a definite conjugate observable of the original generator. The generator itself remains \(D^{(k)}\), and its spectral coordinate remains \(S=k/2+iu\).

Here \(\mathscr G_M\) is the **image of the original filtered source under \(\mathscr D_M\)**. This is the domain on which the arithmetic jet is defined. The two derivative pieces are retained together before that observation.

The source identity
\[

So a theta relation that becomes a supported zero in \(Q\) has a derivative whose finite arithmetic observation can remain nonzero.

**This does not differentiate \(e\) into a nonzero number. It differentiates the retained source relation before the quotient sends it to \(e\).** The necessary larger domain is now explicit.

### Construct that domain from the same relation ideal

Put
\[

\qquad

\[

The conormal module has the actual coordinate map

Monic division proves the isomorphism: \(\mathcal P\) is free over

The derivative at fixed relative coordinates is

\partial_S^{\mathrm{rel}}
=
\frac1k\sum_i\partial_{s_i}.

Because \(\partial_S^{\mathrm{rel}}(I^2)\subseteq I\), it induces
\[
\boxed{

\qquad
[P]_{I^2}\longmapsto
[\partial_S^{\mathrm{rel}}P]_I.

Retain

## 1. An actual cohomological submodule for the sum-density estimate

Keep the original base and coefficient square:
\[

p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\

The arithmetic quotient still has its infinite target. Every displayed scalar map carries the supported scalar \(e\) and external absence \(\tau\) separately before applying \(p\).

\[

\qquad

\qquad

\qquad

\qquad

\qquad

The operator remains the **sum**, not the average.

### Compute its cyclic arithmetic image

For each possible sum
\[
\lambda=\rho_1+\cdots+\rho_k,
\]
define
\[
\ell_\lambda
=
\max_{\rho_1+\cdots+\rho_k=\lambda}
\left(1+\sum_{i=1}^k(m_{\rho_i}-1)\right).
\]
Equal sums are grouped by their exact equality; different occupations remain present in \(B_k\).

Set
\[
\boxed{
\chi_{h,k}(S)
=
\prod_{\lambda}(S-\lambda)^{\ell_\lambda},
\qquad
C_{h,k}=\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_{h,k}).
}
\]

There are two specified maps:
\[
\alpha_{h,k}:C_{h,k}\hookrightarrow B_k^{S_k},
\qquad
[P]\longmapsto P(A_k)1,
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\eta_{h,k}=M_{U_k}\alpha_{h,k},
\qquad
[P]\longmapsto U_kP(A_k)1.
}
\]

The first is an injective unital algebra map. The second is an injective \(\mathbb C[S]\)-module map carrying the actual arithmetic unit. Its intervening map \(M_{U_k}\) has inverse \(M_{U_k^{-1}}\); it has not been declared a unital algebra homomorphism.

**Proof of injectivity and the exponent formula.** At an ordered root tuple, the local algebra is
\[
L_{\boldsymbol\rho}
=
\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_k]/
(z_1^{m_{\rho_1}},\ldots,z_k^{m_{\rho_k}}),
\]
and
\[
A_k=\lambda I+N,
\qquad N=M_{z_1+\cdots+z_k}.
\]

Its largest surviving total degree is
\[
d_{\boldsymbol\rho}=\sum_i(m_{\rho_i}-1).
\]
The corresponding term of \(N^{d_{\boldsymbol\rho}}1\) has coefficient
\[
\frac{d_{\boldsymbol\rho}!}{\prod_i(m_{\rho_i}-1)!}\ne0.
\]
The next power vanishes. Taking the maximum over tuples having the same sum gives precisely \(\ell_\lambda\).

The vector \(1\) is permutation-invariant and already has this annihilator. Thus restriction to \(B_k^{S_k}\) preserves the minimal polynomial. Multiplication by the retained unit preserves injectivity.

In particular,
\[
\boxed{k\rho\in\operatorname{Spec}(A_k|_{\eta C_{h,k}})
\quad\text{for every }\rho\in Z.}
\]

So the new submodule contains an actual nonzero eigenvector at every exponent required by the amplification argument.

## 2. The complementary arithmetic information has an explicit retraction and trace

The comparison is
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow C_{h,k}
\xrightarrow{\eta_{h,k}}
B_k^{S_k}
\longrightarrow T_{h,k}
\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

This is a sequence of \(\mathbb C[S]\)-modules. Its quotient is lifted using your original internal quotient, which sends a relation to the zero of its own support fibre. Its universal property is already supplied by the formalization work. fileciteturn280file1L53-L71

I also constructed an equivariant retraction rather than leaving the complement abstract.

On the generalized \(\lambda\)-space, let
\[
N_\lambda=A_k-\lambda I,\qquad
w_\lambda=e_\lambda(A_k)U_k1,\qquad
\ell=\ell_\lambda.
\]
Choose the specified top-monomial coefficient functional \(\vartheta_\lambda\) from a root tuple attaining \(\ell\). Its coefficient on \(N_\lambda^{\ell-1}w_\lambda\) is nonzero.

Define
\[
\pi_\lambda^0(v)
=
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
\vartheta_\lambda(N_\lambda^{\ell-1-j}v)X^j

\[

\]
The constant coefficient of \(p_\lambda\) is nonzero, so its inverse modulo \(X^\ell\) exists. Set
\[

}
\]

Direct multiplication gives
\[
\pi_\lambda N_\lambda=X\pi_\lambda,
\qquad
\pi_\lambda(w_\lambda)=1.
\]
Combining the sum blocks produces
\[

\qquad
\boxed{\pi\eta_{h,k}=1.}

The two inverse coordinate maps are
\[
(c,t)\longmapsto\eta_{h,k}c+t,
\]
\[
v\longmapsto\bigl(\pi v,\ v-\eta_{h,k}\pi v\bigr).
\]

The second component retains the remaining nilpotent blocks. This splitting is not asserted orthogonal: the arithmetic metric retains its cross terms under these coordinates.

For an occupation vector \(\mathbf n=(n_\rho)\), \(\sum n_\rho=k\), the full symmetric multiplicity at a sum is
\[

=
\sum_{\sum n_\rho\rho=\lambda}
\prod_{\rho}
\binom{n_\rho+m_\rho-1}{m_\rho-1}.
\]
Consequently,
\[

=
\sum_\lambda\ell_\lambda f(\lambda)
+
\sum_\lambda(a_\lambda-\ell_\lambda)f(\lambda).
}
\]

The second sum is the quotient’s trace. Both sums retain the cohomological factor \((-1)^k\) in top degree.

For example, an order-three local factor taken twice has a six-dimensional symmetric module. The cyclic part has length five at \(2\rho\), while the quotient retains one further dimension there. This is an algebraic example of the formula, not a claim that \(\xi\) has a triple zero.

## 5. The next relation is precisely the class sent to \(e\)

Define
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak b_N
=
\mathcal V_{h,k}(p_{N+1})
-
\mathcal R_Nb_{N+1}.
}
\]

Its full arithmetic jets vanish. Its leading polynomial term gives the explicit isomorphism
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb C
\xrightarrow{c\mapsto c\mathfrak b_N}
\mathcal D_{N+1}\cap\mathcal D_N^\perp
\xrightarrow{z\mapsto[z]}
\mathcal D_{N+1}/\mathcal D_N,
}
\]
where
\[
\mathcal D_N
=
\mathcal V_{h,k}
\bigl(\chi\,\mathbb C[S]_{\le N-q_k}\bigr).
\]

Its size and cross-pairing are
\[
\boxed{
\|\mathfrak b_N\|^2
=
\omega_{N+1}
+
b_{N+1}^*\mathcal G_Nb_{N+1},
}
\]
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak b_N^*\mathcal R_N
=
-b_{N+1}^*\mathcal G_N.
}
\]

For a nonzero coefficient, this relation is nonzero at degree \(N\). Its transport to degree \(N+1\) gives
\[
(\lambda_N,[\mathfrak b_N])
\longmapsto
(\lambda_{N+1},0).
\]

That is the receiving supported zero. External absence still maps to \(\tau\).

The exact metric update is
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal G_{N+1}
=
\mathcal G_N
-
\frac{
\mathcal G_Nb_{N+1}b_{N+1}^*\mathcal G_N
}{
\omega_{N+1}+b_{N+1}^*\mathcal G_Nb_{N+1}
}.
}
\]

So the \(e\)-transition, its norm, its cross-pairing, and its effect on the arithmetic metric are calculated together.

## 6. The differentiated polynomial source is now computable from one-factor moments

The preceding estimate was
\[
\mathcal I_{h,k}
+
4\int\|n_{h,k}(u)\|^2\,du
=
\frac{\mu_h^{k-1}}{k}\mathcal I_h.
\]

For the new cyclic source, the full derivative remains
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\partial_u\!\left(\Psi_{h,k}P(k/2+iu)\right)
={}&
\Psi_{h,k}
\left(
iP'(k/2+iu)
+\frac{m_{h,k}'}{2m_{h,k}}P(k/2+iu)
\right)\\
&+n_{h,k}P(k/2+iu).
\end{aligned}
}
\]
The two components are orthogonal. The relative term is still present.

I calculated **all polynomially weighted moments of this derivative**, not only its constant-column estimate.

Set
\[
\mu_j=\int t^j|a_h(t)|^2\,dt,
\qquad
\nu_j=\int t^j|a_h'(t)|^2\,dt.
\]
Fixed arithmetic phase and integration by parts give
\[
\int t^j\overline{a_h}a_h'\,dt
=
-\frac j2\mu_{j-1},
\qquad j\ge1,
\]
and zero at \(j=0\).

Introduce the formal series
\[
\mathcal M(z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\mu_j\frac{z^j}{j!},
\qquad
\mathcal N(z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\nu_j\frac{z^j}{j!}.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\int u^j m_{h,k}(u)\,du
=
j![z^j]\mathcal M(z)^k,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\int u^j\|\partial_u\Psi_{h,k}\|^2\,du
=
j![z^j]\left[
\frac1k\mathcal N(z)\mathcal M(z)^{k-1}
+
\frac{k-1}{4k}z^2\mathcal M(z)^k
\right].
}
\]

**Proof.** Expand \(u^j=(t_1+\cdots+t_k)^j\). The diagonal derivative terms give the first summand. The distinct-index terms give
\[
\frac{k-1}{k}
\left(-\frac z2\mathcal M(z)\right)^2
\mathcal M(z)^{k-2},
\]
which is the second summand.

That term vanishes for the zeroth moment, but it does not vanish for arbitrary polynomial moments.

For coefficient functions \(c_P(u)=P(k/2+iu)\), the entire derivative Gram form is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak D_k(P,Q)
={}&
\int\overline{c_P}c_Q\,\|\Psi_k'\|^2\,du
+
\int\overline{c_P'}c_Q'\,m_k\,du\\
&+\frac12\int
\left(
\overline{c_P}c_Q'
+
\overline{c_P'}c_Q
\right)m_k'\,du .
\end{aligned}
}
\]

All its entries on a finite polynomial source now follow from the one-factor arrays \(\mu_j,\nu_j\), with all \(k\), mass, derivative, and cross-term factors retained.

The general Fisher-information projection mechanism remains the established background; these formulas apply it to the original arithmetic amplitude and calculate the additional polynomial data needed here. citeturn143300view2

## 7. Every original conormal depth has an exact sum-coordinate quotient

This is the second main new result.

Keep the original ideal
\[
I_k=(h(s_1),\ldots,h(s_k))
\subset\mathbb C[s_1,\ldots,s_k].
\]

For \(r\ge1\), its actual thickening is
\[
B_{k,r}=\mathbb C[s_1,\ldots,s_k]/I_k^r.
\]

For an ordered root tuple, define
\[
L_{\boldsymbol\rho,r}
=
1+\sum_{i=1}^k(m_{\rho_i}-1)
+(r-1)\max_i m_{\rho_i}.
\]
At a sum \(\lambda\), take
\[
\ell_{\lambda,r}
=
\max_{\sum\rho_i=\lambda}L_{\boldsymbol\rho,r}.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
I_k^r\cap\mathbb C[S]
=
(\chi_{h,k,r}),
\qquad
\chi_{h,k,r}
=
\prod_\lambda(S-\lambda)^{\ell_{\lambda,r}}.
}
\]

**Proof.** At a root tuple, the original local ideal is
\[
(z_1^{m_1},\ldots,z_k^{m_k}),
\]
with the local units in \(h(\rho_i+z_i)\) retained through their invertible generator maps.

A monomial survives its \(r\)-th power exactly when
\[
\sum_i\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha_i}{m_i}\right\rfloor
\le r-1.
\]
Its largest possible total degree is
\[
\sum_i(m_i-1)+(r-1)\max_i m_i.
\]

That degree occurs in \((z_1+\cdots+z_k)^D\) with a nonzero multinomial coefficient, while every term of the next degree vanishes. This proves the exact local exponent. Taking maxima over equal sums proves the contracted ideal formula.

Hence there is an injective algebra map
\[
\boxed{
\alpha_r:
\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_{h,k,r})
\hookrightarrow B_{k,r}^{S_k}.
}
\]

The quotient and derivative squares both commute:
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_{r+1})&\xrightarrow{\alpha_{r+1}}&B_{k,r+1}\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_r)&\xrightarrow{\alpha_r}&B_{k,r},
\end{array}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\delta_r\alpha_{r+1}
=
\alpha_r\partial_r,
}
\]
where
\[
\partial_r[P]=[P'],
\qquad
\delta_r[P]=
\left[\frac1k\sum_i\partial_{s_i}P\right].
\]

The vertical quotients are ring maps. The derivatives are coefficient-linear maps, lifted through the corresponding original semimodule construction.

### A concrete higher-order example

For the algebraic fixture
\[
h(s)=(s-\rho)^2,\qquad k=2,\qquad X=S-2\rho,
\]
the exact result is
\[
\boxed{\chi_{h,2,r}=X^{2r+1}.}
\]

At \(r=2\), the relationship to the ordinary square of the first annihilator is
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb C[X]/(X^6)
\twoheadrightarrow
\mathbb C[X]/(X^5)
\hookrightarrow
\mathbb C[z_1,z_2]/(z_1^2,z_2^2)^2.
}
\]
The first map has the retained kernel generated by \(X^5\).

Meanwhile, \(X^3\) is nonzero modulo \(X^5\), maps to the supported zero modulo \(X^3\), and its derivative is
\[
\boxed{\partial X^3=3X^2\ne0\pmod{X^3}.}
\]

This is an explicit higher relation above the **same** scalar support. It does not iterate the scalar zero-adjunction.

## 8. The arithmetic unit and trace remain attached to that derivative

Let \(U_{k,r}\) be the full Taylor class of
\[
\prod_i(g/h)(s_i)
\]
in \(B_{k,r}\). Define
\[
\eta_r=M_{U_{k,r}}\alpha_r.
\]

The exact derivative equation is
\[
\boxed{
\delta_r\eta_{r+1}(P)
=
U_{k,r}\alpha_r(P')
+
(\delta_rU_{k,r+1})\alpha_r(P).
}
\]

The second term stays in the full relative ring. Its component outside the cyclic image is recorded by the explicit quotient
\[
B_{k,r}\longrightarrow B_{k,r}/\eta_rC_{h,k,r}.
\]

For an original relation \(\chi_{h,k}P\), its first differentiated arithmetic observation is
\[
\boxed{
J^{(k)}\mathscr L_k
\mathcal V_{h,k}(\chi_{h,k}P)
=
U_k\alpha_1(\chi_{h,k}'P),
\qquad
\mathscr L_k=\frac1k\sum_i\log x_i.
}
\]

The term involving \(\delta U\) has an undifferentiated \(\chi\), so the quotient sends that term to its supported zero.

The cyclic residue contraction is therefore
\[
\sum_\lambda
\operatorname{Res}_{S=\lambda}
f^{\dagger_k}(S)P(S)
\frac{\chi_{h,k}'(S)}{\chi_{h,k}(S)}\,dS
=
\sum_\lambda
\ell_\lambda\,
\overline{f(k-\bar\lambda)}P(\lambda).
\]

The full symmetric arithmetic trace has \(a_\lambda\) instead of \(\ell_\lambda\), with their difference retained in \(T_{h,k}\). Moreover, the original vector pairing pulled back through the weighted inclusion is exactly
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}_{B_k^{S_k}}
M_{(\eta f)^\dagger\eta P}
=
\operatorname{Tr}_{B_k^{S_k}}
M_{U_k^\dagger U_k\,\alpha_1(f^{\dagger_k}P)}.
}
\]
The factor \(U_k^\dagger U_k\) remains.

Thus \(\chi_{h,k}\) is an annihilator of the existing sum action, connected to \(g=2\xi\) through the source map, full arithmetic unit, and trace comparison. It is not substituted for the arithmetic function.

Previously, testing one eigenvector bounded the largest individual real-part defect. This bounds **their entire positive sum**, with all generalized-eigenspace multiplicities retained.

of common multiplicity \(m\), the calculation gives

\boxed{

## 3. Exterior powers retain the same allowance, rather than multiplying it

For \(1\le p\le\dim C\), define the **additive exterior generator**
\[
A^{[p]}(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_p)
=
\sum_{j=1}^p
v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge Av_j\wedge\cdots\wedge v_p.

Its relationship to the multiplicative exterior action is
\[

A^{[p]}
=
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}
\bigwedge\nolimits^p(e^{tA}),
\qquad
\bigwedge\nolimits^p(e^{tA})
=
e^{tA^{[p]}}.

In the unscaled wedge basis, let
\[
(G_N^{[p]})_{I,J}
=
\det(G_N)_{I,J}.

\[

G_N^{[p]}A^{[p]}

G_N^{[p]}\mathsf H_N^{[p]}.

\[

+
G_N^{[p]}A^{[p]}

\epsilon_NG_N^{[p]}.

There is no factor \(p\) multiplying \(\epsilon_N\).

\[

and both \(L_+\) and \(L_-\) are one-dimensional.

The exterior space decomposes through the actual wedge maps into
\[

={}&
\bigwedge\nolimits^p Z_0\\
&\oplus
\left(L_+\wedge\bigwedge\nolimits^{p-1}Z_0\right)\\

\bigwedge\nolimits^{p-2}Z_0\right).

0,\quad\epsilon_N,\quad-\epsilon_N,\quad0.
\]

\qquad

There is no genericity assumption about zero ordinates here.

To construct the sum with margins \(a,b\), choose any integer
\[

\]
The four occupation counts
\[

\[

\[

=
\prod_{a,b=0}^k(S-\lambda_{a,b})^{\ell_k},

\[

=
\ell_k(k+1)\left\lceil\frac k2\right\rceil.

\[

&=
2\delta\ell_k(k+1)
\sum_{a=\lfloor k/2\rfloor+1}^{k}(2a-k)\\
&=

2\delta\ell_k(k+1)
\left\lfloor\frac{(k+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.

\end{aligned}
\]

For \(k=2n\), the inner sum is \(n(n+1)\). For \(k=2n+1\), it is \((n+1)^2\). The imaginary parts cancel in the determinant trace.

\[

## 2. The repository’s gamma reference closes exactly under the sum map

## 3. The entire relative fibre has an explicit projection and complement

Define
\[

Its adjoint is the explicit fibre integral
\[

\begin{aligned}
(C_\Sigma F)(u)
={}&\frac1{r_{\lambda,k}(u)}
\int_{\mathbb R^{k-1}}
F\!\left(t_1,\ldots,t_{k-1},u-\sum_{i<k}t_i\right)\\

\prod_{i<k}r_\lambda(t_i)\,
r_\lambda\!\left(u-\sum_{i<k}t_i\right)

Fubini proves

\qquad

Writing \(P_\Sigma=U_\Sigma C_\Sigma\), the two inverse maps are
\[

F\longmapsto

## A2177 | node da706e04-bfb8-4d3f-9747-194c30e053b2 | assistant | chain 4483

**One of the analytic estimates in the new endpoint criterion is now proved for the actual arithmetic measure.** For a fixed packet \(h\), retaining all its selected zero orders, I obtain
\[
\boxed{
\left(
\frac{\omega_{h,k,2n}}{\omega_{h,k,n}}
\right)^{1/(2n)}
\le C_h n,
\qquad n\ge k\ge3,
}
\]
where \(C_h<\infty\) depends on \(h\), but **not** on the tensor degree \(k\) or polynomial degree \(n\).

This establishes the \(O_h(q_k)\) polynomial-norm input proposed in the formalization session’s handoff, on the explicit window \(q_k\le N<2q_k\). That handoff had correctly left this arithmetic estimate unproved. fileciteturn303file0L247-L261

Combining the bound with its endpoint-selection theorem gives a sharper statement about the remaining source–relation volumes: **an off-line quartet would force**
\[
\boxed{
\liminf_{k\to\infty}
\frac{
\log\!\left(
V_{q_k-1}V_{q_k}/(V_{2q_k-1}V_{2q_k})
\right)
}{
q_k\log k
}
\ge2.
}
\]
The upper bound excluding that volume growth is not proved here. The norm factor in this particular criterion, however, is no longer an assumed estimate.

## 1. The estimate concerns the original arithmetic source

I read the current main revision, which now includes the exterior/trace formalization, and the endpoint and confluent-transfer developments in PRs #23 and #24. Their source maps remain the inputs here; I have not replaced them with another positive metric. fileciteturn304file0L2-L2 fileciteturn305file0L8-L13

## 2. The new analytic input is a lower bound after three actual convolutions

The earlier gamma comparison supplied an upper envelope. For the endpoint norm ratio, I constructed a lower envelope for the **unchanged arithmetic density**.

The starting lemma is
\[
\boxed{
\int_{T-1}^{T+1}
|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2\,dt
\ge c_\zeta(1+|T|)^{-42},
\qquad T\in\mathbb R,
}
\]
for a fixed positive constant \(c_\zeta\). The exponent \(42\) is a sufficient explicit exponent; no optimal local mean-square estimate is claimed.

### The local-mass proof

For \(|T|\ge10\), put
\[
f_T(z)=\zeta(\tfrac12+iT+iz).
\]

On the ellipse
\[
z=\frac12(w+w^{-1}),
\qquad |w|=8,
\]
the functional equation and the vertical-strip gamma estimate give
\[
|f_T(z)|\le M_T=C_0(1+|T|)^6.
\]
The relevant strip is fixed, and the zeta pole lies outside the ellipse. For the part with positive real component, the direct identity
\[
\zeta(s)=\frac{s}{s-1}
-s\int_1^\infty\{x\}x^{-s-1}\,dx
\]
gives the needed polynomial growth; reflection handles the remaining part. These use the classical zeta functional equation and gamma estimates, without RH. citeturn510644view0turn510644view1

The absolutely convergent reciprocal Dirichlet series gives
\[
|\zeta(2+iT)|\ge\zeta(2)^{-1}.
\]

Let
\[
r_*=\frac{3+\sqrt{13}}2<4.
\]
Then
\[
\frac12\left(-ir_*+\frac1{-ir_*}\right)=-\frac{3i}{2},
\]
so \(f_T\) at this point is \(\zeta(2+iT)\).

Write
\[
m_T=\max_{x\in[-1,1]}|f_T(x)|.
\]
The maximum principle on the annulus \(1\le|w|\le8\), applied through the displayed coordinate map, gives
\[
\zeta(2)^{-1}
\le
m_T^\vartheta M_T^{1-\vartheta},
\qquad
\vartheta
=
1-\frac{\log r_*}{\log8}
>\frac13.
\]
Hence
\[
m_T\ge\zeta(2)^{-3}M_T^{-2}.
\]

Cauchy’s estimate also gives
\[
\sup_{[-1,1]}|f_T'|\le M_T.
\]
Around a point attaining \(m_T\), there is a one-sided interval of length \(m_T/(2M_T)\) on which \(|f_T|\ge m_T/2\). Therefore
\[
\int_{T-1}^{T+1}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2\,dt
\ge
\frac{m_T^3}{8M_T}
\ge
\frac{\zeta(2)^{-9}}{8C_0^7}(1+|T|)^{-42}.
\]

On the remaining compact range of \(T\), the integral is continuous and strictly positive. Its minimum supplies the remaining positive constant.

### Carry the bound through \(g/h\)

The original gamma factor and the elementary polynomial bound for \(h\) imply
\[
w_h(t)
\ge
c_h^{(0)}
e^{-\pi|t|/2}(1+|t|)^{-2\deg h}
|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2.
\]

This inequality is valid at selected centres through the entire identity \(g=hv_h\); it does not divide by an unevaluated zero.

Consequently,
\[
\boxed{
\int_{T-1}^{T+1}w_h(t)\,dt
\ge
c_h^{(1)}
e^{-\pi|T|/2}(1+|T|)^{-B_h},
\qquad
B_h=42+2\deg h.
}
\]

Now \(w_h\) is continuous, integrable, and positive outside a discrete set. Thus \(w_h*w_h\) is continuous and strictly positive everywhere. Define the actual compact quantities
\[
b_h=\min_{|v|\le1}(w_h*w_h)(v)>0,
\qquad
\vartheta_h=\int_{-1}^{1}w_h(v)\,dv>0.
\]

Restricting a nonnegative convolution integral gives
\[
m_{h,3}(u)
\ge
b_h\int_{u-1}^{u+1}w_h(t)\,dt.
\]
For the remaining \(k-3\) factors, restrict their integration variables to \([-1,1]\). Their sum has absolute value at most \(k-3\). This proves
\[
\boxed{
m_{h,k}(u)
\ge
c_h\vartheta_h^{\,k-3}
e^{-\frac\pi2(|u|+k-3)}
(1+|u|+k-3)^{-B_h},
\qquad k\ge3.
}
\]

**The original mass has not been changed.** The complementary integration regions remain part of \(m_{h,k}\); this is a lower bound obtained from one positive contribution to that same density.

## 3. This proves the required endpoint norm bound

Fix \(0<b<\pi/2\), and retain the two original Laplace values
\[
M_h(\pm b)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{\pm bt}w_h(t)\,dt.
\]

The exponential-series inequality and convolution identity give
\[
\boxed{
\omega_{h,k,j}
\le
(2j)!b^{-2j}
\bigl(M_h(b)^k+M_h(-b)^k\bigr).
}
\]
The trial polynomial is \((S-k/2)^j\), whose value on the original integration line is \(i^ju^j\). The operator remains multiplication by \(S\).

For the lower estimate, the exact least squared norm of a monic polynomial of degree \(n\) on \([-L,L]\) is
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak l_n(L)
=
\frac{2L^{2n+1}}{2n+1}
\left(\frac{2^n(n!)^2}{(2n)!}\right)^2.
}
\]
This follows from the leading coefficient and orthogonality of the Legendre polynomial. Under \(S=k/2+iu\), the retained leading phase is \(i^n\), whose squared modulus is one. citeturn510644view2turn825817search0

Applying the lower convolution envelope on \([-L,L]\) yields
\[
\boxed{
\omega_{h,k,n}
\ge
c_h\vartheta_h^{\,k-3}
e^{-\frac\pi2(L+k-3)}
(1+L+k-3)^{-B_h}\,
\mathfrak l_n(L).
}
\]

Set \(L=n\), and apply the upper estimate at degree \(2n\). The exact finite bound is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\left(\frac{\omega_{h,k,2n}}{\omega_{h,k,n}}\right)^{1/(2n)}
\le
\left[
\frac{
(4n)!b^{-4n}
\bigl(M_h(b)^k+M_h(-b)^k\bigr)
e^{\frac\pi2(n+k-3)}
(1+n+k-3)^{B_h}
}{
c_h\vartheta_h^{\,k-3}\mathfrak l_n(n)
}
\right]^{1/(2n)}.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

For \(n\ge k\ge3\), this is at most \(C_hn\).

The degree dependence follows directly from
\[
\binom{2n}{n}\le4^n,
\qquad
(4n)!\le(4n)^{4n},
\qquad
n+k-3\le2n.
\]
The factorial and monic-norm factors contribute \(O(n)\) after taking the \(2n\)-th root. The retained mass factors contribute bounded factors of the form \(\exp(O_h(k/n))\). The polynomial lower-envelope factor contributes
\[
(2n)^{B_h/(2n)},
\]
which is uniformly bounded.

Equation (36) of the note gives a literal sufficient \(C_h\), retaining all these constants. It is deliberately not optimized or presented as a numerically certified constant.

**This establishes a bound on the actual arithmetic norm sequence, uniformly in the required tensor and polynomial degrees.**

## 4. The endpoint criterion now leaves a precise four-volume threshold

The formalization session’s theorem is
\[
\boxed{
\min_{0\le j<r}\epsilon_{h,k,n+j}
\le
\left(\frac{\omega_{h,k,n+r}}{\omega_{h,k,n}}\right)^{1/(2r)}
\sinh\!\left(
\frac1{2r}
\log\frac{V_{n-1}V_n}{V_{n+r-1}V_{n+r}}
\right).
}
\]
It selects a member of the existing canonical family. Its proof retains both telescopes and the zero-contraction case; the report distinguishes its checked finite components from the written Jensen assembly. fileciteturn303file0L143-L215

Taking \(r=n\ge\max(q,k)\) now gives
\[
\boxed{
\min_{n\le N<2n}\epsilon_{h,k,N}
\le
C_hn\,
\sinh\!\left(
\frac1{2n}
\log\frac{V_{n-1}V_n}{V_{2n-1}V_{2n}}
\right).
}
\]

For the packet **consisting exactly of** an off-line quartet
\[
\tfrac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma,
\qquad \delta,\gamma>0,
\]
with common multiplicity \(m\), retain
\[
q_k=[1+k(m-1)](k+1)^2
\]
and the existing aggregate defect
\[
L_{h,k}
=
2\delta[1+k(m-1)](k+1)
\left\lfloor\frac{(k+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]

Here \(q_k\ge k\), and
\[
\frac{L_{h,k}}{q_k}\ge\frac{\delta k}{2}.
\]
The exterior theorem bounds \(L_{h,k}\) by every admitted allowance, including the degree selected above.

Define
\[
\mathcal B_{h,k}
=
\log\frac{V_{q_k-1}V_{q_k}}{V_{2q_k-1}V_{2q_k}}.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\frac{\delta k}{2}
\le
C_h\sinh\!\left(\frac{\mathcal B_{h,k}}{2q_k}\right),
}
\]
and therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal B_{h,k}
\ge
2q_k\operatorname{arsinh}\!\left(\frac{\delta k}{2C_h}\right).
}
\]

Since \(h\) is fixed,
\[
\operatorname{arsinh}\!\left(\frac{\delta k}{2C_h}\right)
=
\log k+O_h(1).
\]
This proves the threshold
\[
\boxed{
\liminf_{k\to\infty}
\frac{\mathcal B_{h,k}}{q_k\log k}\ge2.
}
\]

The remaining upper estimate in this endpoint criterion is therefore sharply specified. The previously proposed
\[
\mathcal B_{h,k}=o_h(q_k\log k)
\]
would suffice; an upper limit strictly below \(2\) would already contradict the displayed lower threshold. **Neither upper estimate is being claimed here.**

No second cost-free exterior iteration is used. The formalization session’s correction to that iteration’s multiplicity cost remains intact. fileciteturn303file0L297-L329

## 5. Those four volumes are two explicit costs of retained \(e\)-relations

I also expressed the remaining volume quantity directly through the original relation layers.

For admitted degrees \(i<j\), put
\[
F_{i,j}=[b_{i+1},\ldots,b_j],
\qquad
\Omega_{i,j}
=
\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{i+1},\ldots,\omega_j),
\]
where \(b_a=[p_a]_\chi\) retains all quotient coordinates.

The existing full-jet kernel has the exact update
\[
K_j=K_i+F_{i,j}\Omega_{i,j}^{-1}F_{i,j}^*,
\qquad K_i=G_i^{-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{
\frac{V_i}{V_j}
=
\det\!\left(
I+\Omega_{i,j}^{-1}F_{i,j}^*G_iF_{i,j}
\right).
}
\]

The source map behind this determinant is
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak b_{i,j}
=
T_{i,j}-R_iF_{i,j}:
\mathbb C^{j-i}
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal D_j\cap\mathcal D_i^\perp,
}
\]
where \(T_{i,j}\) has the actual source columns
\(\mathcal V_{h,k}p_{i+1},\ldots,\mathcal V_{h,k}p_j\).

Its jets vanish, its highest polynomial coefficients give the inverse onto the new relation layer, and its Gram is
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak b_{i,j}^*\mathfrak b_{i,j}
=
\Omega_{i,j}+F_{i,j}^*G_iF_{i,j}.
}
\]

The representative update remains
\[
\boxed{
R_j
=
R_i+
\mathfrak b_{i,j}
\bigl(\Omega_{i,j}+F_{i,j}^*G_iF_{i,j}\bigr)^{-1}
F_{i,j}^*G_i.
}
\]

Every correction is an original theta boundary. The complete transport is
\[
\mathbb C^{j-i}
\xrightarrow{\mathfrak b_{i,j}}
\mathcal D_j/\mathcal D_i
\hookrightarrow
\mathscr B^{\widehat\otimes k}/\mathcal D_i
\longrightarrow
\mathscr B^{\widehat\otimes k}/\mathcal D_j.
\]
Its final composite is zero. In the original split lift, it is the receiving fibre’s **supported zero**, not \(\tau\).

Applying this to
\[
(i,j)=(q_k-1,2q_k-1),
\qquad
(i,j)=(q_k,2q_k)
\]
gives
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal B_{h,k}
=
\sum_a\log(1+\lambda_a^{(0)})
+
\sum_a\log(1+\lambda_a^{(1)}),
}
\]
where each \(\lambda_a^{(\ell)}\ge0\) is a generalized eigenvalue of the corresponding explicit pair
\[
\bigl(F_{i,j}^*G_iF_{i,j},\,\Omega_{i,j}\bigr).
\]

**This is the remaining volume cost in terms of the relations that become \(e\)-zero.** Their source norms and cross-pairings are still present before that quotient.

The PR #24 transfer coordinates provide another exact calculation of the same four endpoints. Only its matrices at indices
\[
0,\quad1,\quad q_k,\quad q_k+1
\]
are needed, together with the specified products of \(\omega_j\). The common confluent Vandermonde cancels only in the displayed endpoint ratio; its raw-derivative factorials remain in the underlying maps. The note spells out that formula.

## A2225 | node 3fe5603d-ea16-4fb3-b0d0-995546d1c47a | assistant | chain 4571

**The remaining four-volume term now has an exact interpretation on the original arithmetic representatives:** it measures how much of their information can be recovered after restricting to an earlier polynomial degree.

I constructed that restriction map, its metric adjoint, its interaction with the arithmetic action, and a convergent finite upper certificate for its logarithmic volume loss. The central identities are
\[
\boxed{
T_{i,j}=K_iG_j,\qquad
R_iT_{i,j}=\operatorname{pr}_{\le i}R_j,\qquad
T_{i,j}T_{j,l}=T_{i,l}.
}
\]
Here every \(G_N\) is the existing canonical arithmetic metric, \(K_N=G_N^{-1}\), and every \(R_N\) is its existing minimum-norm representative.

The original relations remain visible in
\[
\boxed{
R_i-R_j
=
R_i(I-T_{i,j})-(I-\operatorname{pr}_{\le i})R_j.
}
\]
The two terms on the right have the same arithmetic image. Their difference is the original theta relation that becomes the receiving fibre’s supported zero.

## 1. The source, infinite quotient, and arithmetic action stay fixed

The base remains \(\mathfrak b_\tau\), carrying
\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow{G(j)}&G(\mathbb C)\\
p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\
\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{j}&\mathbb C.
\end{array}
}
\]
The first arithmetic target remains infinite. The maps carry the supported scalar \(e=0^\bullet\) and external absence \(\tau\) separately before applying the arithmetic observation.

Retain
\[
C_+=[V\xrightarrow{\Theta}\mathscr B],
\qquad
Q=\mathscr B/\Theta V,
\qquad
D=-x\partial_x,
\qquad
g=2\xi.
\]

For the fixed full packet \(h\) and tensor degree \(k\), the finite cyclic object is still
\[
E=\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_{h,k}),
\qquad
q=\deg\chi_{h,k},
\qquad
A=M_S,
\qquad
S=s_1+\cdots+s_k.
\]

Its source is
\[
\mathcal VP
=
P(D_1+\cdots+D_k)(F_h^{\otimes k}),
\qquad
\mathcal MF_h=g/h,
\]
with the actual norm
\[
\|\mathcal VP\|^2
=
\int_{\mathbb R}|P(k/2+iu)|^2m_{h,k}(u)\,du.
\]

The full arithmetic inclusion remains
\[
\eta[P]
=
\upsilon_h^{\otimes k}P(A_k)1,
\qquad
\upsilon_h=j_h(g/h),
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
J^{(k)}\mathcal V=\eta\pi_\chi,
\qquad
q^{(k)}\mathcal V
=
\sigma_h^{\otimes k}\eta\pi_\chi.
}
\]

Thus the retained unit and all nilpotent jets are still attached. The underlying full-jet construction already fixes the metric through the specified source and relation space; it does not leave an arbitrary positive form to choose. fileciteturn310file4L7-L18

## 2. The degree restriction is the adjoint of the original quotient transport

Use the unscaled monic polynomial basis
\[
p_0,\ldots,p_N
\]
and its actual squared norms \(\omega_0,\ldots,\omega_N\), with
\[
\omega_0=\mu_h^k.
\]

In fixed remainder coordinates, define
\[
B_N=[b_0,\ldots,b_N],
\qquad
b_n=[p_n]_\chi,
\qquad
O_N=\operatorname{diag}(\omega_0,\ldots,\omega_N).
\]

The source formulas are
\[
\boxed{
K_N=B_NO_N^{-1}B_N^*,
\qquad
G_N=K_N^{-1},
\qquad
R_N=O_N^{-1}B_N^*G_N.
}
\]
They give
\[
B_NR_N=I_E,
\qquad
R_N^*O_NR_N=G_N.
\]

For \(i\le j\), let
\[
L_{i,j}:\mathcal P_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal P_j
\]
be coefficient padding, and let \(P_{i,j}\) retain the first \(i+1\) monic coordinates in \(\mathcal P_j\). Orthogonality makes \(P_{i,j}\) the actual orthogonal projection onto the earlier source.

The quotient transport is
\[
I_{i,j}:(E,G_i)\longrightarrow(E,G_j),
\qquad
u\longmapsto u.
\]
It is the transport induced by the source inclusion:
\[
B_jL_{i,j}=I_{i,j}B_i.
\]

The larger source admits more original relations, so
\[
G_j\preceq G_i.
\]
Consequently this identity transport is a contraction between its two specified metrics.

Its metric adjoint is
\[
\boxed{
T_{i,j}:(E,G_j)\longrightarrow(E,G_i),
\qquad
T_{i,j}=K_iG_j.
}
\]

**Proof.**
\[
\langle I_{i,j}u,v\rangle_{G_j}
=

## 1. What the Deligne rereading adds

I reassembled and hash-checked the six supplied S20 parts, then read the relevant retained French and English LaTeX against the current page-local French records. The [reading record](sandbox:/mnt/data/Tau_Deligne_Specialization_Curvature/SOURCE_REVIEW.md) identifies the exact files, ranges, and transcription discrepancies. This is a selected reading of *La conjecture de Weil II*, not a new audit of its entire proof. citeturn759319view0

The decisive addition is **not just another tensor operation**.

In §§3.2.8–3.2.13, Deligne first controls what occurs at the exceptional fibres. The resulting calculation gives integral weights for the relevant nonconstant constituents. The independent bound is **strictly below two**, so those integral weights are at most one. Constant constituents contribute zero to the specified first cohomology of the projective line. Only after those steps do the Leray and tensor-square maps improve the bound on the same eigenvalue.

The older French transcription loses two essential details: it writes a non-strict inequality in 3.2.10 and loses the square on the tensor eigenvalue in 3.2.13. The current page record retains both.

The later purity statement also concerns a particular comparison:
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)
\twoheadrightarrow
\operatorname{im}c_i
\hookrightarrow
H^i(X,\mathcal F).
\]
The two already-proved bounds meet on that image; the mixed source and target are not removed. The degree and dualizing twist are part of the argument. fileciteturn325file1L48-L86 fileciteturn325file1L114-L140

**What I added here is the corresponding concrete work on our side: construct the curve, calculate the exceptional comparison and its complete fibre, retain the action, and calculate the determinant metric on that object.**

## 2. Build the curve from the existing representatives

Keep the original coefficient square over the marked \(\tau\)-base:
\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow{G(\jmath)}&G(\mathbb C)\\
p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\
\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{\jmath}&\mathbb C.
\end{array}
}
\]
The first arithmetic target remains infinite. The split coefficients retain \(e=0^\bullet\) and external absence \(\tau\) before applying \(p\).

For the current finite cyclic object,
\[
E=\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_{h,k}),\qquad A=M_S,
\]
retain
\[
K_N=B_NO_N^{-1}B_N^*,\qquad
G_N=K_N^{-1},\qquad
R_N=O_N^{-1}B_N^*G_N.
\]
Here \(B_N\) is the original full remainder matrix, \(O_N\) contains the actual monic source norms, and the arithmetic inclusion still contains \(\upsilon_h^{\otimes k}\). The canonical metric is determined by that source and its admitted relations. fileciteturn320file6L7-L18

For \(i\le j\), pad the earlier source through
\[
L_{ij}:\mathcal P_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal P_j
\]
and define
\[
\boxed{
\Delta=L_{ij}R_i-R_j:E\longrightarrow\mathcal P_j.
}
\]

Both representatives have remainder identity, and the later representative is orthogonal to its relation space. Therefore
\[
B_j\Delta=0,\qquad R_j^*O_j\Delta=0,
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
C:=\Delta^*O_j\Delta=G_i-G_j\succeq0.
}
\]

Now form the actual family
\[
\boxed{
R(z)=R_j+z\Delta:E\longrightarrow\mathcal P_j.
}
\]
Direct expansion gives
\[
\boxed{
B_jR(z)=I_E,\qquad
G(z):=R(z)^*O_jR(z)=G_j+|z|^2C.
}
\]

Every finite \(z\) therefore retains the same arithmetic jets and cohomology class:
\[
J^{(k)}\mathcal VR(z)=\eta,
\qquad
q^{(k)}\mathcal VR(z)=\sigma_h^{\otimes k}\eta.
\]

The marked endpoints are
\[
R(0)=R_j,\qquad R(1)=L_{ij}R_i.
\]
The new coordinate \(z\) parametrizes this comparison. The original spectral coordinate remains \(S\), with its original action \(A\).

## 3. Compactify it and compute the exceptional fibre

Set
\[
E_0=\ker\Delta,\qquad
E_1=E_0^{\perp_{G_j}},\qquad
r=\dim E_1.
\]
Let \(P_0,P_1\) be the corresponding specified projections.

On \(\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb C}\), with homogeneous coordinates \([u:v]\), define
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr E_{ij}
=
(E_0\otimes\mathcal O)
\oplus
(E_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)).
}
\]

The map into the original source is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\Psi:\mathscr E_{ij}&\longrightarrow\mathcal P_j\otimes\mathcal O,\\
x_0+x_1\otimes(u,v)
&\longmapsto R_jx_0+uR_jx_1+v\Delta x_1.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

This is injective on every fibre. For \(u\ne0\), applying \(B_j\) forces \(x_0=x_1=0\). At \(u=0\), it first forces \(x_0=0\), and injectivity of \(\Delta|_{E_1}\) forces \(x_1=0\).

On the finite chart \(z=v/u\), this is exactly \(R(z)\). On the infinity chart \(w=u/v\), it is
\[
\boxed{
\Psi_\infty(w)
=
R_jP_0+wR_jP_1+\Delta P_1.
}
\]

The original arithmetic observation becomes
\[
\alpha=B_j\Psi:\mathscr E_{ij}\longrightarrow E\otimes\mathcal O,
\]
with local expression
\[
\boxed{\alpha_\infty=P_0+wP_1.}
\]

Consequently,
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow\mathscr E_{ij}
\xrightarrow{\alpha}
E\otimes\mathcal O
\longrightarrow i_{\infty*}E_1
\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

This is the effective-divisor exact sequence on the modified columns, with its actual source map supplied above. citeturn759319view1

### The lost fibre is retained in the derived comparison

Specializing \(w=0\) gives \(P_0\). The derived fibre of the displayed cokernel is the actual complex
\[
\boxed{
[E\xrightarrow{P_0}E]
\quad\text{in degrees }-1,0.
}
\]
Its cohomology is
\[
\boxed{H^{-1}=E_1,\qquad H^0=E_1.}
\]

Intrinsically, the kernel carries
\[
E_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)|_\infty;
\]
the chosen infinity frame gives the displayed coefficient identification.

In the split lift,
\[
w^\bullet\longmapsto e
\]
under specialization. A represented vector killed by \(P_0\) maps to the receiving supported zero, **and remains present in the derived kernel**. External absence maps to \(\tau\). This is precisely the original internal-homology treatment of a class whose image becomes a boundary. fileciteturn320file11L90-L112

The global comparison is also calculated:
\[
\boxed{
H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathscr E_{ij})=E_0,
\qquad
H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathscr E_{ij})=0.
}
\]
Its source image is \(E_0\subseteq E\). The full \(E\) remains the target and the saturation of the image lattice; it is not silently assigned to the smaller global image.

## 4. Duality and the arithmetic action now have explicit boundary maps

Dualizing the comparison gives
\[
\boxed{
0\to E^*\otimes\mathcal O
\to\mathscr E_{ij}^{\vee}
\to
i_{\infty*}\!\left(E_1^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)|_\infty\right)
\to0.
}
\]

The two boundary factors pair through
\[
\boxed{
(E_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)|_\infty)
\otimes
(E_1^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)|_\infty)
\longrightarrow\mathbb C_\infty.
}
\]
Both line factors remain.

The connection transported through \(\alpha\) is
\[
\nabla_\infty=d+P_1\frac{dw}{w}.
\]
Its residue is \(P_1\), and its horizontal monodromy is
\[
\exp(-2\pi iP_1)=I.
\]

The original arithmetic operator transports through the same map:
\[
\boxed{
\widehat A_\infty
=
(P_0+w^{-1}P_1)A(P_0+wP_1)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
A_{00}&wA_{01}\\
w^{-1}A_{10}&A_{11}
\end{pmatrix}.
}
\]

Thus the precise possible pole is
\[
w^{-1}P_1AP_0.
\]
The kernel of a metric comparison has not been presumed \(A\)-invariant.

### Construct the smallest enlargement that repairs that pole

Take the actual invariant hull
\[
\boxed{
F_A=E_0+AE_0+\cdots+A^{q-1}E_0,
\qquad q=\dim E.
}
\]
Cayley–Hamilton proves that this is the smallest \(A\)-invariant subspace containing \(E_0\).

Let \(\mathcal M=\alpha(\mathscr E_{ij})\). At infinity,
\[
\mathcal M_\infty=E_0\mathcal O+wE\mathcal O.
\]

Its smallest coherent \(A\)-stable enlargement inside the original target is
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M_A=\sum_{a=0}^{q-1}A^a\mathcal M,
\qquad
(\mathcal M_A)_\infty=F_A\mathcal O+wE\mathcal O.
}
\]

The exact sequences are
\[
0\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M_A
\to i_{\infty*}(F_A/E_0)\to0,
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
0\to\mathcal M_A\to E\otimes\mathcal O
\to i_{\infty*}(E/F_A)\to0.
}
\]

The second sequence now carries the regular original action throughout. It gives the equivariant global sequence
\[
0\to F_A\to E\to E/F_A\to0
\]
and retains the trace
\[
\operatorname{Tr}f(A)
=
\operatorname{Tr}(f(A)|F_A)
+
\operatorname{Tr}(f(\overline A)|E/F_A).
\]

The enlargement has a calculated source cost. Put
\[
s_A=\dim F_A-\dim E_0.
\]
The inclusion of the old lattice into the enlarged one has determinant \(w^{s_A}\). Pulling through the **original** source metric gives
\[
\boxed{
\det G_A(w)=|w|^{-2s_A}\det G_{\mathcal M}(w).
}
\]

**Regularizing the arithmetic action transfers the retained boundary contribution into a specified metric pole.** It does not make that contribution disappear.

## 5. The endpoint cost is the determinant curvature of this curve

Let
\[
\mathscr L_{ij}=(\det\mathscr E_{ij})^\vee.
\]
Its metric in the finite chart is
\[
(\det G(z))^{-1}.
\]

Define the curvature with its complete coefficient:
\[
\boxed{
c_1(\mathscr L_{ij})
=
\frac{i}{2\pi}\partial\bar\partial\log\det G(z).
}
\]

The operator in this formula is exactly the preceding relation-cost operator:
\[
\boxed{
Z=G_j^{-1}(G_i-G_j)
=(K_j-K_i)G_i.
}
\]
It is positive self-adjoint for \(G_j\).

Differentiation gives
\[
\boxed{
c_1(\mathscr L_{ij})
=
\frac{i}{2\pi}
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
Z(I+|z|^2Z)^{-2}
\right]dz\wedge d\bar z.
}
\]

Write
\[
\kappa_{ij}(t)
=
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[Z(I+tZ)^{-2}\right].
\]
The coordinate identity
\[
i\,dz\wedge d\bar z=2\,dx\wedge dy
\]
and polar integration give
\[
\boxed{
\int_{\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)}c_1(\mathscr L_{ij})
=
\int_0^\infty\kappa_{ij}(t)\,dt
=
r.
}
\]

That agrees with the independently computed divisor:
\[
\det\alpha=u^r,\qquad \deg\mathscr L_{ij}=r.
\]

### Recover the exact endpoint volume

Put
\[
f(t)=\log\det(I+tZ),
\qquad
M(t)=tf'(t).
\]
Then
\[
M'(t)=\kappa_{ij}(t),\qquad M(0)=0.
\]

Fubini gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^1\log(1/t)\kappa_{ij}(t)\,dt
&=\int_0^1\frac1s\int_0^s\kappa_{ij}(t)\,dt\,ds\\
&=\int_0^1f'(s)\,ds\\
&=\log\det(I+Z).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(G(1)=G_i\) and \(G(0)=G_j\),
\[
\boxed{
\log\frac{V_i}{V_j}
=
\int_0^1\log(1/t)\kappa_{ij}(t)\,dt.
}
\]

This is the same endpoint ratio as before, now computed on a compactified, marked curve with its boundary sheaf and metric.

### Its second fundamental map retains the arithmetic cancellation

The actual source projection is
\[
P_z=R(z)G(z)^{-1}R(z)^*O_j.
\]
Define
\[
\mathcal N_z=(I-P_z)\Delta.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal N_z^*O_j\mathcal N_z
=
C-|z|^2CG(z)^{-1}C,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
G(z)^{-1}\mathcal N_z^*O_j\mathcal N_z
\right]
=
\kappa_{ij}(|z|^2).
}
\]

The individual arithmetic observations are
\[
B_jP_z\Delta=\bar zG(z)^{-1}C,
\]
\[
B_j\mathcal N_z=-\bar zG(z)^{-1}C.
\]

Their sum is the original relation. **Neither projected part is declared a boundary separately.** Their cancellation is retained before its quotient value becomes \(e\).

## 6. The previous trace certificate is now a curvature-jet estimate

Differentiating the curvature density at the marked point gives
\[
\boxed{
\kappa_{ij}^{(n)}(0)
=
(-1)^n(n+1)!\operatorname{Tr}(Z^{n+1}).
}
\]

Therefore the last note’s quantities satisfy
\[
\boxed{
t_1=\kappa_{ij}(0),
\qquad
t_2=-\frac12\kappa_{ij}'(0).
}
\]

Its independent-pair quantity becomes
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal A_2
=
\frac12\left(
\kappa_{ij}(0)^2+\frac12\kappa_{ij}'(0)
\right).
}
\]

Thus the already-proved two-trace bound is now a bound on the logarithmic curvature moment of this particular determinant line:
\[
\boxed{
\int_{|z|<1}\log(1/|z|^2)c_1(\mathscr L_{ij})
\le
\log(1+a)+(q-1)\log(1+b).
}
\]
The \(a,b\) on the right are precisely the earlier functions of \(q,t_1,t_2\). No new estimate is being attributed to Deligne here; the geometric object underlying our existing estimate has been constructed.

## 7. The construction also follows the actual arithmetic constituents

Deligne’s determinant-weight bookkeeping concerns constituents, so I carried this construction through an actual invariant inclusion
\[
I_F:F\hookrightarrow E,
\qquad
AI_F=I_FA_F.
\]

Set
\[
R_F(z)=R(z)I_F,\qquad
G_F(z)=I_F^*G(z)I_F,\qquad
\Delta_F=\Delta I_F.
\]
The resulting constituent bundle maps into \(\mathscr E_{ij}\). On its modified part, the map is explicitly
\[
\boxed{
x\otimes(u,v)
\longmapsto
uP_0I_Fx+P_1I_Fx\otimes(u,v).

## 1. The next operation in Deligne’s argument

I reassembled and hash-checked the supplied S20 archive, then read the relevant LaTeX and current page-local French records. The additional passages are **§§3.7.2–3.7.4**, together with **Corollary 1.8.12**.

The important operation is this: Deligne puts exponential sheaves into a polynomial parameter family, controls that family **at infinity**, obtains a lisse cohomological family, and then uses connectedness and the weight machinery to pass from a calculated member to the family. Constant rank alone is not the purity argument. The supplied text’s Corollary 1.8.12 explicitly requires the lisse mixed structure when propagating purity from one point. The underlying paper is *La conjecture de Weil II*. citeturn139834view0

## 2. Complete the cohomology of the curve already constructed

Keep the preceding source family:
\[
\Delta=L_{ij}R_i-R_j,\qquad

Its original remainder map kills \(\Delta\), while every finite \(R(z)\) retains the same arithmetic jets and cohomology class. Those are the predecessor’s actual maps. fileciteturn329file0L30-L55

Let
